I absolutely loved this game! The characters, the art, the themes! I loved it!
But that's "Loved", not "love".
Before I get any hatred towards this, I am a guy who needs motivation to play a game for an extended amount of time, such as Call Of Duty (pls no hate) which gave me motivation to play multiplayer and level up, but as soon as I reached that higher level, I got bored and stopped playing (which is when I moved onto PC gaming). A multitude of my most played games consist of this motivational mechanics, like Payday 2, Terraria, BF3/BF4. And Team Fortress 2's approach to this motivational mechanic was the addition of hats and weapons, crates and keys, and item effects. This developed the community in a whole and kept the game alive way past other multiplayer shooters (8 years!). And the community in this game is beautiful; As they create immense amounts of artwork, models and maps. They also made the TF2 economy which was my motivation to play this game for over 1,000 hours. For two years, I was estatic to hop on my favorite "Trade_" map and get me some profit! I even got myself my first unusual which made me thirst for more! It made me lust for those very rare pixels! But as time goes by I see the inevitable problem that all economies face. Inflation. As more and more people play the game, the more weapons drop, and as more weapons drop, more metal get created and pushed into the system and as metal was the main economic currency for trading unique hats things started to change. Keys were worth more and more refined metal everyday (from 2.33 to 15.77!!!) which didn't really affect me that much as I had moved onto unusual trading. However, the same problem goes for buds, the main currency for unusual hats. Inflation strikes again. For people who don't know, duping is the act of getting your items replaced by steam support after they've been stolen from a hacker, now, I think you can see where this goes but if the account dupes their items, that means there's a whole inventory that's been put in circulation twice which has a very negative effect on the rarity and price of the items. This leads onto a lot of buds being duped that the price has gone from 20 keys to 4 keys. This deeply affects the prices of my inventory and I fear for the overall worth of my inventory so as a last resort I trade in my unusuals for a CS:GO knife. And as the economy countinued to downfall I lose my motivation and my interest in the game. I miss the ecstacy of getting a sweet new hat. It breaks my heart, but I have to part ways with this beauty of a shooter.
TL:DR - I'm a materialistic prick that uses hats as motivation and I lose interest as my materialistic properties become worthless.

TF2 is a rather cute cartoony graphic type of game, yet is fun for most ages, the charactars are diverse and have their  strengths and weaknesses, which adds to the curiosity which hooks in host new players along with the meet the series vidioes on youtube (i.e. meet the spy).
Like the charactars, the game has its strengths and weaknesses, such as the sourse engine, which the game runs on, and just to say, gmod and half-life 2 also run on sourse, so its a really old engine that can only take so much pressure with graphics and connectivity issues, just to be kind though, the game is from 2007, when the gaming industry was still at the stone age with graphics, so basically give the game credit on that. Another weakness on this game is that its really confusing for a new person, and dont think that youtube or a wiki will help you, there are so many weapons and classes and maps and gamemodes, not to mention that its hard being a noob on servers.
Without hurting the game reputition now, lets look at some strengths. There is always someone to play. While the game came out in 2007, the servers are still strong and the game gets constant updates keeping the game running. TF2 is really cheeky and colorful. TF2 stands out from almost all fps titles with "stunning fps graphics" and "crystal clear gameplay", well guess what? It doesn't matter that much, as long as the bright graphics stay the way they are and the charactar diolgue lines stay the same, the atomsphere will be the magnet that keeps people in.

The game is a shooter unlike any other, that focuses on teamwork and mastering one or more of 9 distinct classes available for play. While not too challenging for new players, there is a very high skill ceiling so there is a huge degree of variability in player skill levels, and a new player will definitely benefit from playing with a more experienced one who can teach and explain as they go, as well as what default settings to change. There is still developer support to this day, with a very large content update going up just two weeks before I posted this review, and the Community behind the game is incredible and is the reason the game has survived as long as it has, with Steam Workshop creations and custom maps and Source Filmmaker submissions being made every day there is always something new to do or a new way to play. These things aside, the game is not for everyone, with someone who wants a more hardcore or realistic shooter might not appreciate the game for what it is, and if you don't like shooters then you probably won't like this one either. Either way, I encourage anyone who is interested in the game to check it out because I enjoy it, and it operates on one of the best "Free To Play" models ever conceived, so try it out it's free what have you got to lose?!

Welp. Time to redo this review again.
In my previous review of this game, I had told people to stay away due to the lack of content, glitchy gameplay, and Valve's incompetentness. While the last bit may be true, depending who you're talking to and about what, it is evident that the Jungle Inferno has brought some massive changes to make the game fun once more. Do I think it should of taken 15 months? No, but hey. It wasn't another Meet Your Match at least. Guess I should talk about content.
Pyro's new weapons (And the Heavy with his lonely banana)- I would say these are all interesting additions to the Pyro's fairly limited arsenal before the update, with all of them bringing something a little new to the mumbling maniac. Some people are complaining the Dragon's Fruy is OP, which I can't tell if I agree or not. Either way, it's very strong indeed. Gas Passer is pretty neato, but I think it would be much better if your spawned with a fresh one instead of having to wait: Though, damaging players does speed it considerably. The Jetpack (Whatever it's called, ain't got the time) is in a fine spot of balance, while meanwhile I actually like the Banana for Heavy a good deal. It's the mid way between the Dalokas and the Sand♥♥♥♥♥.
Maps- I liked 'em. Good variety, VERY pretty, and not to hard to process. Not much to say, I just like them a lot (Except Mercenary Park's spawn glitches, but those'll be fixed sometime.
Taunts- Another small thing, but I felt it needed. The Heavy taunts added some more to him which was nice, I bought the Dueling Banjo for Engi as soon as I could, and the Pyro's attempt of being Gordon Ramsey was humorous.
Final verdict- Those it was in a very thin piece of ice, TF2 made it's way off and is now once again a game I can enjoy with my friends. I personally thank the community for making this possible, and I wish everyone a great day.
-The Canadian Jew

Team Fortress 2 - The World's First War Themed Hat Simulator
This game is incredible, and I haven't even played for over 100 hrs (which is saying something in the community)! Team Fortress 2 combines FPS fun with humour and.... Hat collection? After 3 years speculating whether or not to get Steam, I decided to roll with the punches and get it. My prime target was the game EVERYBODY seemed to own besides me - TF2. Well, I wasn't expecting what I got. The community online were welcoming, and it seems I was just on time to catch the whole 'Gun Mettle = CS: GO" fiasco!
Anyway, the game itself is brilliant, the community (usually) make it even better, and the fact that Australia is shown as more powerful than China sealed the deal for me! Overall, you CAN'T live without playing this for at least an hour, and whilst progress seems slow at first, you'll soon come to terms with 'Buds', 'Ref' and 'Keys'. No, the latter is NOT used to open locked things (well, it is, but... You'll find out) but to trade with! Duh!
Trading is another great mechanic on Steam overall, but in TF2, the system is clean and is, at the very least, not full of scammers like CS: GO is. There are the odd few, but  you'll learn to cope and will soon be toting Aussie Weapons, wearing Burning Flames Team Captains (well, keep dreaming) and will be gambling in Raffles like you have unlimited amounts of money! There are SOME cons to TF2, but they aren't severe:
- You can't trade all items without premium (buying something with real money)

Aren't you glad Team Fortress 2 didn't wind up looking like this? Valve has created quite a game with the long-awaited Team Fortress sequel, bearing many similarities to its predecessor, though incorporating enough changes to make it feel fresh. The most obvious aspect, which you may have noticed from any of the screens and video posted, is the visual style. Even after getting sucked into probably too many hours of play in the beta over the past few weeks, we're still amazed at the art design, both in how it looks and how it animates.
But let's not get too carried away with the graphics. It's a game, after all, and the most important factor is how it plays and if it's entertaining. It's interesting to see both Team Fortress 2, which has been in development on and off for some seven years now, and Splash Damage's Enemy Territory: Quake Wars, which has seen its own share of setbacks and delays, finally come out right around the same time. Their nearly simultaneous retail release presents and interesting situation for you, the consumer, as to how to spend your cash. You may fondly remember your days in Return to Castle Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory, dropping air strikes on hapless attackers and eagerly charging into bunkers to spout forth deadly plumes of flamethrower fuel. Yet you can't forget your days with Team Fortress Classic, or even further back with the original Team Fortress Quake mod, with its now painfully dated character models but compelling team-focused online play.
There's really no right answer in this case as to which game is ultimately better. It's merely personal preference. Quake Wars is assuredly the more complicated game. For those uninitiated in the ways of Enemy Territory, the scope, dynamic objectives, speed at which the tide of battle can turn and the number of things you need to quickly consider when that happens, and user interface can be rather daunting. After learning the ins and outs it's clearly an excellent product, but it lacks that immediate, irresistible appeal so prominent in Valve's Team Fortress 2. And accessibility may very well be the deciding factor in determining which product users prefer. Regardless, it's an excellent time to be a gamer, since as tough as it may be to pick one or the other, making either choice rewards you with a well designed and highly entertaining title.
Like in Team Fortress Classic (TFC), Team Fortress 2 has nine character classes: Spy, Pyro, Soldier, Heavy, Medic, Sniper, Demoman, Scout and Engineer. Each class' abilities on the battlefield have been streamlined, which, along with the graphics, is what makes Team Fortress 2 so much more accessible than TFC. No longer do you have Engineers running around with railguns and EMP grenades. Medics can't "infect" the other team, Spies don't have tranquilizer darts, and none of the classes have hand grenades.
In TF2, each class has roughly three main ways of attacking - a primary weapon (the Heavy's minigun, Pyro's flamethrower, Engineer's sentry gun, etc.) and secondary (various classes have shotguns, others pistols, while the Demoman has a highly effective mine thrower) and melee weapons (the Scout's bat, the Medic's bonesaw, and so on). Though classes now possess fewer means of attacking, the resulting gameplay feels much more focused. Each class has a very clearly defined role and the means to ensure they perform successfully. The only limiting factor is, of course, how effectively your team meshes together.
If your Engineers aren't guarding their structures, Spies can wipe them out in seconds with a few sapper charges. If your team is full of Heavies and Soldiers but lacks Medics, you're not going to get very far. If you're playing a capture point map without any Scouts on your team, you might as well just leave the server or start berating your squadmates until a few switch classes. The Medic, though, seems to be the hinge on which all gameplay balance swivels. For TF2 they've been given a health hose, which blasts out a restorative stream at friendlies within range and "sticks" to them as long as you keep the fire button depressed. As you heal injured teammates, or "overheal" to 150 percent health, an ubercharge meter builds in the bottom right of the screen. Unleashing this renders both target and Medic invulnerable for a few seconds, which is sometimes the only way to break through chokepoints populated with Heavies, Medics, and multiple tier three sentry guns.
Even though Medics may be the most vital to a team's success, the other classes remain useful. Scouts, who are now rather deadly, are far and away the fastest, and their ability to double-jump and change direction in mid-air makes then all the more difficult to hit. Spies, in addition to being able to one-hit kill backstab the enemy, cause general chaos among enemy ranks. If your opponents know a spy is running around, they'll waste time and lose focus by shooting at their own teammates to try and reveal a disguised culprit.
Pyros tend to be the most effective spy detectors, and can be frequently seen doing fiery pirouettes in 2Fort matches all over the beta servers, as a spy incognito will betray his cover by bursting into flames upon contact with the burning spray.In a September 26 Steam update, friendly fire was removed from TF2, which was definitely a good move. Friendly fire ruins much of the game considering the close-quarters maps combined with the wide area of effect attacks of Heavies, Pyros, Demomen, and Soldiers. Without FF, teammates are free to shoot each other, since if they bleed health, they're a spy.

I have quite a bit of time put in this game by now and am comfortable posting a review on it, not that it will matter as there are thousands of reviews and testimonials all over the internet by now, but I will still try to be objective and fair.  The game is a shooter unlike any other, that focuses on teamwork and mastering one or more of 9 distinct classes available for play. Within each class there are a variety of weapons to select and equip in a series of custom loadouts. While not too challenging for new players, there is a very high skill ceiling so there is a huge degree of variability in player skill levels, and a new player will definitely benefit from playing with a more experienced one who can teach and explain as they go, as well as what default settings to change. There is still developer support to this day, with a very large content update going up just two weeks before I posted this review, and the Community behind the game is incredible and is the reason the game has survived as long as it has, with Steam Workshop creations and custom maps and Source Filmmaker submissions being made every day there is always something new to do or a new way to play. These things aside, the game is not for everyone, with someone who wants a more hardcore or realistic shooter might not appreciate the game for what it is, and if you don't like shooters then you probably won't like this one either. Either way, I encourage anyone who is interested in the game to check it out because I enjoy it, and it operates on one of the best "Free To Play" models ever conceived, so try it out it's free what have you got to lose?!

Welp. Time to redo this review again.
In my previous review of this game, I had told people to stay away due to the lack of content, glitchy gameplay, and Valve's incompetentness. While the last bit may be true, depending who you're talking to and about what, it is evident that the Jungle Inferno has brought some massive changes to make the game fun once more. Do I think it should of taken 15 months? No, but hey. It wasn't another Meet Your Match at least. Guess I should talk about content.
Pyro's new weapons (And the Heavy with his lonely banana)- I would say these are all interesting additions to the Pyro's fairly limited arsenal before the update, with all of them bringing something a little new to the mumbling maniac. Some people are complaining the Dragon's Fruy is OP, which I can't tell if I agree or not. Either way, it's very strong indeed. Gas Passer is pretty neato, but I think it would be much better if your spawned with a fresh one instead of having to wait: Though, damaging players does speed it considerably. The Jetpack (Whatever it's called, ain't got the time) is in a fine spot of balance, while meanwhile I actually like the Banana for Heavy a good deal. It's the mid way between the Dalokas and the Sand♥♥♥♥♥.
Maps- I liked 'em. Good variety, VERY pretty, and not to hard to process. Not much to say, I just like them a lot (Except Mercenary Park's spawn glitches, but those'll be fixed sometime.
Taunts- Another small thing, but I felt it needed. The Heavy taunts added some more to him which was nice, I bought the Dueling Banjo for Engi as soon as I could, and the Pyro's attempt of being Gordon Ramsey was humorous.
Final verdict- Those it was in a very thin piece of ice, TF2 made it's way off and is now once again a game I can enjoy with my friends. I personally thank the community for making this possible, and I wish everyone a great day.
-The Canadian Jew

I have to be honest with you, it took me awhile to get into the game. A long while. It really is fun with a pretty hilarious community if you play long enough. Now, as a p2p, still pretty new, with a backpack worth of only about $20, I am here to give a little starter guide for this game.
1) Dont wear the gibus, or pyrovision goggles, these are the essence of noobs, just, if you dont have good cosmetics, dont wear any.
2) While many weapons may be considered bad, or lame, or a noob weapon. Use the weapon you enjoy and feel the most comfortable with.
3) One of the harder classes to play is sniper, it can be a great class, but requires practice. It also homes aiming skills which is valuable in-game.
4) Dont ask for free-bees. Noone likes an f2p user who just wants to stay an f2p, but have good items.
5) When you want to step up and be a p2p, try to go for a cheap cosmetic or weapon on sale, then (if a weapon) you can test run it, see if you enjoy it, then buy it for an even more discounted price. Congrats, you now have a Mann Co hat and a whole lot more backpack space. The Mann Co hat isnt the most respected hat, but better than the gibus or no hat, keep that in mind.
6) Now that you are a p2p, you have access to a large array of market items and trade websites. While you may have thought a scrap is worth alot, 1 ref (9 scrap) is worth literally nothing in terms of taunts and cosmetics. Save up, get good stuff.
7) DONT USE MANN CO STORE ANYMORE!!! This is important, the items are overpriced, try getting the item off of a website like tf2outpost or trade.tf. If you put your money in steam wallet already, use the community market.
I feel that it is my debt to review such a great game, if you have any additional questions about tf2 you can ask me on twitter: @BrandonIsNerd

Team Fortress 2 is by far one of the most fun games I have ever played. One of the main factors, if not THE main factor for this is the diversity. I used to play some MMORPG's for example and one thing that annoyed me the most was, that after a while there's nothing interesting, nothing different than either quests and leveling. Of Course you cannot compare such games with a shooter. But this games has more diversity than just beeing a shooter.
First of all, what initionally made me pick up this game in the first place was it's graphic style. It's just crazy. I mean in which other game you can SPAM a rocket launcher rather than shooting once and then reload 10 minutes. And it's just called Rocket Launcher, not RPG 8621. Or just having the possibility blowing everything up with the demoman. This leads me to my next very important factor, the class diversity
It's even stated by Valve in their developer commentaries, that they wanted to make each and single class completely different from each other. And creating even 9 of them. Each one has a completely independent playstyle from the other classes. You can't compare a crazy and flink guy like the scout with the silent, sneaky frenchman spy. There is literally everything a casual gamer could play. From going Ham Pyros, down to defending Engineer. Every role has it's place, even though some weaknesses of the classes are more punishing than others. With that beeing said, I'm moving onto my next factor, the Teamplay
This one is something that exists in the game itself, though rather disguised in public games. Even though the game has the possiblity of using voice chat, most players don't use it at all. I actually don't know the exact reason, except because the others don't do it either, but surely it would add to the teamwork part of the game. This follows my transition to the next topic, the Competitive "area". This one is little bit hidden. Many people participate in Pick-Up-Games where you get some random people to play with and against. The point of these games are getting structure and predictability into the Chaos and craziness of TF2. You play either 6 versus 6 OR 9 versus 9 games, in which you either can pick beetween one of two Scouts, one of two Soldiers, one Demoman and one Medic, OR 1 guy for each class (also called Highlander). In these games, the factor teamwork starts getting very important and impactful. Communication is mostly supported by the voicechat programm Mumble so you don't have to push this damn key everytime you want to say something. Mechanical skill is always useful, handy and important in solo situations, but you will loose even with good mechanics, if they enemy team is working together better than your own.
At the end I can say that Team Fortress 2 is one of the best (actually F2P) games I have ever played. It's is fun for newcomers, it has a skillcap, so you can practice if you want, you can use voicechat to work with your team or just playing 15 min because you have nothing better to do. If you want to dive deeper into this game, you can go play competitive, improve your skills, your teamwork abilities, and combine this for an awesome amount of fun and joy.

Rating: 9.5/10
Recommendations: anyone looking to get into PC gaming
Review: This game as you can probably tell from my hours in it, is my favorite game to play online. but the reason why I like it is actually that this game is the reason I switched from console to PC. but the reason I waited to write a review for this game is because I was stuck in the middle trying to think "is this game actually good or not?" So for almost a year i neglected this game trying to decide if it was worth my time to keep playing or to just move on to counter-strike or just stop playing games in general. So you can imagine how good this game is but yet if you get in the middle of a decision that prolongs you to the point where it almost shuts down your will for PC gaming. but after 9 months of thinking, in the mid-summer of 2014 my old friends who I dont really talk to anymore convinced my to actually play the game again on different servers instead of just playing on a trade server or actually play competitive. I joined them on a "Jailbreak" server called "PlayBoy" and it was great in my opinion. I continued to play for about 6 months and then I finally decided that this game was great for those who are either casual or competitive. which was the missing link in my decision, because if you play on Official valve servers or any other server that requires actual skill to get the kills and help the team win i consider you a Competitive player and I think most people would agree with me. but I think what I was actually missing in my continuous experience which continues to this day was actually experiencing the casual play. such as going on a trade server and looking for trades while trying to kill people and not care if you got killed because you have the trades on your mind instead of actually killing or being killed. and with the recent update, "Gun Mettle" alot of people have miss-interperted it because people have been thinking "Oh wait this game isn't TF2 anymore it's TF:GO!" or "Good-bye TF2, Hello TF:GO!" and at first when I saw the skins being added I actually
with them which was probably a mistake i couldnt forgive myself for because when I saw everything nerfed/upgraded I realized that everyone is wrong about the Gun Mettle update. because there was still more then just skins in TF2 which seperates TF2 and CS:GO from each other which makes TF2 the game it first started out as and still survives as to this very day because you have choices in TF2 unlike CS:GO! so no matter what change valve can make to this game TF2 will always be defined as TF2 in my opinion and will remain as a great game that only got better along the way.
TL;DR Version: Great game since 2007, i commend you Lord Gaben you deserve them Snickers bars. ;)

Well, after around 1,000 hours of playing Team Fortress 2, I decided it would finally be a good idea to write a review for new players coming into the game.
Overview:
Team Fortress 2 is a fun-filled multiplayer based FPS (First Person Shooter) that has two teams, RED vs. BLU, fighting to do certain objectives to win the round/map. Even if Team Fortress 2 appears to be empty and just a mindless shooter, the nine characters featured (Classes) are bursting with personality and TF2 has a backstory in the form of comics.
Gameplay (9.5/10)
Team Fortress 2's actual gameplay is very intense based around teamwork (Sorry, Cod players.) Each class offers an entirely new role on the battlefield, so you can shift your style of gameplay to next if your starting to get bored, along with the addition of weapons, there are endless combinations to your loadout that can spice up gameplay just a little bit more than usual. Lastly, there are always people playing. I only give this a 9.5 as after a long time of playing, you begin to loose the feeling of "something new" between each class. Putting a shroud of boredom on the game at times.
Community (7/10)
Team Fortress 2's community is either absolutely disgusting or amazingly friendly, some players seem like they are straight out of CS:GO (Counter strike: Global Offensive, which has a very horrid community) while others will support other players and play the game like it was meant to be played. Many good TF2 community members create custom content for the game, ranging from skins, maps, and configs.
Characters/Charm (10/10)
Probably one of the greatest reasons why people play TF2 as extensively as they do today, the nine characters are just filled with personality and charm (comical, for the most part.) The bonus of this is that you feel what the characters are thinking based on what you are doing. With the help of the community with Source Filmmaker and Gmod videos, these classes were really brought to life and you develop a like/hate relationship with them, you may despise playing Spy because of how much of a coward and backstabbing devil he is. But you love the adrenaline rush of inflitrating the enemy's lines.
Pricing (10/10)
TF2 is almost completely Free to Play, no gimmicks included. You download the game, you get the entire taco. The only thing you cannot do is trade or get cosemetics for your character. But why would that matter? You get the weapons, you get the classes, you get the maps. So you still get to play the game, and if you've been playing for long enough and want to upgrade to premium, one purchase on the Mann. Co store (Which could be about fifty cents) will give you all the perks of having of being upgraded without any "Monthly transactions."
Economy (What? (8/10) )
So you must be thinking, TF2 has an Economy? In fact. It does, TF2 has an entire system and economy based around metal and hats. That sounds insane, doesn't it? But it's true. There are servers on TF2 dedicated to trading metal for hats and other things such as weapons. The system is not entirely flawless, as people get scammed daily due to not knowing the "price" of a certain item, and there are the "big sharks" that have everything and only trade for the bigger things.
Overall
I give TF2 a well-rounded 9/10, it is nothing short of satisfying or extremely fun, and there is no reason not to try it, it is free! Give it a shot, you won't regret it.

The massively popular game, Team Fortess 2, is quite a highlight in both the shooter genre and all multiplayer games to date. It boasts nine classes, dozens of modes, tons of user created content and an overall breath of fresh air to the FPS genre.
Like I said earlier, there are nine classes, all with their strengths, weaknesses, and over-arching personalities.
Scout: Runs the fastest out of all the classes and can double jump. Also completes objectives quicker and is powerful at close range, but otherwise sports low health and poor longe range options.
Pyro: Has a powerful close range game with it's flamethrower which can inflict afterburn: a status that lingers for ten seconds, constantly dealing damage. Can be a tricky enemy by reflecting certain projectiles. Also is fairly durable with above average health.
Soldier: Boast one of the most powerful damage outputs in the game with his rocket launcher. He can also gain impressive mobility by rocket jumping. (Though great skill is required) Has a bulky amount of health, but fairly slow.
Demoman: Posesses the ability to blow up everything in sight with a grenade launcher and also meticulously set up defensive barriers with sticky bombs. Fairly durable with above average health. Also quite slow on the ground.
Engineer: Focuses on area denial with his hulking sentry guns. Can also support teamate with a health and ammo deploying dispenser and can transport them in to battle much easier with a teleporter. Strip away the devices, and engie is the weakest class with poor firepower and low health.
Hoovy: Has the most extreme damage output in the game with his minigun. Also has the most health in the game and can deploy tasty lunches at any time. He is so slow however, so he is seceptable to backstabs and headshots.
Medic: Poses as the backbone of the team, by utilizing his medi gun to heal friendly classes. And when he reaches 100% full Uber, he can turn himself and his subject invulnerable for a short time. Otherwise, he has mediocre power and health.
Sniper: Can one-shot kill any class in the game with a fully charged headshot. But he struggles in close range and doesn't have the health to back it up. Also has jars of pee for some reason.
Spy: Can become invisible, disguise as a player on the opposing team, and render sentries disabled. The beurocrat also posesses the backstab: a technique that one-shots any class. However, the Spy has low health and poor guns, so be sneaky with him.
All the classes listed above provide a fresh gaming experience and are just fun to play as. With all the updates prior, every class, weapon, etc has been fine tuned to create the most balanced team possible. So if you play the game and keep getting destroyed by the opposing team, it's only you and your team to blame.
Also, a few years ago, the game mode Mann vs Machine was released. It's a horde based co-op experience and alot of fun as a distraction to the main game. It is quite brutal in difficulty though, so be warned.
And as of July 3, the Gun Mettle update was released. It is a generally great update with new maps, skins and taunts. It also added a new dropped weapons feature, but it's purely optional.
Honestly, even if TF2 was a bad game I'd still recommend a go, and that is because it's free. But I do recommend investing a little money into it, because frankly, your not getting the full experience. So, what are you waiting for? Go! Download TF2 and buy the prettiest hats you see! And then use them to stylishly destroy your foes in the chaotic frenzy that is Team Fortess 2.

So I just got tf2 about a week ago and first of all id like to say Im not too impressed. The first time I tried out this game I kept getting spawntrapped and dying, the second time I downloaded it my game kept freezing. Now on the third time trying to play it I can finally see it for what it is. First of all the game is called "TEAM fortress 2" and teamwork in this game is essential to victory. However most of the time your teammates just go off and do their own thing or do the noobiest things in the game. If you DO manage to get a good teamwork going the teams will most likely get scrambeled and you will have to start all over. And then you get matches where your team doesnt even help, infact they antagonize you saying stuff like "Your just a noob go back to cod" and if you ask them like say what the dispenser does they'll just say "It dispenses stuff" just to annoy you (so the community is not friendly to new players).
Now the main problem I have in this game is skill level: You do not need to be skillfull to rack up kills in this game. Just be an engineer and get a level 3 turret and a level 3 dispenser and constantly camp next to it and repair it and you will rack up kills. Aside from that the game can be thought of as pay to win, or more precisely pay to be OP. All you need is an expensive rocket launcher and be able to rocket spam to rack up kills which by the way for those who have not played, rocket spamming is one of the many cheap playstyles in this game. Another cheap playstyle is scouts who run the fastest and can double jump will just run around you in circles and keep jumping (Because when you jump you gain speed) and will keep shooting at you. If you dont have high enough sensitivity it is impossible for you to kill them. Sometimes scouts can even triple jump so they can jump right over your head repeatedly. If there are friendly teamates behind you they may be able to shoot at the scout but then he will panic and run off like a little b!tch because thats what players do in this game.
Luck is more a factor on whether you get kills or not with some classes like for example the spy: Hes stealthy, he can cloak, disguise and his main weapon is a blade - which by the way if his main weapon is a blade it shouldn't be weak af when attacking from the front. The spy needs to get atleast 4 maybe even 5 or 6 swipes with his blade to kill an enemy while attacking from the front, and thats his MAIN weapon and yet other classes are running around with blades one shotting people even heavies, hitting them in the front! Spies are EXTREMELY underpowered in this game. You will either constantly be checked for by pyros who will spam flames looking for you, even when they dont even know there is a spy near them. Or they will walk into you just slightly, subtly accidentally and then fire in a frenzy trying to find where you are. If you do manage to sneak up behind an enemy you better backstab him fast before he magically turns around the second you uncloak and even if he doesnt turn around he will most likely be moving which makes it harder for you to catch up and sometimes the backstab doesnt even register and it counts as a frontal stab. If you manage to get the kill AND manage to get away without another one of his teammates noticing, you are very lucky. Also the idea of disguising is cool but its broken. Considering as soon as you kill an enemy while disguised you turn back to the normal you again makes it a nearly always useless mechanic. I think it was made for taking out enemy turrets and such which, as I mentioned earlier would be impossible because nearly all engineers camp by their turrets so theres only 3 outcomes. You start sapping a sentry, the engineer sees you and kills you and instantly repairs the turret, you kill the engineer but then the turrets will kill you OR you get lucky enough that the engineer isn't close by and you manage to use the sapper on the turret. And that's only if they have one sentry, if they have more than one like 2 or 3 max level with dispensers max level and are camping next to their sentries....the objective of the ENTIRE TEAM becomes to destroy the sentries all because the enemy team had an unfair advantage - time, which you will spend the whole match taking up trying to destroy the sentries because the disguise mechanic is broken and therefore useless. And you might say "Oh but it's all about the role you have to play and thats why its not that good." Man I downloaded this game to have FUN and if my fun is limited by the "role" of a class then it is not a good game because the game is limiting the potential of the players based on the mechanics of the game and denying the freedom of their unique playstyles.
Speaking of roles - sometimes the roles do not even work. The heavy is supposed to be a tank, and yet I can get one or two shotted and thats not by spies or snipers its by soldiers and scouts (And that links back to being OP by paying money for weapons). And you might say "Oh well you need a medic behind you!" that is EXACTLY where the problem lies with this game. The outcomes of situations are based not on the skill of a single player but on the community and the teamwork of players which as Ive said before, rarely ever comes together.
You see Valve made the game with the intention of a bunch of classes with different roles that could all work in unison as a team and win the match. And then it all falls apart and you know why? Cause it's a GAME and were playing it to have FUN - some people are gonna want to run around the map and cloak all match, others want to be a tank and just destroy everything in sight. All people have different ideas of fun and that's where the problem lies because it is "Co-operate and play the way we wanted you to or die" and is a fatal and crucial mistake on valves part and ruins this game. And if I have to rely on OTHERS to to get kills in this game then Im never going to play it. Turrets are OP in groups, melee weapons can out kill any other type of gun (Other than if they are a spy), and cheap playstyles and bad mechanics  RUIN the fun.
Bottom line - The hit detection in this game as spies (And also other classes too, its just worse on spies) is absolutely terrible and the damage spies deal goes against common sense. The abilities are OP, especially with medics and cheap playstyles ruin the fun. The community is bad, votekicking people off for no reason, and also trapping them in places.
EDIT: After getting the "Cloak and dagger" spy watch and trying it out....spies are actually playable! You can now get kills as a spy!

Well, after around 1,000 hours of playing Team Fortress 2, I decided it would finally be a good idea to write a review for new players coming into the game.
Overview:
Team Fortress 2 is a fun-filled multiplayer based FPS (First Person Shooter) that has two teams, RED vs. BLU, fighting to do certain objectives to win the round/map. Even if Team Fortress 2 appears to be empty and just a mindless shooter, the nine characters featured (Classes) are bursting with personality and TF2 has a backstory in the form of comics.
Gameplay (9.5/10)
Team Fortress 2's actual gameplay is very intense based around teamwork (Sorry, Cod players.) Each class offers an entirely new role on the battlefield, so you can shift your style of gameplay to next if your starting to get bored, along with the addition of weapons, there are endless combinations to your loadout that can spice up gameplay just a little bit more than usual. Lastly, there are always people playing. I only give this a 9.5 as after a long time of playing, you begin to loose the feeling of "something new" between each class. Putting a shroud of boredom on the game at times.
Community (7/10)
Team Fortress 2's community is either absolutely disgusting or amazingly friendly, some players seem like they are straight out of CS:GO (Counter strike: Global Offensive, which has a very horrid community) while others will support other players and play the game like it was meant to be played. Many good TF2 community members create custom content for the game, ranging from skins, maps, and configs.
Characters/Charm (10/10)
Probably one of the greatest reasons why people play TF2 as extensively as they do today, the nine characters are just filled with personality and charm (comical, for the most part.) The bonus of this is that you feel what the characters are thinking based on what you are doing. With the help of the community with Source Filmmaker and Gmod videos, these classes were really brought to life and you develop a like/hate relationship with them, you may despise playing Spy because of how much of a coward and backstabbing devil he is. But you love the adrenaline rush of inflitrating the enemy's lines.
Pricing (10/10)
TF2 is almost completely Free to Play, no gimmicks included. You download the game, you get the entire taco. The only thing you cannot do is trade or get cosemetics for your character. But why would that matter? You get the weapons, you get the classes, you get the maps. So you still get to play the game, and if you've been playing for long enough and want to upgrade to premium, one purchase on the Mann. Co store (Which could be about fifty cents) will give you all the perks of having of being upgraded without any "Monthly transactions."
Economy (What? (8/10) )
So you must be thinking, TF2 has an Economy? In fact. It does, TF2 has an entire system and economy based around metal and hats. That sounds insane, doesn't it? But it's true. There are servers on TF2 dedicated to trading metal for hats and other things such as weapons. The system is not entirely flawless, as people get scammed daily due to not knowing the "price" of a certain item, and there are the "big sharks" that have everything and only trade for the bigger things.
Overall
I give TF2 a well-rounded 9/10, it is nothing short of satisfying or extremely fun, and there is no reason not to try it, it is free! Give it a shot, you won't regret it.

The massively popular game, Team Fortess 2, is quite a highlight in both the shooter genre and all multiplayer games to date. It boasts nine classes, dozens of modes, tons of user created content and an overall breath of fresh air to the FPS genre.
Like I said earlier, there are nine classes, all with their strengths, weaknesses, and over-arching personalities.
Scout: Runs the fastest out of all the classes and can double jump. Also completes objectives quicker and is powerful at close range, but otherwise sports low health and poor longe range options.
Pyro: Has a powerful close range game with it's flamethrower which can inflict afterburn: a status that lingers for ten seconds, constantly dealing damage. Can be a tricky enemy by reflecting certain projectiles. Also is fairly durable with above average health.
Soldier: Boast one of the most powerful damage outputs in the game with his rocket launcher. He can also gain impressive mobility by rocket jumping. (Though great skill is required) Has a bulky amount of health, but fairly slow.
Demoman: Posesses the ability to blow up everything in sight with a grenade launcher and also meticulously set up defensive barriers with sticky bombs. Fairly durable with above average health. Also quite slow on the ground.
Engineer: Focuses on area denial with his hulking sentry guns. Can also support teamate with a health and ammo deploying dispenser and can transport them in to battle much easier with a teleporter. Strip away the devices, and engie is the weakest class with poor firepower and low health.
Hoovy: Has the most extreme damage output in the game with his minigun. Also has the most health in the game and can deploy tasty lunches at any time. He is so slow however, so he is seceptable to backstabs and headshots.
Medic: Poses as the backbone of the team, by utilizing his medi gun to heal friendly classes. And when he reaches 100% full Uber, he can turn himself and his subject invulnerable for a short time. Otherwise, he has mediocre power and health.
Sniper: Can one-shot kill any class in the game with a fully charged headshot. But he struggles in close range and doesn't have the health to back it up. Also has jars of pee for some reason.
Spy: Can become invisible, disguise as a player on the opposing team, and render sentries disabled. The beurocrat also posesses the backstab: a technique that one-shots any class. However, the Spy has low health and poor guns, so be sneaky with him.
All the classes listed above provide a fresh gaming experience and are just fun to play as. With all the updates prior, every class, weapon, etc has been fine tuned to create the most balanced team possible. So if you play the game and keep getting destroyed by the opposing team, it's only you and your team to blame.
Also, a few years ago, the game mode Mann vs Machine was released. It's a horde based co-op experience and alot of fun as a distraction to the main game. It is quite brutal in difficulty though, so be warned.
And as of July 3, the Gun Mettle update was released. It is a generally great update with new maps, skins and taunts. It also added a new dropped weapons feature, but it's purely optional.
Honestly, even if TF2 was a bad game I'd still recommend a go, and that is because it's free. But I do recommend investing a little money into it, because frankly, your not getting the full experience. So, what are you waiting for? Go! Download TF2 and buy the prettiest hats you see! And then use them to stylishly destroy your foes in the chaotic frenzy that is Team Fortess 2.

Team Fottress 2 is a fast paced, first-person-shooter. The game contains 9 classes, each with their own personalities and pacing of gameplay, with many well-designed maps that fit with every character's playstyle (to different extents), and many guns and gags to mess around with. Each class fall into the rule of: "Easy to learn, hard to master", every class has their set of weapons and skills that are simple to understand, but can be enhanced greatly by player skill\experience to give the player a greater impact in the battlefield. The maps are generally well-designed for all the classes to move and fight in. Very few maps feel restrictive; however, when they are restrictive it's feels very uncomfortable to move around in, so becareful. The guns in Team Fortress 2 feels great to fire, from their fantastic sound design and overall damage output, the gunplay in generally feels fluide and fast, the game will need the players time and skill for enjoyment. While still on the topic of guns, the balancing and stats of some guns\weapons are either: Great, to direct down grades. Balancing in Team Fortress 2 is overall inconsitent, some guns are in need of major reworks or fixes, speaking of fixing, the games hit registration is a bit: off. Not too off to where it's broken, but just enough to be an annoyance. Oh! almost forgot the modes, the game has three different gamemodes: Casual, Competitive, and Mann vs. Machine. Casual is 12 v 12, in which and bunch or randoms are put together and must work together to get the job done. Competitive is more serious (obviously) it's 6 v 6, in which players of similar ranks must work together to win the match, but in a more controlled and stable gameplay enviorment compared to Casual. Mann vs. Machine is co-op gamemode in which your team must defend yourselves from ai controlled robots. There's also community servers if you're feeling a bit crazy. In summary TF2 is a fun FPS that has some hiccups, but overall if you have the time and patience to learn and play the game, you're gonna have a fun time!
This game is fun to play, but it takes up A LOT of space (depends on how much space your disk already has).

Important Notes: 1. This is NOT a rant about MYM. Did MYM cause me to change this review? Yes, but it has more to do with community interaction in the past year than the update itself. I'm not happy with all of the changes in MYM, but the update wasn't completely horrible. It had some good things in it as well.
2. I made a very positive review of this game a LONG time ago, which is posted at the bottom of this review. It contains a good amount of information that is still (mostly) relevant, so be sure to check it out. It should be helpful for those who are looking into playing this game.
Don't get me wrong. I still love this game. I'm still going to play this game. However, there are SO many issues with it at the moment that have been consistantly ignored.
For the past year, the updates for this game have been... lacking, to say the least. Now, thats not to say they were horrible: although they created some problems, they also added new features that helped move the game forwards.
However, the community brought up concerns for balance changes and features that were causing issues and needed reworking. These concerns seem to have been completely ignored, with some concerns, such as asking for a buff to a weapon, having the opposite change being put in place, such as Valve nerfing the weapon that needed a buff.
Now, I respect Valve a lot. They've made great games and kept them alive for a long time. However, if this game is going to survive, they NEED to communicate with the players more. Right now, they seem to be ignoring the playerbase entirely.
Another issue is how Casual mode was implemented. There isn't anything wrong with Casual, and its actually good that Valve decided to add a new mode to encourage players to play differently. However, it could have been added ALONGSIDE quickplay. One of my favorite features of this game was that I could load it up, find a match, and stay on the server for hours. In fact, thats how I met alot of my steam friends. We would chat for up to three hours before adding each other to play games together. On top of that, I could have my friends join me at anytime rather than having to wait for the match to be over.
However, with Casual, I need to group up with my friends BEFORE I enter a match as they cannot join mid game and I need to find a new match after every round. This means that I can't have a friendly conversation with other people as it will most likely get cut off by the end of the match.
Now, if they added Casual ALONGSIDE Quickplay, this wouldn't be a problem. And I know that the long wait times was a bug with Casual's matchmaking bot, but it still takes a bit more time to find a match than with Quickplay, and where you need to find a new match at the end of every round, the time can stack up.
Due to the current state of this game, I just can't recommend it. I hope Valve can address the issues the community is having at the moment and can establish a better method of communication with the playerbase to avoid future problems. However, in TF2's current state, the future of the game looks pretty bleak.

This is an amazing game. Although it is constantly bombarded with complaints, I think Valve has done an excellent job of keeping this game still alive even through all these years. They might have did wrongs, (EOTL, I've got my eyes on you.), but as seen in the more recent gunmettle update added the much hyped for Cp_snowplow, which redeemed itself.
Each class is designed so that they overpower certain classes, while being weak to another. The spy, for instance, is usually strong against heavy, but weak against pyros. (Hate those things) But this isn't a bad thing. It is still possible to win in a fight, but you usually either have an advantage or disadvantage. With careful teamwork. you can make unstoppable rushes or inpenetratable defenses.
Also, each class has a high learning curve. Some games, like the much hyped for overwatch let you "Rocket jump" with the touch of a single button, but this in my opinion makes it fun for newer players, but leaves more experienced players yearning for a skill they can achieve. In TF2, it is extremely hard to master. Every class has its own "Special skill" that you must learn to perform in the real game. Like scouts surfing with the shortstop to soldiers much coveted rocket jump, it gives the game a sence of achievement, like that feeling when you get your first rocket jump and go soaring.
This game is also constantly being updated. Heck, since last week I got at least 5 updates, about 1 every day since this update, just to fix unnoticable exploits. I mean, who would notice a knockback with the scorch shot while under the uber of a quickfix.
Just recently, this update fixed many unnoticed weapons, neglected by many. For instance, the big earner more infamously known as the big yearner, was recently buffed to give a speedboost whilst keeping all its attributes. This caused a new gameplay style, paired off with the nerfed dead ringer which was rampant and allowed the spy to play extremely aggresively, you can be the "Fast" spy.
Others might say TF2 is a dead game, but for me, this game even if it is surpassed, will still live on in those games.

This is an amazing game. Although it is constantly bombarded with complaints, I think Valve has done an excellent job of keeping this game still alive even through all these years. They might have did wrongs, (EOTL, I've got my eyes on you.), but as seen in the more recent gunmettle update added the much hyped for Cp_snowplow, which redeemed itself.
Each class is designed so that they overpower certain classes, while being weak to another. The spy, for instance, is usually strong against heavy, but weak against pyros. (Hate those things) But this isn't a bad thing. It is still possible to win in a fight, but you usually either have an advantage or disadvantage. With careful teamwork. you can make unstoppable rushes or inpenetratable defenses.
Also, each class has a high learning curve. Some games, like the much hyped for overwatch let you "Rocket jump" with the touch of a single button, but this in my opinion makes it fun for newer players, but leaves more experienced players yearning for a skill they can achieve. In TF2, it is extremely hard to master. Every class has its own "Special skill" that you must learn to perform in the real game. Like scouts surfing with the shortstop to soldiers much coveted rocket jump, it gives the game a sence of achievement, like that feeling when you get your first rocket jump and go soaring.
This game is also constantly being updated. Heck, since last week I got at least 5 updates, about 1 every day since this update, just to fix unnoticable exploits. I mean, who would notice a knockback with the scorch shot while under the uber of a quickfix.
Just recently, this update fixed many unnoticed weapons, neglected by many. For instance, the big earner more infamously known as the big yearner, was recently buffed to give a speedboost whilst keeping all its attributes. This caused a new gameplay style, paired off with the nerfed dead ringer which was rampant and allowed the spy to play extremely aggresively, you can be the "Fast" spy.
Others might say TF2 is a dead game, but for me, this game even if it is surpassed, will still live on in those games.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Team Fortress 2 is the long awaited sequel to Team Fortress, which went through an infamous 9 years in development. During this, lots of ideas and concepts were realised and scrapped until Valve agreed on the sort of 1960's esque pixar like cartoon art style, which I think really helped this game stand out from the crowd of generic, "realistic" modern military games at the time, when everyone wanted to be real without thinking of art style. Then, the Orange box was announced, to sell Half Life 2: Episode Two, along with the bonus games of Portal and Team Fortress 2, finally, we were getting what was long considered vaporware.
Team Fortess 2 was a pretty fun Multiplayer game, with fun characters and great atmosphere, along with an awesome modding community, and community in general, it was pretty much "The most fun you'll ever have online" according to PC gamer, and while I won't really agree, it was definately up there. For a pretty decent ammount of time, it went from being the 2nd most popular Orange box game, and then the most popular, and would only get more content through updates, among them were new items.
The new items I felt really were needed in this game for longevity's sake and an incentive to keep playing for achievements, but then Valve added hats, and eventually there was enough items in the game to warrant a trading system. Little did valve know however that there was some serious hat economy going on in TF2, and so when they realized this, they added the item shop, now Valve was making money off of virtual items. It's not really anything new, a bunch of people did it on Second life and Furcadia did it about a decade before (And more overpriced), but Valve made so much money off of it, they realised that they could pretty much make the game free, and in fact not make games at all since they can just release a bunch of hats people can buy. This game is pretty much what I can say eventually lead to the downfall of Valve, when they discovered that they could get more money faster and cheaper by just making a virtual item.
Still, despite this, I feel TF2 is still a fun game worth playing. I know it sounds really crazy, but there are a lot of pretty cool mod servers and custom maps, I still feel like there's a lot of fun to be had, even if the game is basically milked out for all it's worth. Thanks to the art style, the graphics have aged like fine wine and the characters are still fun.

Good FPS game. True, cosmetics are a bit of a money grabber but they make the game what it is. This game is quite casual in gameplay unlike other FPSs and is funner thathat way. The best thing about the game is the variety of classes, and different strategies within each class, which offers a wide array of possibilities for different types of players.
Overall, I'd rate it 9/10, extremely good for an F2P game.
Note: Valve tried to merge this game with CS:GO (skins, grades, wear, cases) and I think that TF2 should be kept as it's own game. The recent invasion update has been more TF2 (thanks Valve).

Creative Bankruptcy is plugging in an eight year old game into the unregulated market of minutely different yet wildly expensive images applied to 3d meshes that has been so profitable to that company's other multiplayer first person shooter. The beauty is that, much like hats and weapon designs, they won't even need to hire artists to develop these assets after a while--because they just pay the community less than actual employees to do it for them.
It is true that gun skins and tour crates do not have an effect on gameplay. However, I would think gameplay would be an important part of an update to a game. Especially when it's the big selling point of that update.
And I'm not saying this will kill TF2. It won't. I've played this game on and off since it came out and you had to pay money to even get the game, and it still hasn't died. Even if the glory days are over you can sit down and still have a decent round or two if you are dying to.
But if any company that didn't have the mythology that Valve has as being THE company that's different from all the rest released an update to a long standing game that required you to pay not once but twice to access its content--with the inevitability of future payments confirmed--the digital ink bemoaning the practice on message boards across the web wouldn't be able to dry fast enough.

What if you add a Game, with overall complete Mechanics, Packed with game modes, And with 9 Simplistic Clas-, I mean Mercs, and Run it on the Source Engine with a Cartoon-ish and querky art style, what do you get? This Masterpiece of a game. 9 Mercs is enough to get every one by, no matter the match, of course, have to much of 1 Merc, Isn't good, besides the facts, every class has a way of killing another class, is there a Heavy, Spy will do the trick! Is that Spy now murdering your team? Pyro will set 'em a blaze, and he won't come back. The game (Tries) to balance every thing to make the game fair, and I'd say it does it good enough to make gamers world wide come back to this game, Also, for the many weapons it gives the Merc's to use in battle, It is sure to keep many lasting for a long time.
But, I'm only talking about the good side.
Valve is a Top-Notch game development team, Don't get me wrong, but manly focus on tempting Free to Play Players to Become Premium, and not as much as the game balancing and Adding items, because, let's face it, just because I said the currently existing items will last for a long time, some people don't find Items interesting enough, and want more to keep them interested, And Since the addition of the Steam Workshop, most will find that Valve doesn't notice the Perfection in alot of items you can find today. And most Weapons added are from the Workshop. I am not trying to go out of my way to say Valve is lazy, but rather Should spend more time on The game itself, instead of keeping the river of cash flowing. Finally, The Team Fortress 2 Economy is on a tipping See-saw, and Valve, is on one end, not giving a crap.
If you don't know, Keys And Ear Buds are going up in price and they, are high in price already. I suggest you search the topic up, as this Review as getting long enough.
But honestly, I like game the way it is.
Then again, it is my Opinion, and my Opinion doesn't really matter.

Back in Spring 2015, I played Team Fortress 2 for the first time, and it was hella fun. But I picked a wrong time to start playing since the game has lacked updates on that time, then came Gun Mettle. I wasn't really affected by it, since I'm new and all, they only added some new maps and bug fixes and weapon skins, so I was fine with it. Then the god-forbidden Tough Break update. I got my hopes up for a new weapon(s) and what did I get? New maps, skins and of course the "make-my-gun-lightup-like-an-xmas-tree-izer". And then, the phlog buff. I really don't know what Valve was thinking, the phlog was already notorious for its noob-friendly stats, you can literally W+M1 with it and get a 5 man kill streak, with no effort at all. And then they buffed it, why.. I thought to myself that I'd give the TF2 Team another chance, and when I heard of the "neato" update (MyM). I started getting excited for it, since matchmaking was being asked for for a long time by the community. Then it came, the new update, I was playing before the update came out and when I got disconnected and saw my downloads tab, I got super pumped up. Then led to disappointment, they changed quickplay to a CSGO-esque style server picker, and the horrible horrible way of delivering the update overall. You know, TF2 is a
game. Not meant to be taken seriously by the majority of its players unless they're full-on tryhards, which belong in matchmaking. I remember the times when I got home from school and started playing TF2 the whole weekend since it was fun as hell. Now, I have to sit through 2-5 minutes of finding a casual match, then getting disappointed, since it's just a matter of who-pubstomps-who. TF2 is not supposed to compete with
games like Overwatch and CSGO. It's a
game, for the second time.
I really wish I had more time to play this game. But so far, it's OK.

Team Fortress 2 is an amazing game. It has survived since 2007, which is a great feat. Some people say this is because the game is free, but you don't keep playing a game for 8 years if it's bad just because it's free! Not to mention, many people buy hats, weapons, etc. for real money!
How has TF2 survived this long? This game is probably the most creative FPS ever made. In games like CS:GO and Call of Duty, you are in some generic military team taking out other generic military opponents. I don't mean to bash these games, but the cold, military FPS shooter combination is getting awful stale.
That's where TF2 comes in. Sure, TF2 is about mercenaries which are soldiers in the military, but you might notice something when choosing who to play as....... There are nine different classes, all with different weapons, play styles, looks, and most of all, PERSONALITY!
Personality is one thing a lot of generic FPS games lack nowadays. Heck, if you scroll up, you can watch an entire short movie about the Pyro's personality, which was made more to show it's personality than to actually introduce how the character plays!
Speaking of creativity, look at the weapon choices. There are several different weapons and tools to choose from for each class. You can use the starter weapons, but the real game begins when you discover the other ones. Each non-stock weapon has it's own pros and cons, unless it's a reskin of a stock weapon. This creates variety in gameplay and new strategies. You could literally go on a killing spree with a ham or pummel the enemy team with a mailbox.
Also if you want to keep your wallet, don't read into "stranges" and "unusuals".... trust me.
Like many FPS games, there are a variety of game modes. Payload, a race to push a cart carrying a bomb to the goal, good old capture the flag, king of the hill, and more! All of these game modes have multiple maps to choose from.
But maybe you don't want to actually play the game. You want to sit around be a goofball on trade servers. You can do that too, you casual! The game has many cosmetic hats you can show off, and taunts to mess around with. Boy does it feel good to snipe someone and laugh in the face of the kill cam.
By the way, yeah, there's a trade feature. Trade me all of your stuff.
Speaking of other ways to play the game, the awesome community has created custom gamemodes, such as VS Saxton Hale, a juggernaut game mode.
Valve has really interacted with the community to help this game grow as well. New maps, taunts, hats, and weapons have been ripped straight from the community that has kept this game alive for 8 years.
I just want to mention real quick, TF2 DOES have a competitive community. But I wont go into that since this review is aimed at people still missing out on this game.
One more thing, there's a game mode where you get to fight a robot army. 'Nuff said.
TL;DR
All in all, TF2 is a great game with plenty of variety, personality, and fun. I have made friends and I have lost hundreds of dollars. GG. 10/10.

I really don't know what Valve was thinking, the phlog was already notorious for its noob-friendly stats, you can literally W+M1 with it and get a 5 man kill streak, with no effort at all. I started getting excited for it, since matchmaking was being asked for for a long time by the community. Then it came, the new update, I was playing before the update came out and when I got disconnected and saw my downloads tab, I got super pumped up. game. Not meant to be taken seriously by the majority of its players unless they're full-on tryhards, which belong in matchmaking. I remember the times when I got home from school and started playing TF2 the whole weekend since it was fun as hell. Now, I have to sit through 2-5 minutes of finding a casual match, then getting disappointed, since it's just a matter of who-pubstomps-who. TF2 is not supposed to compete with
games like Overwatch and CSGO. It's a
game, for the second time.

Team Fortress 2, here I go. Looking for a game that's free to play, a first person shooter, and down right fun as hell? Well, you've come to the right game! All 9 classes add for a diverse choice of playing styles, but that's only part of it. Weapons, lots of extra weapons. The large universe of weapons can assist you in your play style or just change it completely
. The large selection of weapons allow for a diverse and quite unique experience for the first person shooter genre, and there's still not something that can match up to this game. But, the main reason most people play Team Fortress 2 is for it's 1 of a kind trading system. While is is sometimes unrelliable, trade servers and all, Team Fortress's 2 trading system is a game changer. You can trade hats, miscs, and weapons, and trust me, you're better off having hats, because in this game, your generally considered
for having loads of hats and unusuals. Ah! Unusuals, almost forgot about those things. Unusuals are basically hats with special effects like flames or a snow cloud over your head or on your head. They are obtained through purchasing Mann Co. Supply Crate Keys
from the Mann. Co Store or the Steam Market or other sources, and using them to unbox a crate that corresponds with that specific key, generally reffered to unboxing or un-crating. Players have a very rare chance to unbox these "Unusuals", but when you do, consider yourself "Done with trading"
. That's Team Fortress 2 in a LONG Nutshell.

Team Fortress 2 is an FPS Free 2 Play, where you have the possibility to choice one of nine classes, everyone balanced(except pyro, shame on you, pyro). I played this game for a lot of time, and i'm not bored yet.
+ Nine classes, one extremely different from the others, and, at the same time, very balanced
+ Lots of maps and gameplay (Well, compared to other games)
+ A lot of guns/items very balanced (For example, i knife who get you bleed for six seconds, will take less damage in front of the normal knife)
+ You can forge items/guns from other items/guns
+ Taunts ( There's people who hate taunts, but, in my opinion, they are nice)
+ You can play without spend a cent(Like me, but that's not mean they're not trying to make you buy something)
+ It's Free!
- Mann Co. Shop (The game try everything to make you buy something. EVERYTHING)
- Limited Bag (Very Tiny, you can expand the bag by buying something from the Mann Co. Shop)
- Screaming Children, screaming children everywhere ( You can mute them, anyway)
- Pyro ( They burn EVERYTHING, except other pyros. Spies, Engineers, Scouts etc...  can't survive if pyros are in the offing. And they are very easy to use. In short words, they're gods)
- Mann Vs Machine mode is not free(you have to pay a ticket for one game. Yes, one I think, i've never play it)
- People who kick you for nothing ( I was kicked out from a round, accused of cheating, just 'cause i've ask to shut up to a moron who was doing NOTHING)
I will update this list if i find something more.

So I attended E3 and got to have a special one on one confrence with Gabe himself. He showcased a new game that was to be officially released on the third of July 2015. The name of the game?
Counter Fortresss Global Teamfensive: The Sequel (also known as CFGT)
Take a read of this exclusive interview with Gabe I managed to record (don't worry it's not IGN).
- start of interview -
Why hello Lord Gaben, I'm here to talk to you about your new game, Counter Fortresss Global Teamfensive: The Sequel. Share with me all the special details about the game if you'd be so kind to, from start to finish. I would also like to know how you came up with the idea on the game. I know you've always been disclosed about your games at Valve, but you can trust me, I'm not recording this.
Hello to you too. I'd be very proud to talk about our new game, and our innovative approach to this new game. It came along this one confrence we had. It went like this.
"♥♥♥♥ TF2 IS ♥♥♥♥ING UP"
"I KNOW WHAT DO WE DO"
-random guy in corner, turns his chair in slow motion- " we make tf2... COUNTER STRIKE"
-everyone celebrates-
So we've decided to borrow some inspiration from our money cow- I mean popular game Counter Strike, but we kept everything that made the game good (to us) and took the gameplay from our best selling free to play game Team Fortress 2. We've introduced brand new exclusive Stattra- I mean strange weapons that you can unbox from very special cases. These weapons have a kill count attatched to the side of the weapon, something no game has ever done before. We've also decided to give players a unique opportunity to chip in $6 to a pass where they can earn never before seen, rarity of weapons by appearance going in the order of, Factory New, Minimal Wear, Field-Tested, Well-Worn and Battle Scarred. We believe that by adding these features, we'll gain even more players, and hopefully forget about that disaster game Team Fortress 2 and it's economy that we slipped up with by giving people what they wanted. You also get to earn a unique coin that can be displayed in game to show off to everyone you've participated in a very special coin, again another feature that's unique to our game. We really tried our hardest to make a unique first person shooter experience in our new game, Counter Fortresss Global Teamfensive: The Sequel. We hope you enjoy the game that hits you this Summer.

Entirely unique classes give you entirely new experience. Teammates are essential and teamwork is the key. The ultra high skill ceiling makes the game constantly challenging and rewarding.
The feature I love most about this game is the Medic's Ubercharge ability. It gives the Medic, a stereotypically boring push-over type support class, a friggin GOD MODE POWAH along with the teammate(s) he heals. He doesn't headshot, doesn't gib people but he owns matches. This ability gives the support the highest importance and connects the whole team together because if it doesn't take care of the med, it is going to lose horribly. For me, I don't play the med myself but the Uber+the usual healing power makes exploding the other team's only life support pretty addictive.
For the negative side, there're always some cheaters roaming about in public servers and Valve can't do or doesn't do much about it. The unique environment does require some time to understand the flow of things for new players and you do need teammates who knows what they're doing to actually play the game to its potential.
Its free, its fantastic.

I've been playing TF2 since November of 2011. I've been playing this game throughout the weirdest years of my life thus far. Something about this caught my eye when I was 11 years old and I've been playing it ever since. 6 years goes by really quick, it seems like just yesterday I figured out I could use steam achievement manager to get free items, or I finally completed the Croc o' style item set.
In my 2000 hours I've seen most of it, I've drifted from idle/trade servers as the gibus scout just trying to level his strange weapon, to quickplay servers as a semi-decent sniper, to the medic main who goes on community servers with his friends looking for real challenges. I've mained every single class at one point or another, switching on and off every couple of months. I don't think at any point I've ever been bored.
This game is unique. There is nothing like Team Fortress 2. I have tried just about every single game that people claim is the "New TF2" and none of them even come close. No matter where I go or what I play, I find myself coming back here because nothing can deliver the same experience.
Some would argue that this game is dying. I don't agree with them. I see TF2 as an unkillable beast, 60,000 people come to play this game every single day of the week, this game has maintained a place in the top ten most played games on steam for a majority of its lifetime. This game is never going away, the people of this game are never going away. And that's not going to change no matter how inconsiderate Valve is of this game.
TF2 is like a ship, and right now, Valve is the captain of that ship. As Valve ignores her more and more, Team Fortress 2 is going to get lost at sea. She's never going to sink, she'll still be there, ever drifting with her 60,000 strong crew day in and day out. I think I'm fine with getting lost at sea on such a beautiful ship.
Team Fortress 2 isn't going away. We'll be here for a long time. You can join the crew anytime you like, I mean, it's free.
