Team fortress 2 the most played game in my library. TF2 has it all, funny, action, team work, gore, replayabilty. so im going to divide it up into those 5 parts.
1st-Funny/comical
TF2 has a very cartonny look. not to say that is bad, it actually makes the game that much better. it also has many funny cosmetics and taunts. the name tags and description tags are a good way to make people laugh with any funny name you decide to put on it*. the meet the classes are very funny also.
*beware there are mature players on this game so there will be a few NSFW (not safe for work) names on some guns. for example i have a gun named "The tampon" with the description being, "It has blood on it and it heals. What more do you need in a tampon?"
2nd- action
TF2 is and always will be a FPS (first-person shooter) it is not as popular as COD or BF4, but it has just as much action. in TF2 you have 9 classes each with diffrent play styles. (i will not go into depth with each one.) Each one adds something new to the battlefield so that players will always be looking for cover or that one medic on your team. In short it is very fast paced but still very fun.
3rd- Team work
TF2 has team work in its name, thus it is centered around team work. Although some matched will have you felling like you were just left for dead, most matches won't. for every match that lacks in team work there are 10 or more that make up for it.
4th-gore
Like i said it is a cartonny game but that dosen't mean that it dosent have its fair share of gore. You will see bodies blowing up with blood following it. Keep in mind that this game does not thrive on this, that only happens when you get killed by an explosive. and when it does happen you won't see much of the gorey bits because most of it is croped out of the screen because of a window that appears when you die.
5th-replayabilty
This game is hihgly replayable. Although it can get tedious from now and then, all you have to do is play with a buddy and it gets way more better. And if it dosen't, playing games like CS:GO that is very fun but at the same time stressful, will have you wanting to play a game like TF2.
in short this game can be very fun but can get tedious. when that happens just play a diffrent more realistic game you will realise how fun TF2 can be.
Note:
the community for this game is not the best but is very friendly

Entirely unique classes give you entirely new experience. Teammates are essential and teamwork is the key. The ultra high skill ceiling makes the game constantly challenging and rewarding.
The feature I love most about this game is the Medic's Ubercharge ability. It gives the Medic, a stereotypically boring push-over type support class, a friggin GOD MODE POWAH along with the teammate(s) he heals. He doesn't headshot, doesn't gib people but he owns matches. This ability gives the support the highest importance and connects the whole team together because if it doesn't take care of the med, it is going to lose horribly. For me, I don't play the med myself but the Uber+the usual healing power makes exploding the other team's only life support pretty addictive.
For the negative side, there're always some cheaters roaming about in public servers and Valve can't do or doesn't do much about it. The unique environment does require some time to understand the flow of things for new players and you do need teammates who knows what they're doing to actually play the game to its potential.

Team Fortress 2 has been my most played game, and I love it to death. The game features to opposing factions, RED and BLU, fighting for territory with hired mercenaries. The class selections is well balanced, and strategy is key, unless you're like me and just like stealing the intel. This is a genre, FP shooter, that I almost hate, but the cartoonish graphics and cosmetics, along with the vast array of weapons, makes it an awesome game. I've probably put around 40$ into items for this game, but you can still enjoy it for 0$, but I'd recommend buying the cheapest item in the store, just to get the trade ability. Here are the pros and cons of this game.
Pros
-Fast paced gameplay combining strategy with madness
-Awesome graphics, even with a bottom of the barrel laptop
-Customizeable characters with unique items and personalities
-Great game to have fun with your buddies
-The scout is featured (my favourite class)
-You will get at LEAST 500 hours of gameplay before the game gets dull
-Offline practices to help newer players learn about the game
Cons
-People do scam you if you aren't careful, had it happen to me a year ago
-Valve kinda nudges you towards buying items, but I'd only buy the keys if you do
-Community can be harsh, but remember, this is in most games
Overall, this game has been a really great, and it has shown me a great 2 years. I'd seriously recommend getting it. It is free after all.

This is a pretty awesome and fun game. You can select up to 9 different classes: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy on either a Red or Blue Team. The gameplay consists things like capturing control points, launching an Australiam bomb, and pushing a payload cart with a bomb, all while killing enemies with different unique weapons and even earning certain items as you play and different hats and accessories you can wear. It may not sound like much, but it's really fun, trust me. It's bloody and gory, but in a funny cartoony way. The voice acting is also hilarious; I find the"FIRE FIRE FIRE!!" sounds, the Pyro's "HELP! HELP!!" and the Heavy's death cries really funny. I like to play as Pyro, Heavy, Scout and Soldier, although I am doing good as well as an Engineer and a Spy.
I recommend this game to everyone who likes first person shooter games. Probably one of the other best things about this game is that it's free!

The only things I don't like about this game are squeakers, the P2P elitists, and people who say "TF2 is dying". Overall, it's a pretty good game.

I don't care what people say, the classes in this game are very well balanced... unless there's a hacker.  Then snipers are basically gods.  Or spies with the ambassador... or Heavies with increased damage... the list goes on.  But yes, the classes are well balanced... okay fine.. maybe a few items like Phlo pyros should never have existed..
but anyhow.. that hasn't made too many people quit this game!  Heh, I'm a M1 pyro, so I'm one of those noobs that everyone hates, but torching people's a lot of fun.  That.. and backstabbing... building a LV3 sentry... (well, not as fun if no one is spy checking, but w/e)
All I'm saying is, if you don't love this game, then I doubt you'll like many FPS games.  Considering there's so many ways to play this game instead of just aim and shoot.  The drawback is, you really need to take your time to learn the maps, otherwise you'll be a real liability to the team.
with that said, the auto balance feature in the game is F*cked up in the recent years.  In certain games, a team can be missing 5 guys and the game refuses to auto balance.  In certain servers, the games are perfectly balanced, many RED lost but BLUE had to put in ALOT of effort to secure that win, and yet, the game decides to F*ck-all and auto balance.
No idea where this trend started, but people start saying "rekt" a LOT in the games..  Yes, we kill you 100 times, you kill us one time and I've been "rekt".  I don't get offended.. It just feels a lot like hearing people play broken music over their mics.. its annoying.
now, everytime I kill someone with my backburner, people call me M1 pyro.  Kiddies, like me explain what a M1 Pyro is.  It is a pyro who just stupidly charges at you holding M1 no matter the distance.  What I do, is I sneak behind you, and backburn you, I don't "dragon charge" you.  not to mention I don't whip out my flamethrower till i get very close, I use my shotgun and my flaregun ranged.. so.. I think some kids need to learn the definitions before actually using the terms.
I RARELY accuse hackers ingame.  I merely leave the server when I detect a cheater..  And these are confirmed hackers, not just OMFGWTFBBQ I got UBER HEADSHOTTED DURRR.  No, I spectated, saw how the player's screen stutters with the crosair literally snap onto people's heads.  I don't know whether VAC is slowing down or hackers are improving drastically.  But one thing's for sure, almost every game I've been part of.  There's at least one hacker.

This game is by far one of the best games I have ever played. I have recently hit 1,000 hours so as you can see it is kind of addicting.
It seems like just a first person shooter until you spend five minutes on a server. You'll quickly realize that this isn't your average shooter.
The game is based around 9 different classes, scoot, soldier, pyro, demoman, pootis, engie, medic, sniper, and shpee. There are many many weapons to use making the game never boring not to mention the amount of maps.
Now to discuss different aspects of the game.
Classes: Every class has it's uses and can kill every other class and be killed by every other class. Although some are easier to play Heavy, pyro and others may be harder sniper, spy eventually they become easy to play.
Weapons: The weapons for the most part are all useful in some way although, with the sheer amount of them there are some duds, (my personal least favorite is the loch and load), but the most of them are either useable or amazing. And with everyone using a different weapon it makes for interesting gameplay. There are three types of weapons primary, secondary, and melee. All three have uses but your primary is usually the most important. It can throw your enemy for a curve ball when you use a secondary or melee though.
Community: The community for Team Fortress 2 is far better than most. Most people here are normal people not raging 12 year olds, and are for the most part fun to play with. I'd say that this games community is far better than counter strikes, CoD's, halos or any other games.
Items and Values: The game is totally free to play but you will probably find yourself spending far too much money on items. Things have different values and are usually not what the in game store says they are. What I would suggest is buy something cheap off of the store to get premium then just buy off of the steam marketplace. Note if it says "Unusual" it's valuable. The amount of different varieties of items is overwhelming and makes the game just a bit crazier. Now to talk about cosmetics. These serve absolutely no purpose but to customize your character. although at the same time they are one of the best parts of this game and what gives it most of it's craziness.
Maps and Gametypes: About every map is fun and I have yet to find one I don't like. There are quite a lot of them allowing for the game to last even longer without getting boring. The gametypes are usually nothing too special they aren't bad but for the most part wvery other shooter has the exact same ones except for payload which is my personal favorite.
Teams: Your average team will consist of 12 people, 2 pyro's who just installed the game 10 minutes ago, a scout on an 18 killstreak, 4 statues (AFK people), 2 sandwich heavies, a spy with the cloak and dagger who has been sitting in one spot for at least 94 seconds, an engineer who has set up at the last point and won't move, and you.
All in all it has fun gameplay, a good community, fun classes, cool weapons, tons and tons of items, and fun maps and gametypes.
Definetely a 10/10 game (You should download since it's completely free).

This game is by far one of the best games I have ever played. I have recently hit 1,000 hours so as you can see it is kind of addicting.
It seems like just a first person shooter until you spend five minutes on a server. You'll quickly realize that this isn't your average shooter.
The game is based around 9 different classes, scoot, soldier, pyro, demoman, pootis, engie, medic, sniper, and shpee. There are many many weapons to use making the game never boring not to mention the amount of maps.
Now to discuss different aspects of the game.
Classes: Every class has it's uses and can kill every other class and be killed by every other class. Although some are easier to play Heavy, pyro and others may be harder sniper, spy eventually they become easy to play.
Weapons: The weapons for the most part are all useful in some way although, with the sheer amount of them there are some duds, (my personal least favorite is the loch and load), but the most of them are either useable or amazing. And with everyone using a different weapon it makes for interesting gameplay. There are three types of weapons primary, secondary, and melee. All three have uses but your primary is usually the most important. It can throw your enemy for a curve ball when you use a secondary or melee though.
Community: The community for Team Fortress 2 is far better than most. Most people here are normal people not raging 12 year olds, and are for the most part fun to play with. I'd say that this games community is far better than counter strikes, CoD's, halos or any other games.
Items and Values: The game is totally free to play but you will probably find yourself spending far too much money on items. Things have different values and are usually not what the in game store says they are. What I would suggest is buy something cheap off of the store to get premium then just buy off of the steam marketplace. Note if it says "Unusual" it's valuable. The amount of different varieties of items is overwhelming and makes the game just a bit crazier. Now to talk about cosmetics. These serve absolutely no purpose but to customize your character. although at the same time they are one of the best parts of this game and what gives it most of it's craziness.
Maps and Gametypes: About every map is fun and I have yet to find one I don't like. There are quite a lot of them allowing for the game to last even longer without getting boring. The gametypes are usually nothing too special they aren't bad but for the most part wvery other shooter has the exact same ones except for payload which is my personal favorite.
Teams: Your average team will consist of 12 people, 2 pyro's who just installed the game 10 minutes ago, a scout on an 18 killstreak, 4 statues (AFK people), 2 sandwich heavies, a spy with the cloak and dagger who has been sitting in one spot for at least 94 seconds, an engineer who has set up at the last point and won't move, and you.
All in all it has fun gameplay, a good community, fun classes, cool weapons, tons and tons of items, and fun maps and gametypes.
Definetely a 10/10 game (You should download since it's completely free).

I got this game on my first account because it was free, and a fps.
I kept playing for the sheer chaos of the pub servers. Some of this chaos would include the following:
You join an official Valve server. Once you connect, you select Red, and your favorite class. (my fav. is Soldier)  The first thing you see is that 1-2 people are afk. You walk out of spawn and wait for the gates to open. You see that the Blu team are congaing inside spawn. Stickies are laid out in front of the gates. 3-5 sniper laser-dots are glued to the gates, just waiting for someting to hit. Uber charges are ready on both sides of these gates. Sentries are ready, wranglered and pointed at the gates. The match is about to start. Then, the clock counts down: 3...2...1, and the gates open. All hell breaks loose. Ubers are popped, Snipers are missing headshots, some miraculously hitting heads. People are dieing instantly. Blu is rushing to the adjective, you're on Red, so you take action. But, as soon as you contest the enemy scout capping the point, you are instantly blown up from a random crit. The demoman that crit you taunts, and you auto balance to the other team. You instantly start to rage, then realise that this is tf2, and this kind of stuff happens here.
If you read all of this, thanks I had a lot of fun writing this. I sincerely love this game, and I am sure that many people think the same way.

All I'm saying is, if you don't love this game, then I doubt you'll like many FPS games.  Considering there's so many ways to play this game instead of just aim and shoot.  The drawback is, you really need to take your time to learn the maps, otherwise you'll be a real liability to the team.
with that said, the auto balance feature in the game is F*cked up in the recent years.  In certain games, a team can be missing 5 guys and the game refuses to auto balance.  In certain servers, the games are perfectly balanced, many RED lost but BLUE had to put in ALOT of effort to secure that win, and yet, the game decides to F*ck-all and auto balance.
No idea where this trend started, but people start saying "rekt" a LOT in the games..  Yes, we kill you 100 times, you kill us one time and I've been "rekt".  I don't get offended.. It just feels a lot like hearing people play broken music over their mics.. its annoying.
now, everytime I kill someone with my backburner, people call me M1 pyro.  Kiddies, like me explain what a M1 Pyro is.  It is a pyro who just stupidly charges at you holding M1 no matter the distance. I think some kids need to learn the definitions before actually using the terms.

This game is by far one of the best games I have ever played. I have recently hit 1,000 hours so as you can see it is kind of addicting.
It seems like just a first person shooter until you spend five minutes on a server. You'll quickly realize that this isn't your average shooter.
The game is based around 9 different classes, scoot, soldier, pyro, demoman, pootis, engie, medic, sniper, and shpee. There are many many weapons to use making the game never boring not to mention the amount of maps.
Now to discuss different aspects of the game.
Classes: Every class has it's uses and can kill every other class and be killed by every other class. Although some are easier to play Heavy, pyro and others may be harder sniper, spy eventually they become easy to play.
Weapons: The weapons for the most part are all useful in some way although, with the sheer amount of them there are some duds, (my personal least favorite is the loch and load), but the most of them are either useable or amazing. And with everyone using a different weapon it makes for interesting gameplay. There are three types of weapons primary, secondary, and melee. All three have uses but your primary is usually the most important. It can throw your enemy for a curve ball when you use a secondary or melee though.
Community: The community for Team Fortress 2 is far better than most. Most people here are normal people not raging 12 year olds, and are for the most part fun to play with. I'd say that this games community is far better than counter strikes, CoD's, halos or any other games.
Items and Values: The game is totally free to play but you will probably find yourself spending far too much money on items. Things have different values and are usually not what the in game store says they are. What I would suggest is buy something cheap off of the store to get premium then just buy off of the steam marketplace. Note if it says "Unusual" it's valuable. The amount of different varieties of items is overwhelming and makes the game just a bit crazier. Now to talk about cosmetics. These serve absolutely no purpose but to customize your character. although at the same time they are one of the best parts of this game and what gives it most of it's craziness.
Maps and Gametypes: About every map is fun and I have yet to find one I don't like. There are quite a lot of them allowing for the game to last even longer without getting boring. The gametypes are usually nothing too special they aren't bad but for the most part wvery other shooter has the exact same ones except for payload which is my personal favorite.
Teams: Your average team will consist of 12 people, 2 pyro's who just installed the game 10 minutes ago, a scout on an 18 killstreak, 4 statues (AFK people), 2 sandwich heavies, a spy with the cloak and dagger who has been sitting in one spot for at least 94 seconds, an engineer who has set up at the last point and won't move, and you.
All in all it has fun gameplay, a good community, fun classes, cool weapons, tons and tons of items, and fun maps and gametypes.
Definetely a 10/10 game (You should download since it's completely free).

2014-2016 Review: This game started out as a beautiful creation. This game was an absolutely unique style with its own cartoony graphics followed behind the most BEST ways of presenting the entire 9 man team and their personalitys. However sense the Gunmettle update this game has slowly started to slip from its former glory. This game started to try and copy CS:GO which ruins what was once so Unique about it.This game used to be a game that was a different experience all on its own. It was a team experience that  honeslty brought a smile to anyones face from joining their first pub server to leaving their last this game used to be so Unique it would pull different players in from everywhere. Now its trying its best to stay afloat when everyone can clearly see the game is Dwindling from its former glory. Dont get me wrong. I LOVE team fortress 2. However this game has run out of update Ideas. It hurts to see that the updates are pay to join and have become pay to get a crate to just pay for a key for that crate. Unboxing used to be a optional thing and it still is but its being pressured to unbox more and more by valve with every single update. I have had my fair share of the whole experience in this game and this review is coming from someone who has seen it all.
I have seen the trader experience and the player experience this game offers. I have crossed the battlefield of mvm. I have run across the pubs. I have joined every update and I can conclude that this game is losing its spunk.
I have had a couple Ideas For updates (IE maybe medic makes some sort of mistake and one of the characters get to become female.) I know many of you agree most likely FEMALE characters would be a HUGE change in this game that would make both an interesing sfm AND an interesting update. It would be one that is completely free for the team fortress 2 community and it would be one that allows a female player to become a female character.
Regardless. This is MY opinion on it. I have watched friend after friend cash out on this game and slowly walk away from the memories they made with every step.
It is your choice to play or not to play. What role you take is all your own decision. Here are a couple videos of MY playthroughs to see if you still want to play or not to play.

I think it's around time to remake this review.
Ever since the major backlash from Meet Your Match, the Team Fortress team has really been trying a bit harder to actually update their game and fix some bugs that have been around a while, like the crouch exploit or being able to build outside the playable area or being able to shoot through certain spawn gates. I'm just hoping that this newfound "try a bit harder or else we'll lose players" is long term and not some sort of damage control that'll have their communication and slightly more frequent updates fade by Christmas. If the team keeps this up, I see a better future for Team Fortress both competitively and casually than it was in perhaps one or two years ago, when numbers started dipping.
Now this doesn't means everything right now is perfect and nothing needs changing. I can make a list of all the currently known things that TF2 needs fixed, like certain balancing issues revolving around certain classes and playstyles, the hot mess that is competitive mode, abandonment penalties (and how they completely ruin competitive for me), and many more. But I have faith in the team that they can listen to these complaints and fix or otherwise rework them. They have shown recently that they can fix things quickly, like how a bug having to deal with MvM was fixed the very next day the issue was brought up. But again, I hope that they stay on their game long term and don't just slow down when things go more smoothly.
The game has an amazing community who are truly passionate in the game, who has (mostly) stuck with the game even through its toughest points. This is especially prevalent in just how many community updates I've seen in the past, who the contributors to said updates have truly created some phenomenal things from weapons to cosmetics to full-blown maps. And they do this with absolutely no guarantee that they're going to get their items in the game. It's also shown in how they are several people talking about the issues that the game has/had on places like Reddit and YouTube. If they didn't care about this game nearly as much as they did, they probably would have just straight up leave instead of sticking with the game and talking about its issues.
While I am starting to play TF2 less and less because of what I call "life moving me forward", I do see several people joining and supporting this game in general, but especially competitively in the future.

After a few years playing Team Fortress 2, I still occasionally boot up this game and toy around with the insane amount of variety in weapons this game has. Don't feel like a sniper rifle? Use a bow instead. A little bored of explosions? Swap out your grenade launcher for a sword and shield.
The best part about these weapons is that they're all balanced, meaning that any custom weapon someone has would be an even fight against stock weapons, and Valve are still constantly tweaking weapon balance for the weapons that turn out to be a little to under or over powered. No money must be put into this game to achieve an advantage over someone else.
Obtaining these weapons is fairly easy. Weapons are randomly dropped, which can then be kept or crafted/traded for other weapons. All weapons are of the same value, while the more expensive weapons are purely cosmetic. Again, these weapons are no better than the stock weapons you start with, they simply spice up the game when the stock weapons start to get boring, and by the time they do you would already have many other weapons to equip from random drops.
This game is often compared to Overwatch, but as a player of both games I must say they are almost completely different. The weapon choices of TF2 is similar to the hero choices of Overwatch, and they both have similar gamemodes. But what separates these games is that Overwatch is more focused on smaller teams and maps and often requiring a great team to actually get anywhere, while TF2 is 24 player insanity. And it's amazing.
My only real issue with TF2 is the long death timers, which really ruin the fast paced action of the game and seem to put a lot of players off, although implementing a better system while keeping the game balanced may not be possible.
Team Fortress 2 is without a doubt the greatest free to play game in existence, and is certainly one of the greatest games of all time.

After a few years playing Team Fortress 2, I still occasionally boot up this game and toy around with the insane amount of variety in weapons this game has. Don't feel like a sniper rifle? Use a bow instead. A little bored of explosions? Swap out your grenade launcher for a sword and shield.
The best part about these weapons is that they're all balanced, meaning that any custom weapon someone has would be an even fight against stock weapons, and Valve are still constantly tweaking weapon balance for the weapons that turn out to be a little to under or over powered. No money must be put into this game to achieve an advantage over someone else.
Obtaining these weapons is fairly easy. Weapons are randomly dropped, which can then be kept or crafted/traded for other weapons. All weapons are of the same value, while the more expensive weapons are purely cosmetic. Again, these weapons are no better than the stock weapons you start with, they simply spice up the game when the stock weapons start to get boring, and by the time they do you would already have many other weapons to equip from random drops.
This game is often compared to Overwatch, but as a player of both games I must say they are almost completely different. The weapon choices of TF2 is similar to the hero choices of Overwatch, and they both have similar gamemodes. But what separates these games is that Overwatch is more focused on smaller teams and maps and often requiring a great team to actually get anywhere, while TF2 is 24 player insanity. And it's amazing.
My only real issue with TF2 is the long death timers, which really ruin the fast paced action of the game and seem to put a lot of players off, although implementing a better system while keeping the game balanced may not be possible.
Team Fortress 2 is without a doubt the greatest free to play game in existence, and is certainly one of the greatest games of all time.

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community. Since GameSpot's original TF2 review, the game has benefited from numerous updates and made the jump to a free-to-play business model. So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2014 among the current crop of competitors for your time and money?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community. Since GameSpot's original TF2 review, the game has benefited from numerous updates and made the jump to a free-to-play business model. So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2014 among the current crop of competitors for your time and money?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.

Although I've only played the game for around ~350 hours at the time of writing this, (which is much lower compared to how long some of my friends have played the game for) I can safely say that TF2 was really one of the best multiplayer experiences I've had. It got some of my friends into PC gaming, created small LAN parties with one of my groups of friends, and overall gave us a fun experience.
TF2 stands out in many points. First of all, it's free to play, so even if you really don't like it for whatever reason, there is really no harm in adding it to your Steam library. Second of all, the game is HIGHLY customizable. There's a ton of mods (which don't add anything gameplay-wise however customization instead) for the game, as well as the community servers which intoduce different maps and gamemodes. Lastly, it's one of the only free to play games that DON'T force in-game purchases upon the player. Almost everything can be obtained by drops, trading, the market, etc.
Overall, I really enjoyed TF2 back when our group played it extensively. We might get back into it, even though we moved onto other games such as Garry's Mod and CS:GO (Which are also great games, go figure). So, if you haven't played it yet, and have a few friends with a computer that can run it, (TF2 isn't really a power-hungry game, I've played it on a craptop just fine) you should DEFINITELY play the game together.

Second of all, the game is HIGHLY customizable. There's a ton of mods (which don't add anything gameplay-wise however customization instead) for the game, as well as the community servers which intoduce different maps and gamemodes. Lastly, it's one of the only free to play games that DON'T force in-game purchases upon the player. Almost everything can be obtained by drops, trading, the market, etc.
Overall, I really enjoyed TF2 back when our group played it extensively. We might get back into it, even though we moved onto other games such as Garry's Mod and CS:GO (Which are also great games, go figure). So, if you haven't played it yet, and have a few friends with a computer that can run it, (TF2 isn't really a power-hungry game, I've played it on a craptop just fine) you should DEFINITELY play the game together.

As a guy who has spent countless hours playing this game, I think it's safe to say that this game is one of the best games in my Steam Library. The gameplay is phenominal; The graphics are great, the artstyle is original, and the characters' dialogue are hilarious. Further more, Team Fortress 2 DOES NOT require you to purchase any items. You don't have to buy all the weapons you want: You can just earn them or find them randomly. Unlike other games, You're just fine using the starter items.
The fact that most of the weapons and costumes are user-created is also a big plus. You can vote for your favorite items in the Steam Workshop to be put into the game! This creates a sense of being a part of the game, and also opens up an infinite amount of doors to where this game goes next.
Overall, It's a solid A+++! I can't stress enough how awesome of a game this is!

With a little over 200 hours of playtime, I can officially call myself a Begginner+. Once I hit the 500 hour mark, I will be a Decent player. Overall, this is a fun, addicting FPS that doesn't take itself seriously, unlike others that try too hard to be "realistic".
There are 9 classes to choose from and each can be individualised for a completely different playstyle than the default. You can be a typical Medic going around keeping teammates alive or equip more aggressive weapons and become a battle-medic, killing enemies and focusing on yourself. You can be a default Demoman and blow up targets from afar and set traps, or equip a sword, shield and peg-leg and become a demoknight, getting up close to decapitate enemies. Speaking of peg-legs, the weapons are just as much of a "joke" as the personality of the game. You can kill people with a fish, a railiroad sign, a golf club, a lollipop, etc, and those are just the melee.
The cosmetics are where the game truly shines AND fails. The wearable items are there just to make you look fashionable AND drain your wallet. After 200 hours, I have only a small handful of hats compared to the veterans who have pages and pages or them. While it's nice that there's so much diversity, it's ridiculus how much they cost. Don't be surprised if you see something you like on another player, go to the store, and see it costs over 20 bucks. It's possible to only buy 2 or 3 items and trade your way up to getting some good stuff, or just craft it yourself, though getting enough scraps can take ages, but that's extremely difficult considering the game has been out for almost a decade and most players already have what you want to trade.
Lastly, be prepared to delete dozens if not hundreds of crates by the time you hit 100 hours.
9/10 Not bad
TL:DR : Really fun. Not serious. Expensive hats. Too many crates.

This game is just amazing and it's free to play! I just really love this game so much. 9 different classes, each character is different in both apperance, personality, voicing, and weapon using. Each character is helpful in some way and sometimes those characters could be powerful to take down.
Like for a few exmples:
The combo Medics: Both have Uber Saws and both have the default Medic Gun. Continue to take down their foes with the Uber saws while the other uses their own Uber with their Medic Guns to keep both of them alive. When the saw is full, they switch and do the same prograss all over again. It's a bit tricky but it's a really good way of taking out the other team.
Pyro's airblast: Some players may not realize this but the Pyro's airblast abilty is pretty handy at times. It can send back whatever attack the other team sends at. The Soldier's missiles to the Demoman's bombs, to even the Sniper's arrows! Be careful when being near a Pyro that knows how to time it prefect with their airblasting. Though keep this in mind; the Pyro can't send back everything so be careful.
Soldier/Demoman Rocket Jumping: It doens't really matter what weapon you use, as long as you switch to the right weapon slot you can do the rocket jump with either Soldier or Demo. It's actually pretty fun and it can also suprise anyone who is not looking up at the skies. Though just a quick warning: keep a eye on that health of yours unless your using the actual weapon call the Rocket Jumper.
There are pretty much a lot of ways other players use. Some can be a bit annoying- others it can be helpful. The game is not recommanded for kids by the way, though I know that kids still play games like TF2 anyways. I recommand this game to everyone. 10/10 rating.

After playing only a few thousand hours over different accounts i have decided what i like and what i don't like about this game.
To start off i want to say that i deeply like this game and have dedicated many hours playing both community servers and valve servers, and enjoy both, there is a fairly medium size variety of gamemodes to play, factoring in community there are 50+ which you could play for hours. These many gamemodes can keep you entertainted for hours on end before you realise you were meant to finish that one piece of homework for tomorrow and quickly rush off to do it. I have recently tried the grappling hook mode (i have no idea what it is called) and enjoy it to some extent. CTP and CTF/CTB are still fun to me but i mainly practice my aiming on other community servers like PPM or plaza where i trade and play. The variety of the gamemodes makes the game playable for a long time, whilst more gamemodes and maps are created to make the game more fresh than before.
There are some things that i think would be a great idea to put into the game like : Mini-Dispencers which have been concepted many months ago which i have a nagging feeling like they will be implimented. Another awesome weapon idea is a tracking weapon, though this may be overpowered in some cases it could be easily fixed by reducing ammo and or damage/building damage to even the playing field out a bit more. This is a great idea because it would be able to destroy geniously placed sentries which you would otherwise take a lot of damage off before you destroy them. Another cool concept that i have thought up and i am sure others have as well is a sniper which you can zoom in and out with. I think this could be a cool little addition to the game and would help in short range fire-fights in which a snipers primary would be useless. But hey, that is just what i think. One more small addition is an anti-gore option in the advanced options, i play the game and i would like a way of turning off the gore with a button and not spending hours finding the command, this would help the game (for me) feel less of a ruthless killing game and more fun (in my oppinion).
Now to the things that i don't like about the game. The biggest most anoying thing about this game is the fact that it is too fun to play. Tf2 is one of my very first f2p shooters, and it has a very special place in my heart. The fact I've spent over 4,000 hours in this game says a lot, but I'm sure a lot of you out there have more hours than me. Tf2 is... something special... it's gone through high water and hell and still come out barely scarred. Though the development team is limited in numbers, I believe they're doing their best to keep this game going. Developing new weapons I would imagine is very difficult due to the massive amount of unique weapons this game already has. Figuring out how a new mechanic would react with other gameplay elements takes a lot of time, and releasing them out to the community may result in a few bugs, but that's all part of improving. Nothing in it's first form is "perfect" and there's always loop-holes. Another note is that TF2 is based off of the original half-life code. That's ancient. Imagine having to do your math homework but all the numbers were in roman numerals, just look in the perspective in that math uses modern numbers like 1,2,3,4... etc. versus I, II, III, IV... etc. it's a lot more complicated, (Obviously if you're used to reading roman numerals, it's simple). Using old code that's been worked over for many years is not an easy feat. On the other hand, the fact that Jill (One of the developers) has announced the beta testing for I guess new code? It's definitely a step forward in getting TF2 into a modern state where perhaps more developers at Valve will be inclined to working on. Back to gameplay, balancing teams in casual and competitive is also something a lot of people have been speaking out on lately, and I completely relate. Joining an in progress casual match and being placed on the team with 9 players versus 12 isn't fun at all, and leaving a game with a penalty isn't the greatest because "things" happen. Balancing generally in my opinion an issue spread across almost every game. If the TF2 developers decided to enable an option to join a game in progress, I'd imagine many players would disable it because of experiences of joining an in-progress match where the team you joined is getting steam-rolled or is consistently losing. Based on the some 500 games I've played in casual, usually when I take a look at the scoreboard, every team's casual level is about added up to the same level, but it doesn't necessarily mean equal skill level. I don't think there's an efficient way to satisfy balancing teams and to what the community wants, it's just something hard to achieve.
On a side note, yes, I play the alternative game modes  and have managed / helped develop / admin a few of the side games the community has created. (Freak Fortress 2, Saxton Hale, Slender Fortress, PropHunt, WarioWare, Custom MvM, UberUpgrades, Surf Maps, Achievement Servers, etc.)
I've probably rambled on about a lot of the same stuff but it's what I see a lot being discussed about in the game. I'll come back and edit this as I get pulled even more into this amazing game. <3

The fact I've spent over 4,000 hours in this game says a lot, but I'm sure a lot of you out there have more hours than me. Tf2 is... something special... it's gone through high water and hell and still come out barely scarred. Though the development team is limited in numbers, I believe they're doing their best to keep this game going. Developing new weapons I would imagine is very difficult due to the massive amount of unique weapons this game already has. Figuring out how a new mechanic would react with other gameplay elements takes a lot of time, and releasing them out to the community may result in a few bugs, but that's all part of improving. Nothing in it's first form is "perfect" and there's always loop-holes. Another note is that TF2 is based off of the original half-life code. That's ancient. Imagine having to do your math homework but all the numbers were in roman numerals, just look in the perspective in that math uses modern numbers like 1,2,3,4... etc. versus I, II, III, IV... etc. it's a lot more complicated, (Obviously if you're used to reading roman numerals, it's simple). Using old code that's been worked over for many years is not an easy feat. On the other hand, the fact that Jill (One of the developers) has announced the beta testing for I guess new code? It's definitely a step forward in getting TF2 into a modern state where perhaps more developers at Valve will be inclined to working on. Back to gameplay, balancing teams in casual and competitive is also something a lot of people have been speaking out on lately, and I completely relate. Joining an in progress casual match and being placed on the team with 9 players versus 12 isn't fun at all, and leaving a game with a penalty isn't the greatest because "things" happen. Balancing generally in my opinion an issue spread across almost every game. If the TF2 developers decided to enable an option to join a game in progress, I'd imagine many players would disable it because of experiences of joining an in-progress match where the team you joined is getting steam-rolled or is consistently losing. Based on the some 500 games I've played in casual, usually when I take a look at the scoreboard, every team's casual level is about added up to the same level, but it doesn't necessarily mean equal skill level. I don't think there's an efficient way to satisfy balancing teams and to what the community wants, it's just something hard to achieve.
On a side note, yes, I play the alternative game modes  and have managed / helped develop / admin a few of the side games the community has created. (Freak Fortress 2, Saxton Hale, Slender Fortress, PropHunt, WarioWare, Custom MvM, UberUpgrades, Surf Maps, Achievement Servers, etc.)
I've probably rambled on about a lot of the same stuff but it's what I see a lot being discussed about in the game. I'll come back and edit this as I get pulled even more into this amazing game. <3

There are a total of nine careers that can be simulated in this program, all of which are diverse from one another to give the broadest view of all the possible future careers for you! After selecting your potential future career, you will be placed in a simulated world where you can interact with another person in real time! That other person could even help you excel in a specific career if you believe it is the perfect career for you.

Try it now, today, and I'll guarentee you, you'll be learning and having lots of fun at the same time.

Around 2011 i started playing this game on my friends pc, it was so fun i would go to his house EVERY day after school to play it

2013 was my year of pugs and pro, i had a small team who werent 100% perfect but were good enough, we won a few matches lost a few but the good outweighed the bad, we a couple months in stopped talking to each other and the team split up
July-August 2013 was my programming/modding phase were i modded fallout and programmed crappy games in java and did not play too much tf2
September  2013 - January  2014 i played casually and did a decent amount of trading but not much of anything
2014 january- may was a confusing time for me, i had just finished a crappy game i made and put wayyyyy too much time into and meanwhile the people i used to talk to stopped talking to me so i just decided to quit. (around may 25-30th) and from there i stopped playing, i moved on i thought i was done until.....
may 10th 2015, i had installed linux(ubuntu 14.04lts) and decided to check out the games i had on my pc from my steam library (only 50 out of 110 but all the games i actually play :P) and saw tf2, dusty and rugged asking for me to play it once more, just to get a taste of nostalgia. I got on my old server i used to go on filled with people, and met new friends or regulars i played with, blb, lamb, sir jensen, who reminded me of the tf2 friends i used to have but were gone.Sure the game was unbalanced, made bad decisions and was a silly, hat simulator, but it was MY silly hat simulator and thats why i love it.

Team Fortress 2 was the very first official PC game I have ever owned.I loved this game to bits.I've seen youtubers play it everyday ever since i have heard of it.I really wanted the game so much i tried everything to try and play flash games about it.I knew about steam,in fact,the only reason I got steam was to play it and see it for myself.I was filled with so much joy seeing the main menu,the character looking at me from it,It was like a dream.Yes i may be overreacting,but if you had a laptop from 2007,you'd doubt you could run anything on that.Im going to stop talking about the story on how i got it and the story of what i did to play at least a parody,on to the game itself.The game was very well balanced.I loved the satisfaction of finding a new item as a new comer.Like most first person shooters there's always gamemodes.Tf2 had ver intracit gamemodes.Payload,Capture the points,they were original to me.King of the hill and capture the flag,I've seen those in many first person shooters.None the less,I loved every gamemode.The characters i loved the most.Each class had a different style of gameplay.Each with different,special weapons for only them.My favorite so far is the soldier,I main him.The scout is my second favorite.I would like to say thank you valve for making this game,I speak for everyone who plays it.

OK, I've been delaying this review long enough. Strap yourselves in, this one's gonna be a long ride.
TF2 is, by far, the largest and possibly the greatest online VALVe game. In history. The community is active, expansive, and to be honest and bland, different. This means it comes with custom maps, mods, gamemodes, models, classes, weapons, and moreso. There is no game in my entire library that 119+ people on my friends list play, and they are right about their choice of game.
Even if you don't have money, get this game. It's free, brilliantly designed, and active. The characters each have their own unique personality that makes them stand out. Sometimes it makes me argue with myself which one to choose (even if my main is Soldier.) There is just no way to play this game without exploring all the choices and weapons and different combinations.
It's just... fun, to put it in my simplest way possible. And to think it gets even better.
If you actually do get the "Pay-to-Play" upgrade, (which you can get by buying an item off of the Mann Co. Store; the lowest item costs $0.49 I believe) you get more items each week, and maybe even some more free items! Plus, you can always buy stuff from the offical store, AND the online market.
However, I have to warn people who are just coming into the game. HEED MY WORDS!
TF2 is a hard game to grasp fully, in the correct way. With that in mind, many players will call you a noob. If this is the case, I am open to train some people on some "hang out" servers. It may take a while to download all the stuff, but I'll be waiting. Just don't follow me everywhere, OK?
ALSO! If the first hat you get is the Gibus and/or Pyrovision, delay wearing it. Until you get a bit better at the game, people will laugh and point at you. Lemme tell ya, the Ghastly/Ghastlier/Ghostly/Ghastlierest Gibus is a hater MAGNET. Don't fray though, people will think twice about you when I'm done with ya.
Anyway, that was my review-thing. You can stop reading and actually get this game now.
It has its moments.

I have mixed feelings about this game. It is amazing in some aspects, yet not too much in others.
Let's first start off with the pros. The game is FREE! If you have a computer, then you have no real excuse not to have this game. You say that you may not be able to run it? It runs on the Source Engine! I run it great with my 32MB Intel HD Graphics Card. No excuse to not have it. Also, there is a healthy player base in spite of the game's age. It also recieves updates still to this day. The game also has a good amount of PvP game modes. However, there is an excellent PvE mode in the game as well, namely, Mann vs. Machine. Grab your friends, because you are going to have a blast trying to beat some of the insanely chaotic levels such as Ghost Town at round 66666 or something like that. On top of that, you can also buy many weapons in the Steam Community Market or from crates!
Wait... Buying that kind of stuff? Let's move into some cons. This game can suck you right in to buying weapons for your in-game character. Firearms aren't the only thing, though. There are also many collectible hats. Before I rant on for ages about the market, let's move on. For many classes, the weapons just do not feel nice. For instance, the Heavy's minigun is bad for 1v1 situations due to it's massive spread, though it is great for mowing down a whole group. It is rather hard to just pick-up-and-play as well, as it takes plenty of experimenting to find the right class for you. Also, some of the classes are somewhat unbalanced. The Sniper is a great example. 1-hit kills al over the place for him. Enemy gets too close? He pulls out a very rapid-firing SMG. And the Enginner is a nightmare. Just plant equipment everywhere and begin the trolling. A lot of the community is rude as well. Just because I drop the briefcase this one person just begins blurting out many 4-letter words at me.
THE FINAL SCORE: 78/100
CONCLUSION
This is a good game to play simply for Mann Vs. Machine. I do not feel that this game has any other value than that mode.

It is the most user-friendly too, with it's cartoon visuals, many will find it appealing. It is easy to learn from scratch, and people new to the game will pick up the mechanics and style very quickly. There are around 8 different gamemodes currently: from CTF to good old bases, this is a very widespread game with loads of variety. I'd rate this game a: 9/10. Unique, interesting and free. Why not give it a go?

Literally my favorite shooter of all time. The game never gets old, the community is astounding, the characters are well-written, and the gameplay is always fun.
There are those that think TF2 is dead or all the people online are just sitting around trading, if you are one of those people, please direct your attention to:
And multiple other sites.
I have heard people call TF2 "pay 2 win", and that is simply not true. Actually, a good chunk of the time the stock weapons are better than weapons you get from drops/crates/etc. The weapons you can buy from the store can also come as drops, be purchased cheaply through trading through sites like scrap.tf (we are talking 2 weapons for 1 scrap, which is worth no more than 3 cents), or traded from friends or players in game. Those strange/killstreak/unusual items you get from crates? Those properties are purely cosmetic and give you absolutely no benefit in game.
Yes, TF2 can be competitive as well. Just because it's a silly game does not mean it can't be competitive. TF2 is possibly the most balanced game I have ever played, with a few exceptions (*cough loch'n'load cough*). These exceptions are usually banned in competitive via whitelists to make the gameplay fair for everybody.  Every class/weapon has a counter.
While its true TF2 trading is dying out because of players moving to CS:GO trading, the game itself is not even close to dead.
TF2 has not been abandoned by valve. As a matter of fact, an

Team Fortress 2: The Game that Won't Die
This game is older than dirt. And that shows. The game is not optimized very well, with years of code and bug fixes stacked on top of each other. The graphics aren't top-of-the-line HD 4k ultra!
But these are minor complaints compared to what TF2 does have.
The community around Team Fortress 2, though sometimes salty, and very goofy, is one of the best and most loyal. There are loads of fans creating content for this community, whether that is weapon skins, workshop items, custom maps, SFM posters and movies, YouTube videos, or stupid memes.
Team Fortress 2 is also known as the wolrd's first Hat Simulator with an FPS built in. The amount of customization is nearly endless with the hundreds of hats and other cosmetics this game has to offer, not to mention paints.
TF2 also has one of the best Free2Play models out there. Nothing you buy makes you a better player. There are a handful of weapon unlocks (which you can get just from playing the game) that are arguably better than the default stock weapons, but for the most part, all unlockable weapons are just sidegrades. If you want to spend hundreds of dollars on hats, go right ahead. But no matter how much money you spend on TF2, none of it will make you a better player.
Speaking of being a better player, TF2 is easy to learn, but hard to master. Each of the 9 classes play completely differently and have strengths and weaknesses that balance each other out. The skill ceiling in TF2 is nearly infinite. There's always something new to master, whether that's rocket jumping, surfing, sticky jumping, or a whole host of other skills.
Competitve? TF2 has a strong competitve community as well, spanning 4 continents and thousands of players. Have some fun playing in a 9v9 format with Highlander which uses each class, or try your hand at 6v6. With multiple leagues to play in, and a growing presence online, competitve TF2 is the place to be.
Still not convinced that Team Fortress 2 is a great game? Give it a try! It's FREE for crying out loud!

The Life of a Team Fortress 2 Man
Day 1: Learned about a Neat game from friends called Team Fortress 2, Went home and downloaded it.
Game is great!
Day 1 Ending Playtime = 3 hrs on record
Day 2: Finds Mann Co store and learns about the wonderful weapon varieties and chooses to buy a couple of things, A sandman, Ambassador, Degreaser, and a Brass Beast and continues to play.
Day 2 Ending Playtime = 5 hrs on record
Day 3: Killed a Scout a couple of times and eventually dominated him and got a hat called the Ghostly Gibus, "Wait there are hats in the game?" I eventually noticed I also had a Mann Co Cap that I recieved when I bought the weapons. I put the hats on my people, they looked about 0.5x cooler then they used to be! I got to the Mann Co Store and began buying hats right away!
Day 3 Ending Playtime = 14 hrs on record
Day 4: Have a ton of new hats that I began to trade with my friends. I eventually scammed one of them into giving me an Unusual sadly though I lost all my friends after that, although I didint care cause now I had hats to keep my company. Eventually went to servers to play more
Day 4 Ending Playtime = 26 hrs on record
Day 5: My hats are beginning to speak to me and I got into a relationship with one of them. I love my Pink Gibus so much and I married it on TF2 with a whole ceremony and everything! A hacker joined the server though and hacked everything up and stole all of my items including my Pink Gibus and my Unusual. Im very sad at the moment and I began to buy more hats to keep myself occupied.
Day 5 Ending Playtime = 46 hrs on record
Day 6: Got everything back and learned to play TF2 cautiously. Sadly though my credit card is empty and I cant pay for the bills. I play TF2 all day to comfort myself.
Day 6 Ending Playtime = 70 hrs on record
Day 7: My life is ruined because of TF2. I lost everything I ever had and I couldnt pay for the electricity bill so I cant even play TF2 to comfort myself, I cursed Gaben for what he has done to me and I swore to god that I would one day get my revenge
Hats/10

Team Fortress 2... where do I begin.
First of all there's hats.
Second is that this FPS is like no other you have ever seen before. There are many mechanics built into the game that make it stand out from the bunch. Take rocket jumping for example or taunt-kills. Each individual thing makes this game one of the best to be viewed and/or played. And it's FREE!
On the topic of free, if you do decide on downloading this game, be prepared for people calling you a noob (which is fair since you just GOT THE DAMN THING) or what us TF2 players call "F2Ps". F2Ps is an abbreviation of Free To Plays, a group of people that have downloaded the game for free and do not have a premium account (more on premium accounts in-game.) Although I downloaded the game in September 2012 when it was free and to be honest I disliked it back then (probably because I had a♥♥♥♥♥♥computer with ultra low FPS) but now I enjoy every aspect of the game. That spy just taunt-killed you instead of backstabbing? Well I laugh my♥♥♥♥♥off. Those 2 hoovies in the corner of the room nomming on sandviches? Join in and PUT A ♥♥♥♥ING DISPENSER THERE FOR CHRIST SAKE!
So there you have it. TF2 has been one of my most beloved games in the world. Making me laugh every step of the way.

Team Fortress 2 is a unique first-person shooter that relies on team and class-based gameplay mechanics and the like. With the variance between the 9 classes available, there is likely one that will suit your play style, or one you may simply enjoy. It's cartoony and lighthearted style make for a quite amusing experience as you play more and more with the different classes. You can learn to take advantage of the different classes' capabilities as well as the various weapons available to all players through random loot drops.
In this case, the use of the common free-to-play gimmick comes up as fairly respectable, considering that Team Fortress 2 used to be purchased like most games, making it considerable that the game has a significant level of quality to it, and, gameplay-wise, you get all the content that anyone can get.
Because the nine classes play so differently, you have a lot of things that you can do, without letting the game get too boring. Personally, I play a lot as one class, but that is simply because it is reflective of my play style. While playing TF2 for the first time, it is a good idea to play around with the different classes, as there is some things one must learn going into the game.
The community doesn't seem too encouraging to new players, and that is understandable because the team-based gameplay requires people to work together to complete the objective. Luckily, though, the game has a system where, in most servers, players can start a vote deciding whether or not the teams will be scrambled. This mechanic can help less experienced players on the losing team to not be singled out, or outright blamed for their team's losses.
Overall, being free-to-play, Team Fortress 2 is a must for anybody who likes the general concept of a shooter. It might not be your thing, but if you gave it a try, I don't think it would be a waste of time.

Decided to change my review after meet your match. Meet your match was an update everyone was excited for. People have wanted matchmaking for years and years.... and as soon as it comes out its just a big letdown.
Competetive mode isnt really competetive... all it really does is limit the players in a game and there is barely any communication among the players.The lack of banned items like in ugc or etf2l makes it so there is no meta... making it seem way more gimicky then a competetive gamemode should be. Not to mention the grind you have to commit to when playing competetive. You start at level 1. There are no placements. Just grind. For all the people who have played csgo or overwatch, how would it feel if you started at 1 SR or Silver 1 is csgo. You wouldn't bother with competetive. You would just play for fun. And thats how i feel this "competetive" mode is. Its not really a display of skill, its just showing how much time you put into the game.
Next comes the talk about the quickplay removal. Yes it does technically make pubs better and yea its more competetive. Lets be honest though, TF2 was never made to be a competetive game and valve shouldnt have forced it onto the people who didnt want to play competetively.
Before meet your match (maybe gunmettle too), highly reccomended.

I've loved this game, made many friends playing it.... I discovered bootcamp and mvm about 200 hours in and although I didnt spent more than $20 dollars on the tickets I took overwhelming joy in playing boot camp with all the friends I'd made playing it. Working with them we took down wave 666 and expert difficulty maps and it was fun and the satisfaction was great. I pretty much abandoned normal servers and stuck to boot camp, challenging the meta setups that sapped all the fun out of it in the name of 'winning'. Although I dont have all the mvm acheivements on my list I completed; wave 666, nightmare mode, 31 times and at least once with every class, and every normal, intermediate, advanced and expert mission offered to us across all the maps.
However, this doesnt mean I didnt see the rest of the game changing too. The Gunmetal update and Tough Break, they not only changed everything in the normal servers, I saw MVM change too; and I didnt like it at all. I came to realise that after these updates mvm started to die a bit. the skill levels in servers began to lower and lower and many would give up too soon or simply start kicking people without reason. I have always been against meta setups and the idea of kicking players in bootcamp isnt something I like at all. Meta is acceptable in Mann-up made, you are there to WIN and get australium items, but in boot camp, meta merely sucks the fun and the variety out of matches. Now kicking people, it became so common after Gunmetal; it was already a common sight before but afterwards it averaged out to two people getting kicked every match or atleast the votes being called in mvm servers I was playing on. It made me realise that the community I had become a part of had begun a decline after that update, whether it attracted new players who were like this or transformed some of the older ones I will never know but what I do know is that the mvm I had fallen in love with was gone.
So I changed with it, I made an effort to have 3 or more friends in a party at all times and I rarely went in by myself and it worked well.
And then came Tough Break... this is when I stopped playing tf2 daily and playing bootcamp with my friends; the item changes and the way they had changed boot camp made it difficult to play with the same variety as before and I burnt out fast. Public servers for bootcamp became completely toxic and with me and my friends becoming limited by changes we all burnt out fast.
Nowadays, seeing me in tf2 is a rare occurence and if I am I'll be playing with friends in a 3-6 player party in bootcamp. I'm sad to type the words 'Team Fortress 2 is dead for players like me' but it is the truth. I'm a mvm player who watched the gamemode they love wither and die, I'll miss the days when me and my friends would team up and take on wave 666 together, and we may well be doing it if you see me in tf2, but tf2 is dead for me and that's a fact.
That 'yes' isnt so much regret in downloading the game, but regret for what i saw happen to it over the time I've spent with it.

I have a confession to make. I don't like first person shooters. In fact, I kind of despise them. Until recently, it seemed like EVERY new game was an FPS and it seemed like every year we just got more and more. The games I do like, however, seemed to take a backseat to Call of Duty, Battlefield, Killzone, Halo, etc etc in the main stream. When I told someone that I like to play video games, they would assume I meant FPS. It's because of this I never played anything with a first person perspective until 2010 when I discovered Fallout 3 and NV and realized that not all shooters were created equal.
It would slowly open my eyes to a world I had previously ignored.
Cut to 2014 when I learned that I could run more than just Spelunky or Rogue Legacy on my laptop and enter: TEAM FORTRESS 2.
Another confession: I positively loathe playing games online. I just don't see what's so great about a chat room with guns or swords or whatever.
But somehow, this game is different. Now I can go into mechanics or graphics or controls but that wouldn't explain why this is the first FPS I've tried that really sucked me in.
The biggest reason that I can come up with is that this game doesn't take itself seriously. It's certainly not the GuyDudeBroDoritosMountainDew AAA shooter that tends to grind on my nerves when I see them advertised. TF2 has a charm that a lot of other FPS lack.
I am also bothered by Free to Play games. Most of these are cash grabby affairs that have little value regardless of how much you pay in. And don't get me started on the Pay to Win stuff.
Nope, TF2 shouldn't even be on my radar, much less, my favorites. But there it is, and here we are. So a FPS (hate) online only (double hate) F2P (mega hate) game becomes one of my favorites? How?
TF2 is a great game and has taught me not to judge a game by it's genre. And since discovering it, I've opened myself up to even more experiences.

One of the best, if not the best, multiplayer FPS games and its free.  Don't be discouraged by all the fancy cosmetic items as they have no effect on gameplay.  All weapons can be obtained through the achievement system, through the item drop system, or through crafting unwanted items.  It is not necessary to spend money to play, but a single purchase in the store for 5 dollars will give you access to premium status which lets you trade items as well as find rare items in the drop system.  This game has been around for almost 8 years now meaning that players will have a lot of experience. Once again don't be discouraged, just take it a little bit at a time by starting with the built in tutorials that explain most of the game, and then try a few practice games with bots.  If you still need some help try asking me or other experienced players and they should guide you in the right direction. With matchmaking and other updates on the way, TF2 is still very much alive and some of the most fun I've ever had online.
