I know you won't read this if I'm not brief, so I'll try to make this concise:
Optimisation:
This game is not well-optimised in any way whatsoever, and it's only been getting worse. I used to be able to play the game with 90+ FPS in gunfights on a rig with a GTX 260 graphics card on max settings. That card came out in 2008, and is the recommended card to play Skyrim with according to the system requirements. Nowadays, I can barely pull 30 FPS with that rig and card in gunfights on MINIMUM settings. Third-party FPS configs shoud not be a necessary thing for people without $600 to spend on a half-decent gaming PC for a game that came out nearly eight freakin' years ago.
Bugs:
This game has more bugs than any other finished game than I could personally name from experience, with a large number of them disrupting gameplay. Disguised spies walk around with missing limbs. People have their secondaries or melee weapons floating next to them as they walk around. Sentries aim in incorrect directions or have all of their ammo inexplicibly drained after having sappers attached and removed. Building models stretch in random directions during construction animations. Players get stuck in signs when points are capped. I could go on and on like this.
Game Balance:
This game used to be decently balanced and you would rarely come out of a session thinking "I hate that stupid [variable]; it gives [variable] too much power." Nowadays, I can't play the game without thinking that multiple times in a single match. There are a plethora of unbalanced weapons, and Valve does next to nothing; what they do tends to make things worse. I would add a list of unbalanced unlocks, but it would end up being multiple paragraphs of text.
The Community:
Thanks to no paywall, the game is now filled with obnoxious and immature kids and people with no clue how bad the game has become over the years. Expect lots of le epic maymays and "GET REKT KID" spam from people half your age if you're over twenty.
Valve Servers:
Cheaters, no admins, poor connections, and incredibly low-skilled players. It's a marvel that people still play this game when these servers are the prime place for the quickplay feature to dump new players.
Ad Servers:
Thankfully, you can now disable the ads fairly easily, but they still exist and thusly noobs that don't know how to turn them off exist. Basically, there's an HTML exploit which allows servers to lock players in the join server screen (Message Of The Day), and play an advertisement to them. As a result, there's a large number of servers which exist solely to capitalise off of this. These servers tend to be of poor quality in terms of both connection as well as administration. What's sad is that these crappy servers would die off if Valve would just disable HTML MOTDs by default.
Cheaters:
On most servers, such as the aforementioned Valve servers and ad servers, there is no administration preventing people from abusing third-party cheats, and the system in place to prevent them (VAC) doesn't work in a free-to-play environment due to the fact that A. It's a delayed ban., and B. Banned players will simply make a new steam account. Cheats are a fairly common sight in the unadministrated servers, and there is essentially nothing players can do about them but abandon the current game and switch to a new server.
The Dev Team:
Rather than balancing the game, fixing bugs, preventing cheaters, optimising the game, improving the workshop, making good community maps official, or doing anything productive, what have the developers been doing? Working on an irrelevant, unbalanced, and resented gamemode known as Mannpower. What is Mannpower? Basically take TF2, and add mario power ups and a grappling hook. In theory it sounds like it could be a fun little joke gamemode for April Fool's Day or something, but the developers treat it as if it were serious. In my experience, it plays out like this:
1. Players spawn.
2. A player gets a really good power-up.
3. The player with the good power-up stomps the entire other team until his team wins or the time runs out with them spawncamping.
4. Repeat.
Essentially, if you're not on the team with the good power-up, you're playing as the goombas. I get the sneaking suspicion that the entire reason that this game-mode exists is because noobs want to pub-stomp like the players with 2,000 hours without putting any time in.
In conclusion, TF2 was a great game that towered over all else in terms of quality and gameplay, and then Valve metaphorically parked it in a shady alleyway on a moonless night in Detroit for a few years. All that remains of the dev team are the filthy hobos sleeping in the♥♥♥♥♥♥soaked back seat.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Ingredients
-1-1/3 cups butter, softened
-2-2/3 cups sugar
-4 eggs
-3 teaspoons vanilla extract
-2 cups all-purpose flour
-1 cup baking cocoa
-1/2 teaspoon salt
-Confectioners' sugar, optional
Directions
-In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs and vanilla. Combine the flour, cocoa and salt; gradually add to the creamed mixture.
-Spread into a greased 13-in. x 9-in. baking pan. Bake at 350° for 25-30 minutes or until the top is dry and the center is set. Cool completely. Dust with confectioners' sugar if desired. Yield: 2-1/2 dozen.

+Competitive

-Some glitches here and ther(not big glitches to be worried about only small and un-noticable ones)
-Bad community
-Some hackers
-Some scammers
-We can all agree being f2p is limited and is not bad but buying anything (literaly anything) from the ingame store will get you a premium account which lets you in for more weapons to find and be able to trade
-Quite some over-priced items
Overall i just think Team Fortress 2 is a very creative and fun game that I wouldn't mind spending some money on and the number one thing I personally love about this game is just the fact of the nine different classes and all the different weapons (more than 200) which is useful for people like me that get bored of games very quickly and want something new because if you get bored you can just equip a different weapon which changes the game in a way.
Also while i was looking at all these comments i couldn't find any negative ones so far. - :D
- Quick note if you play Call of Duty then there is a big chance you won't enjoy this game but it is not a 100% chance but around 75% of Call of Duty players do not like Team Fortress 2 for whatever reason also the same the other way meaning around 75% (same number :3) of Team Fortress 2 playes have a hate towards Call of Duty, do not hate me for this but it is just a common fact.

There is no other game like tf2.
Tell me, can you find another game where the communication between players is as unique as this? Literally, if you have played this game for more than a hour, you have seen the many ways that the players can express them. There are so many different cosmetics, paints, skins, and unusuals that it is INCREDIBLY rare to find a clone of yourself (which is why people take screenshots when they miracously do happen) . There are unspoken laws about not killing friendlies, never capping on hightower, and so much more. I can type kill in a casual game, and I would expect a few things to happen :

-Another player walks by and then kills himself (usually causing a chain)
-Taunting over my dead corpse (specifically, the schadenfreude)
-Confusion from a new player
-A thumbs up from a seasoned player walking by
Not a single word was exchanged, yet I could confidently say I have had a conversation with these people. That's just how   the playerbase interacts with each other, and it is damn fun. You could tell exactly what type of person that is from just a single act like this.
As for gameplay, there is a playstyle for EVERYONE. Unlike other games, where they give you a gaggle of different heroes, they just provide you the 9 basic ones who each have different items. From the 9, you get the option of three types of classes : Offense, Defense , and support. but in all honesty, they're all lies. You can play any class with any mindset in mind, not just the one they are associated with. The Soldier, a Offense class? Give him a buff banner and a disciplinary action to be providing support to his teammates. The Demoman, a defense character? Well, slap some boots on him and a giant ♥♥♥♥ing sword and tell me  if he is defensive now. The Sniper, a Support role? Watch a game of competitive tf2. There is just so much freedom in how you want to play that I absolutely despise it when people say "I just don't know what to do :((( " . Also, while the word "team" is in the title, you do not necessarily have to be that team player. You can be a lone wolf, picking off of kills and be having a blast while doing it, or paired up with a friend to do nonsensical things. You don't even have to play the damn game ; you can become a friendly where your entire purpose in life is to provide sandwichs and dance for the people who are!
Tl ; Dr So, give it a try. Don't just choose a class, play it, and then leave because he wasn't fun ; You have options for 8 different ones, and hundreds of different variations between them. The community is also great too. I'd highly recommend playing a casual game, then a community server to experience it fully.

Team Fortress 2 is a FPS with cartoonish graphics and heavy reliance on teamwork. It used to be paid, but it went free to play in 2011.
The graphics, despite being a bit old already, still look good and stylish. The maps are usually well-designed and interesting to look at.
The gameplay stands out from your other FPS games for being very different than conventional shooters out there. You can pick from nine different classes: offensive (Scout, Soldier, Pyro), defensive (Demo, Heavy, Engineer) and support (Medic, Sniper, Spy), each with their own unique tools, style, strengths and weaknesses. This forces you to work with your teammates to cover each other's weakpoints and emerge victorious.
There are two main gamemodes: PvP and MvM. The former has a lot of sub-modes, such as Payload, Control Points, Attack / Defense, King of the Hill, or Capture The Flag. The latter, on the other hand, pits a team of six players in a co-op tower defense mode against hordes of bloodthirsty robots, with the objective of preventing them from delivering a bomb to the end of the map.
There is a lot of unlockable weapons, which allow you to customize and change your gameplay style, as well as a ton (and I mean a
) of cosmetic items, which serve no purpose besides looking cool.
The music, while it can't be heard outside of main menu or promotional videos, is very good and fun to listen to even outside the game.
Unfortunately, this game also has cons. Due to the amount of
content, the game is very heavy, so computers that aren't brand-new might experience some performance issues. Also, due to it being free to play, pub servers are often filled with noobs who have no idea what they're doing, which can destroy your gaming experience considering the game is teamwork-reliant. Multiple Snipers and Spies is a common occurence.
The community is also... well, not the worst, but one of the worst. Just a quick glance at the forums reveals a ton of unusual and Australium-toting "git gud" elitists who aren't very pleasant to talk to if you're new... or in general. However, that doesn't mean there aren't any people who are actually helpful towards newcomers.
It was all fine and dandy, a really good game I loved.

Gun Mettle did a lot of good stuff - general weapon rebalances, added a few new maps (including my all-time favorite, Suijin), so why does it get the flak here?
The skins... actually no. They are stupid and lazily ported from CS:GO, but that's not the problem here.

of all things. Yeah, now we have crappy casual matchmaking with long wait times, short games, and no autobalance. I think Valve did it 'cuz Overwatch did it. bring back our pubs. Their removal is a move I simply put can't understand, and likely to be the nail in TF2's coffin due to a very high percentage of players having been enjoying the game via pubs up until now.
Can I reccommend this game now, that the Uber stealing isn't as punishing as it used to? Well... no. Taking a

-Another player walks by and then kills himself (usually causing a chain)
-Taunting over my dead corpse (specifically, the schadenfreude)
-Confusion from a new player
-A thumbs up from a seasoned player walking by
Not a single word was exchanged, yet I could confidently say I have had a conversation with these people. That's just how   the playerbase interacts with each other, and it is damn fun. You could tell exactly what type of person that is from just a single act like this.
As for gameplay, there is a playstyle for EVERYONE. Unlike other games, where they give you a gaggle of different heroes, they just provide you the 9 basic ones who each have different items. From the 9, you get the option of three types of classes : Offense, Defense , and support. but in all honesty, they're all lies. You can play any class with any mindset in mind, not just the one they are associated with. The Soldier, a Offense class? Give him a buff banner and a disciplinary action to be providing support to his teammates. The Demoman, a defense character? Well, slap some boots on him and a giant ♥♥♥♥ing sword and tell me  if he is defensive now. The Sniper, a Support role? Watch a game of competitive tf2. There is just so much freedom in how you want to play that I absolutely despise it when people say "I just don't know what to do :((( " . Also, while the word "team" is in the title, you do not necessarily have to be that team player. You can be a lone wolf, picking off of kills and be having a blast while doing it, or paired up with a friend to do nonsensical things. You don't even have to play the damn game ; you can become a friendly where your entire purpose in life is to provide sandwichs and dance for the people who are!
Tl ; Dr So, give it a try. Don't just choose a class, play it, and then leave because he wasn't fun ; You have options for 8 different ones, and hundreds of different variations between them. The community is also great too. I'd highly recommend playing a casual game, then a community server to experience it fully.

4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing. spag

Gun Mettle turned TF2 in 50% CS:GO, but then Meet your match made it 99.87% CS:GO.
Though some features are messed up now, it can still be an awesome game, I think its even much better when I started playing it in 2013. Its much smoother, and fun (cause of the new taunts.)
Community is great and bad in the same way. There are good people, and then there are tryhards, toxic people, and overall fun ruiners. But honestly, which game at this time has a perfect community?
Gameplay is a bit broken, because of the hitboxes, and some exploits, but Its still a big fun.

I wrote a review for this game a while ago and I think it's time to rewrite it.
The game has had an interesting history to say the least. If you don't want to read a long review the short answer is: play this game it's worth your time.
I'm not the best player, nor the most dedicated. But the community around this game is amazing. Sure you're gonna meet some a-holes and sure there are some sucky areas of the community. But the people in general are great. You'll see a group of people doing the conga, and think nothing of it. But really it's a few people sharing a silly moment together and enjoying themselves. There are in-jokes being carried and continued that have been around for a decade or close to! A decade! That's amazing (and they're still funny too :P). The people I've met playing this game have come and gone and I'm only friends with a few of them still. But I've met friends for life on this game, across borders, and across oceans.
The game play is solid and rewarding, it is satisfying to kill someone and enraging to be killed. But every time you are killed you can learn exactly why you failed and can train around it. Ther skill cap for this game is incredibly high, and it can go higher than you would ever expect. The skill curve is slow to fast for each class varying from incredibly low to it's highest in a week to months of grind to improve and micromanage each skill. Or it can just be a constant increase that slowly and visibly improves over time. Game sense is key, or you can ignore it almost entirely, you've just got to tailor to how you want to play.
Each class is fun, unique and rewarding. There is little to be said without going into detail but there is something for just about anyone in this game. However, it can be said that each is balanced pretty well and you'll find your own community amongst the various mains for each class.
What has to be said though is how the Meet Your Match update affected the game. It was awful, and caused a huge drop in the number of players, especially due to the release of Overwatch. In fact right after launch I played 1 hour of the game and didn't touch it until November of 2017. 467 days I dropped the game for. And the pyro update, though it didn't fix everything was great. The game is once again fun to play and I love it. Even though I didn't play any tf2 in that time I still loved the game and if you play it you'll understand why.
I've played this game through good and bad times and I cannot say that I regret a single minute of it, and I hope to sink in more hours in future :).

Alright, so let's get this out of the way first. The short of it, yes. TF2 is a great game. It's got somewhat of a steep learning curve at first, and some of the concepts like advanced rocket jumping later on seem hard to grasp, but really it's a game worth your time, and money.
Long story short, you've got nine classes to choose from. Each one has weapons and abilities that make each of them unique and adds variety to the game. From the Scout being the fastest class in the game with his double jump, to the Spy and his lethal backstab. To the Soldier and his aformentioned rocket-jump to the Demoman and his sub class, the Demoknight. The Engineer and his construction PDA to the Sniper and his...♥♥♥♥♥♥jar. Yeah. You've got the idea.
TF2's got a wacky style, in both it's characters and how they play and the way the game looks. It has a cartoony sort of feel to it. The visuals are based off of the working of J.C. Leyendecker and it really shows, especially when comparing both the RED and BLU teams. But not only that, it's more centered around a classic sort of FPS akin to that of DOOM, Quake, Duke Nukem, and Wolfenstein. The game never takes itself too seriously. It has those moments of intense action, but always find ways to calm down, creating a fun experience. And that's a word we haven't seen a lot of in recent years. "Fun." The game is legitimately fun and bursting with creativity.
Honestly, it's hard to talk about this game without gushing out. So, TL;DR... Play it. It's fun. Even if the main game itself doesn't appeal, look for some modded servers. You'll find other things to do. Boss fights, a Smash Bros mod, the infamous Saxton Hale mod, Slender Fortress, just go! Download it and give it an honest try! Why are you still here!? Scroll up and download it already!

Obligatory "I don't recommend this game, but I still think it’s great for experienced players."
The reason why I don't recommend with game with a fair number of hours on record, is because it's a hard game for people to pick up and start learning. Valve makes no effort to teach new players, except for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tutorial that only teaches 4/9 classes. And guess what?
It's broken from what I understand.
This leads to new players having no clue what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on at any time. As a result, the community is unfriendly towards these types of players and I don't blame them. It’s very painful to watch a person that just installed go medic and not heal people, and instead have too much confidence in their syringe gun. This is just one example of what new players will tend to do. Because of this, they inevitably suck, and the people who are experienced and on the same team, must carry this dead weight they create and make up for the newbies lack of skill.

This of course, leads to pubs. It’s a lottery in who gets experienced players or players who just installed. You know that leveling system that was implemented a couple of updates ago? Yeah, that means jack♥♥♥♥♥♥ because it’s just random matchmaking, not based on hours or level. This leaves a good chunk of pub matches completely unbalanced and unfun to play, and it only gets worst while playing as the experienced players will leave the oppressed team, simply because they do not like getting rolled and prefer to wait another couple of minutes for having a chance in joining a team that’s holding their own weight.
Another huge factor that increases the imbalance is people who have friends with a few thousand hours on their hands and queue up together, I can't blame them. Everyone has their own idea of fun and I regularly pocket my own friend with kritz who has a bit of comp experience and we can really roll if we want to.
And by "Comp experience" I mean community organized competitive. This is where I also admired tf2 as its community built competitive leagues such as UGC Highlander (9v9) ozfortress, asiafortress and e2tfl(Europe?) from the ground up, and gained endorsement from the TF2 team over at Valve, as they make 1st 2nd 3rd and participant medals you can equip as a cosmetic.
So back to the point, I think TF2 is not-fun for people who just installed. As to gain any experience, they must comb through hundreds of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tutorial videos and guides to get a good understanding of TF2. There’s a steep learning curve that only starts to flatten out at 300 hours, in terms of pub play.
300 Hours can be a lot for people who can't be bothered, or don't have much time on their hands to fully learn class roles, all the weapon unlocks and the layout and techniques of a few popular maps. These ~300 Hours will include painful gameplay as there will be lessons that will have to go through countless respawns to fully grasp.
I personally think this is a great game when the teams aren't stacked, or one team doesn't have an influx of people who installed tf2 along with steam.
If you're willing to put the effort or have a friend willing to teach you, go for it. Install it. It is free. Don't like it? No harm done. But for people with limited time on their hands, and looking for a multiplayer shooter to get into, I wouldn't recommend it.

If you're looking for a review on this game, then you've come to the wrong place. But, if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe, you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Obligatory "I don't recommend this game, but I still think it’s great for experienced players."
The reason why I don't recommend with game with a fair number of hours on record, is because it's a hard game for people to pick up and start learning. Valve makes no effort to teach new players, except for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tutorial that only teaches 4/9 classes. And guess what?
It's broken from what I understand.
This leads to new players having no clue what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on at any time. As a result, the community is unfriendly towards these types of players and I don't blame them. It’s very painful to watch a person that just installed go medic and not heal people, and instead have too much confidence in their syringe gun. This is just one example of what new players will tend to do. Because of this, they inevitably suck, and the people who are experienced and on the same team, must carry this dead weight they create and make up for the newbies lack of skill.

This of course, leads to pubs. It’s a lottery in who gets experienced players or players who just installed. You know that leveling system that was implemented a couple of updates ago? Yeah, that means jack♥♥♥♥♥♥ because it’s just random matchmaking, not based on hours or level. This leaves a good chunk of pub matches completely unbalanced and unfun to play, and it only gets worst while playing as the experienced players will leave the oppressed team, simply because they do not like getting rolled and prefer to wait another couple of minutes for having a chance in joining a team that’s holding their own weight.
Another huge factor that increases the imbalance is people who have friends with a few thousand hours on their hands and queue up together, I can't blame them. Everyone has their own idea of fun and I regularly pocket my own friend with kritz who has a bit of comp experience and we can really roll if we want to.
And by "Comp experience" I mean community organized competitive. This is where I also admired tf2 as its community built competitive leagues such as UGC Highlander (9v9) ozfortress, asiafortress and e2tfl(Europe?) from the ground up, and gained endorsement from the TF2 team over at Valve, as they make 1st 2nd 3rd and participant medals you can equip as a cosmetic.
So back to the point, I think TF2 is not-fun for people who just installed. As to gain any experience, they must comb through hundreds of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tutorial videos and guides to get a good understanding of TF2. There’s a steep learning curve that only starts to flatten out at 300 hours, in terms of pub play.
300 Hours can be a lot for people who can't be bothered, or don't have much time on their hands to fully learn class roles, all the weapon unlocks and the layout and techniques of a few popular maps. These ~300 Hours will include painful gameplay as there will be lessons that will have to go through countless respawns to fully grasp.
I personally think this is a great game when the teams aren't stacked, or one team doesn't have an influx of people who installed tf2 along with steam.
If you're willing to put the effort or have a friend willing to teach you, go for it. Install it. It is free. Don't like it? No harm done. But for people with limited time on their hands, and looking for a multiplayer shooter to get into, I wouldn't recommend it.

I would like to make it clear right now, I love this game.  I love it to death.  However, in it's current state, I do not, under any means, recommend playing this game.  And I will tell you why.
#1)  Hacking
This game is Valve Anti Cheat secure.  However, every time i play this game, i see hackings so unbelievable and so rage inducing, that I think "Maybe I didn't see it at all?"  Until, of course, it happens again.  And again.  It leaves the game horribly unbalanced.  And when you attempt to kick them for hacking or cheating, everyone defends them.  Why?  Because the hacker is either on their team, or they are friends with the hacker.  They end up kicking you for greif in the end.
#2)  Underage Children
I am going to say now, I don't mind when kids play videogames.  However, if I'm a medic who is healing a dying soldier, and a Heavy (played by child) walks by harassing my♥♥♥♥♥asking for me to heal their 100% health for no reason (by spamming the 'medic' button), I'm going to get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  Not to mention in this Free-To-Play format, the game is then given no security from under age children who, in reality, should not be playing this game.  There are kids that have told me to "Stop saying naughty words" in a game where the Soldier says "Damn" and &quot♥♥♥♥♥quot; all the time.  I'm an adult and can say &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; if I die.  (sorry)
#3)  Unbalanced gameplay
Team scrambling happens as a public vote that is given to both teams.  If one team is kicking another teams♥♥♥♥♥super hard, why would they want the teams to be scrambled?  They wouldn't  They will vote against it every time, making the game super unbalanced in the favor of the winning team.
#4)  Mann Vs Machine (particularly Mann Up)
I love the Mann Up missions but when they gave out a ton of free tickets, the servers got flooded with people who were bossy and demanding.  I got kicked from servers for my gender and my preffered loadout so many times.  Now I'm on a lower slot of the server wait-list because of it.
What would fix it?
I'll be honest and say Free-To-Play sounds super awesome.  However so does everyone else.  But what could prevent most of the problems would be charging for the game.  That way, children need permission from their parents to purchase it and it gets rid of, not all of the problems, but a few of them.  I'm not saying this because I baught it in the past.  I started playing this over a year ago.  And for a 9 year old game, i'm still impressed.  However in it's current condition, it's a disappointment.  And unfortunately, it's aggravated me to the point of almost quitting it for good.

This game has alot many people could ask for, all the way from humor to great FPS action, it's highly addictive and the fact that items drop and it's not P2W boggles my mind.
Pros:
-It's humorous ranging from the things the character's say all the way to how the game plays itself out.
-The community is actually pretty nice, not to much raging going on, makes the perfect, calm-relaxing enviroment to play the game.
-The graphics are exquisite to be an animated game, it's like playing an FPS anime game, love it.
-The diversity and the fact that their can be various classes on one side, ex all spies, make it fun and interesting.
Cons:
-The fact that weapons give you buffs, make it eventually harder to play against higher level people.
-There is no ranking system making the game kind of unfair, cause anyone can be paired with anyone.
I actually have little cons for this game, it's just that good, I honestly loved it, from my personal opinion I would most likely add more classes, due to the fact that they have so many players, adding more characters would be better then just adding items all the time, but hey, my opinion.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Just a heads up, if you care about the legitimacy of my opinion I generally end up in the top 3 of players for each game. I've also clocked at least 800 hours into it.
This game is now a huge neglected piece of garbage. The addition of weapons that gave you free crits (Charge N Targe, phlog, ect.) for doing little to no work makes this game SCREAM noob friendly. There's no point of grinding to get better because there's a weapon for every class that counteracts ANY amount of training you could possibly do.
In the early days the game made a lot of sense, there were not many weapon addons to change the dynamic flow of characters and each class was simple. This balance brought a VERY high skill curve as a result of mastery of a class requirement to be good.
What you find now is a game flooded with players who are way too young to be online in the first place constantly demanding easy kills via higher powered weapons. The entitled younger generation has successfully converted this game into a hold forward COD emulator. (Hence the expression M1+W Pyro)
90% of servers have random crits enabled, which makes balance litterally impossible due to the fact that on top of the random crits they also offer you weapons that give you free crits right out of spawn just for right clicking.
But wait, it gets worse. This game has ONLY survived through the years because it runs off of human addiction. Not because it's fun, but gambling. The only way to get the most demanded items is to SPEND MONEY on keys to open boxes you find as you play. These boxes have a 1% of dropping an item that doesn't even improve your characters ability, it just makes your accessories have shiny particles around it.
I kid you not, this is the ONLY thing about this game that keeps people playing. It's legalized gambling for bratty frag entitled children who find forced meme's to be the greatest invention on the planet earth (so expect to see a lenny face every 5 seconds in the chat window, because one kill to these kids is practically ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic.) Expect to hear yelling from parents and constant moans of entitlement on EVERY server with at least 5 people in it.
I feel like I've wasted a LOT of time in my life hoping this game would return to it's former glory. But just like how the Halo franchise went, the people behind the curtain don't care about quality of play, but monetary extortion of our youth via addictive freemium gambling. (See the new episode of south park on Freemium Gaming to see a more detailed explanation of how games like this work.)
If you're looking for something fun and entertaining, you'd have a better chance with Netflix or a walk in your local park than this game.

This game is fascinating. I remember I tried playing it a year ago but I sucked♥♥♥♥♥ so I gave up on it, even though I played for about fifteen minutes. I tried it again this year, because I read the reviews and everyone seemed so fascinated, claiming the game ruined your life because it completely consumed you, some people going as far as saying that something as simple as the whole hats deal was addictive. I'd laugh it off, thinking "It can't be that bad".
After almost two months of playing, I can confirm; yeah, it's that bad. Perhaps worse.
The first few weeks the liking was soft, I liked the game, the "Meet the" videos were amusing and really drew me to the game, but I was extremely bad at first, "15 kills, 10 deaths" type of bad. I dominated just one player every two rounds; and I even got really excited when I got a revenge (Jesus, it's embarrassing to admit). That's how bad, and even n00by I was. I was coming back to online PC gaming after six years of sticking to console, so that wasn't helping. But then, when I started playing a little bit more... when it was a domination after domination, when I'd become friends with my pocket Medics or the people I was a pocket Medic to... Life changed. This game literally consumed me. I wanted to use a portion of my birthday money to buy myself some cosmetics *just* for my Medic, make him beautiful ya'kno, and I ended up spending all of it in cosmetics for many of the classes. I'd stay up extremely late at night playing, sleep little, to then wake up early to play again. Now it's gotten to the point in which I've played 12 hours straight of TF2 with little rest in-between, two days ago it was *fourteen* hours. With a lot of effort I got up my♥♥♥♥♥♥to work out today just to not be too sedentary, and it was exasperating because I wanted to play. The game's just special like that, ya'know? It's fun. It's unique, creative. And I love the small details like the angry faces the classes make when they're shooting or fighting, the happy faces on the partner-taunts, the faces of agony when they're with low health; details like that make it special. And it's just generally very addictive.
My point? This game is f*cking terrible. I don't give a cr*p if it's free, DON'T INSTALL IT. IT WILL CONSUME YOU AND RUIN YOU. F*CKING RUN. RUN WHILE YOU STILL CAN!!!!!!!! (I still recommend it, though. Just because you'll have a lot of fun)
Now, if you'll excuse me, I'll get back to playing.

First of all: This is a very good game & free to play, so: Just download it and try it, it´s worth.
I played this game nearly 500 hours, so i know, what i´m talking about.
Now some Details:
For me it´s important that F2P Games are not pay-to-win, because some of the people will put more and more money into it and get greater and better weapons which a normal player never can reach.
TF2 do this great: You could get every weapon dropped, and with these you could craft other weapons you want; ALL FOR FREE!
If you want, you could open cases with weapons inside, to get faster new weapons, but this is ok, because you could achieve everything ingame through playing the game.
The game has 9 player classes and you need all of them in your team, every class has her own advantages and disadvantages. Every Player will have his own favorite class and these he doesn´t like, but thats ok.
The weapons have different effects, advantages and disadvantages but nothing over powered, it´s balanced.
Gamemodes are averege: Tdm, ctf and cp are examples.
To conclude: It´s a very nice and funny game, but after a so long playtime it becomes kind of monotonous.
I know, VALVE is adding new content, feautures and items, but i want to keep the playing experience that i recognize from the past, as i was 14 years old.
If you never played this game and like shooters, give it a try, download these 10 GB and have a look at a glorious game that changed my childhood.

Game Grade:  A-
Shorthand Review:  Sit back and relax as you blow through your foes with an arsenal of comedy.  What more can you want from a free game?
Detailed Review:
Team Fortress 2, or TF2, is a wonderfully comical first person shooter.  The game does not focus on graphics or realism by any means (unless beating down your foes with a lollypop is normal for you).  TF2 is quite enjoyable from a comical standpoint which is outstandingly hilarious.  Something else you can enjoy in the game is the balanced game play (will be addressed later in the review).  The replay value of TF2 is rather high due to the countless modded servers and new equipment you can unlock.  The game is very fun and you can rest knowing that the download time was well worth it (seeing its a free game the only thing spent is time).
Team Fortress has a very unique and comical first person shooter aspect to it.  The fighting in the game is all based off of comedy.  Weapons can range from a smelly fish to an actual hand cannon.  Like weapons, the equipment is quite entertaining.  For all of you that like first person shooters, you shouldn't be afraid of this loss in realism.  There are still satisfying damage, accuracy, and unlocking systems that are involved.  This will keep you coming back to the game for newer and better weapons and/or equipment.  In all, combat is fun and takes skill to master the battlefield.
I think everyone can agree many games with potential are ruined by a pay-to-win system.  This is not true for TF2.  Every weapon and piece of equipment can be unlocked randomly throughout the game.  You can, however, pay to get something quicker.  Also, you are given crates which can be unlocked with a purchased key but again all the stuff can be earned.  Some things are harder to get than others so don't expect to get all the great equipment right off the bat.  To sum it all up, combat is fair and balanced.
As in most games, people create modded servers.  These modded servers are, for the most part, fair and do not kill the game.  These servers tend to have the most people because they are very enjoyable.  While we are on the topic of players, I would like to address the player base.  Unfortunately, there are some immature people on the mic.  You can avoid this problem by muting them and falling back into the focus of the game play.  Other than that, the community is still active and rather fun to play with.
All in all, Team Fortress 2 is worth a try.  It is a great game you can play with friends and work forever on getting all the achievements.  If you are active in the Steam market, items can be traded and sold with ease.  I can promise you that you won't regret downloading this game.

For me it´s important that F2P Games are not pay-to-win, because some of the people will put more and more money into it and get greater and better weapons which a normal player never can reach.
TF2 do this great: You could get every weapon dropped, and with these you could craft other weapons you want; ALL FOR FREE!
If you want, you could open cases with weapons inside, to get faster new weapons, but this is ok, because you could achieve everything ingame through playing the game.
The game has 9 player classes and you need all of them in your team, every class has her own advantages and disadvantages. Every Player will have his own favorite class and these he doesn´t like, but thats ok.
The weapons have different effects, advantages and disadvantages but nothing over powered, it´s balanced.
Gamemodes are averege: Tdm, ctf and cp are examples.
To conclude: It´s a very nice and funny game, but after a so long playtime it becomes kind of monotonous.
I know, VALVE is adding new content, feautures and items, but i want to keep the playing experience that i recognize from the past, as i was 14 years old.

I couldnt decide what to write in this review , so im gonna share with you guys my favorite apple pie recipe Enjoy! :
Pastry
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon salt
2/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons shortening
4 to 6 tablespoons cold water
Filling
1/3 to 1/2 cup sugar
1/4 cup all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
1/8 teaspoon salt
8 cups thinly sliced peeled tart apples (8 medium)
2 tablespoons butter or margarine
1) In medium bowl, mix 2 cups flour and 1 teaspoon salt. Cut in shortening, using pastry blender (or pulling 2 table knives through ingredients in opposite directions), until particles are size of small peas. Sprinkle with cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing with fork until all flour is moistened and pastry almost cleans side of bowl (1 to 2 teaspoons more water can be added if necessary).
2) Gather pastry into a ball. Divide in half; shape into 2 flattened rounds on lightly floured surface. Wrap in plastic wrap; refrigerate about 45 minutes or until dough is firm and cold, yet pliable. This allows the shortening to become slightly firm, which helps make the baked pastry more flaky. If refrigerated longer, let pastry soften slightly before rolling.
3) Heat oven to 425°F. With floured rolling pin, roll one pastry round into round 2 inches larger than upside-down 9-inch glass pie plate. Fold pastry into fourths; place in pie plate. Unfold and ease into plate, pressing firmly against bottom and side.
4) In large bowl, mix sugar, 1/4 cup flour, the cinnamon, nutmeg and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Stir in apples until well mixed. Spoon into pastry-lined pie plate. Cut butter into small pieces; sprinkle over filling. Trim overhanging edge of pastry 1/2 inch from rim of plate.
5) Roll other round of pastry into 10-inch round. Fold into fourths and cut slits so steam can escape. Unfold top pastry over filling; trim overhanging edge 1 inch from rim of plate. Fold and roll top edge under lower edge, pressing on rim to seal; flute as desired. Cover edge with 2- to 3-inch strip of foil to prevent excessive browning.
6) Bake 40 to 50 minutes or until crust is brown and juice begins to bubble through slits in crust, removing foil for last 15 minutes of baking. Serve warm if desired.

This is the Steam Game. When I ask people if they have a Steam profile, I say 'Do you play TF2?' This game could be considered one of the first MOBAs. With nine classes, hundreds of weapons, and nearly infinate 'builds,' what's not to love? This can support nigh every play style, from support (medic) to ADC (heavy/pyro) , from 'jungling' (spies) to sniping (...sniper!). No one class is supreme, and some need help from the other classes. A medic alone is easy prey. A solo heavy can hold his own. But a heavy/medic combo is something to behold definately. There are classes that can go with out help, but that's not as fun as a surge done with six close friends firing bullets, rockets, grenades, fire, and syringes into every one who crosses your path. In my oppinion, TF2 plays as intense as you want. When I started out, I was just playing around with the engineer, because I liked his hat. And now, I'm a pretty good Engi!
Postscript: A lot of the complaints are over 'ducks,' and allow me to try and explain what that means. Once upon a time, I was in a server. And every so often you would see a duck on the ground. Oh and we would scramble to get them! I did forget what they did, but I didn't think they were annoying, and I havn't found any since. So try it out, it's free!

Let me tell you a story...
Long ago, in 2011, a small child quietly plays Halo 3 in his living room. At this point in time, he rarely uses his computer, and when he does he doesn't play games. The child loved collecting things in Halo, but never embraced this and played other games which had these features.
A year passes and things don't change much, But Halo 4 releases that year. Eventually, the child did get it, along with CoD BO1 + 2 a while after. He loves both of these games, and he cares about making himself look cooler in both. He leveled up in CoD so he could put a silly tag on his gun, so he could make it look how he desired.
He also found The Orange Box this year. He had hear a little of the games included, and wanted to have it. He played a little of Portal, a little of Half Life, and a little of Team Fortress 2. He didn't play it much, but it was the best game buy of his life. He looked up TF2 and TOB in general, and discovered that the PC edition was much better.
The year is 2014 at this point, and the child boots up Steam for the first time. Instantly sorting out his profile, he goes to TF2 and hits install. After a short wait and a click, the game is open. It lags on the title screen. The child is dissapointed, but he still plays on. He gets his first hat here, on his least played class: Pyro. He upgrades to a new computer sooner or later, and it can run TF2 much better. He rarely touches the console anymore, not enjoying the games he finds there.
He complains about some updates and how W+M1 takes no skill, but the time is 2016 and he still plays TF2 sometimes, but not as often. He mainly watches videos or chats with his friends these days. He picks up TF2 somewhere around mid-late 2016. He loves the game all over again.
TL;DR - This game changed my tastes in all games, and I still play it today after around 3 years.
And yes, I'm still a child. 10/10

This is the Steam Game. When I ask people if they have a Steam profile, I say 'Do you play TF2?' This game could be considered one of the first MOBAs. With nine classes, hundreds of weapons, and nearly infinate 'builds,' what's not to love? This can support nigh every play style, from support (medic) to ADC (heavy/pyro) , from 'jungling' (spies) to sniping (...sniper!). No one class is supreme, and some need help from the other classes. A medic alone is easy prey. A solo heavy can hold his own. But a heavy/medic combo is something to behold definately. There are classes that can go with out help, but that's not as fun as a surge done with six close friends firing bullets, rockets, grenades, fire, and syringes into every one who crosses your path. In my oppinion, TF2 plays as intense as you want. When I started out, I was just playing around with the engineer, because I liked his hat. And now, I'm a pretty good Engi!
Postscript: A lot of the complaints are over 'ducks,' and allow me to try and explain what that means. Once upon a time, I was in a server. And every so often you would see a duck on the ground. Oh and we would scramble to get them! I did forget what they did, but I didn't think they were annoying, and I havn't found any since. So try it out, it's free!

I doubt anybody really needs to be told why to try Team Fortress 2, especially with its reputation and lack of a price tag, but I suppose I should throw my 2 cents in anyway.
Team Fortress 2 is a fun game that gives you fun options in how you want to play. You get 9 classes to toy with, each having an interesting personality and a unique playstyle. Then, as you play, you'll come across weapons that let you experiment within each class's playstyle. The more you play, the more stuff you amass, and the more options you'll have at your disposal. If you haven't already, take a dip into the world of Team Fortress 2. You're almost guaranteed to find something you like!

One of the best free-to-play models on Steam. There are better, but this is definitely a great example.
You can either stay "F2P", and receive weapons and crates as drops.
Or, you can buy anything from the "Mann Co. Store", and receive Premium, which gives you a free hat in the process, depending on whether you're buying it from in-game, or on the online store.
It has multiple playstyles, varying from class to class and weapon to weapon. Default weapons for the Scout provide a different playstyle to one for example a Force-A-Nature, Bonk and Sandman Scout.
Depending on your style of humour, the Mercenaries can be funny, morbid(ly obese) or sarcastic. They each have their own personality (which are magnified by "SFM" (Source Film Maker) videos), which brings out the 'reality' of the characters.
Also, free content updates with a huge community and amazing videos used with film software? That's right, you get all of that.
All in all, it's definitely a game worth trying. If you like it, you can continue playing, maybe eventually even help out a little bit by contributing money and guides to the developers and community (respectively). If not, feel free to uninstall the game and bide your time with some other game. Steam (and I) are not forcing you to play it.
I hope you enjoy the game or have already enjoyed it.

Uncomprehensively an amazing game!
Gameplay takes a while to get used too, i.e. Rocket jumping, the game is generally unique providing funny and unrealistic physics that everyone just gets used too!
The game provides so much ways of playing it, so its not all about being a tryhard and killing EVERYONE in plain sight.
The TF2 community offers amazing CUSTOM gamemodes like:
- VS Saxton Hale
- Deathrun
- Smash Fortress
- Pubs
- and MANY more!
Though its not just the community that makes this game awesome, its the game itself and the Developers (Praise Robin Walker!) who makes this game so enjoyable!
The game is nicely frequently updated with bug fixes, amazing content like updates including new weapons, balance changes and MOST Importantly... Hats, whats TF2 without them!?
This game is for both casual people who just enjoy a more relaxed FPS featuring taunts, by taunts that are so unique you can sit down on a lovely chair with an umbrella having a nice sip of beer, or become epic sax guy with a.. you guessed it! A saxophone!
Team Fortress 2 in basic is a team based First Person Shooter, that features 9 classes, so you have your pick on which one you prefer.
They are in order
-Scout (Offensive Class)
-Soldier (Offensive Class)
-Pyro (Offensive Class)
-Demoman (Defensive Class)
-Heavy (Most Iconic Russian, Defensive Class)
-Engineer (Defensive Class)
-Medic (Support Class)
-Sniper (Support Class)
-Spy (Support Class)
Thats a large class selection that gently suits everyones type of playstyle!
and the game has got no "Pay to Win" feel, you can get weapon drops just by playing the game! but you can always pay a bit of money if you feel the need to enhance your experience of the game.
Overall TF2 is a VERY addictive, fun, more laidback FPS that provides competitive and casual gameplay and provides one of the most unique gameplay and experiences out there in the gaming industry!
So what are you waiting for? Hop right in to the fun!
I highly recommend this game for anyone, Competitive player or not.

You can play this mode for free but not get any items but you can buy a ticket for $2.99 and then you will get a weapon or a hat (most likey weapon). I would just play for free. The class diversity is good and each of the nine classes have a story and are from different countries to give them there accents. Some game modes are realy fun to play like atack and defend and payload race. I just wish valve would stop working on TF2 and start working on Half life 3. What can I say about Team Fortress 2 that hasn't been by most fans and gamers?  A few words to describe it is fun, competitive, interactive, exciting, and very co-operative. Let’s start with objective of the game shall we. The entire plot revolves around having two teams (the blue team and red team)fighting it off in different game modes such as arena, capture the flag, control point, king of the hill, payload, man vs machine, and other types. This game even takes the game mode of prop hunt straight out Garry’s Mod (thank you Valve) .To actually get the entire story plot though, they're found in the comic books from the official site. Of course this game has no single player mode, so everything pretty much derives from the online multiplayer.
The gameplay is pretty much a easy to control first person shooter. You have the option to select through 9 different choices of character roaster with expert assassins with their own unique skills. There's the ever so cocky scout, the American patriot who never went to war solider, the mysterious yet psychotic pyro, the drunk Irish demo man, the Russian heavy, the laid back engineer, the brilliant medic, the sharp shooting sniper, and the infamous spy. For a game that doesn't have much story, all these guys have a lot of character and likeness to them. If you haven't seen it, though I guess no one wouldn't, I'd recommend watching the Meet the videos. What I enjoy about the art style is that both the player models and background have that 20th century look to them, it’s just so appealing. Oh, and don’t worry, there a lot of great maps to choose through the game, not including all the other maps from all the other maps made from the steam workshop. That’s another thing to give thanks; the tf2 community are always providing many updates to the game while uploading many new skins, weapons, clothing’s, taunts, and so,so,so many hats to buy from. Just for that, it definitely has a lot of re-playability to get new items to trade with.
Overall I can say that this game is worth everything it gives and possible more. Hell, it’s a free to play game, so there’s no excuse to not have this game in you game list. My only nitpick would be the amount of crates given to you even though you’re not really interested in opening them. Plus, this game came out in Steam in 2007, and now it’s the year 2015, so it definitely has been showing its age. You have the option to sell them, but likelihood of people buying them are pretty slim, unless they’re rare crates. Like I also said, this game depends majorly on online multiplayer, so part of the fun will really depend on the kinds of people you going up against (probably try-hards) Other than that it’s fine. My final verdict for this game is a solid 8.5/10. It has a few problems to it, but nothing really noticeable compared what this this really shines through. You can definitely tell there was a lot hard work the developers and the community put into this game. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who simply enjoys a competitive gunfight, or has a fine addiction to hat collecting. Let’s all expect great things to come later on in the future for the next installment of the team fortress series. Actually, let’s hope there will be an actually story plot for single or co-op campaign. Seriously! All these guys are hilarious, and after watching their recent video “Expiration Date” on YouTube, you know that they could pull something like this off (or possible let people create custom stories on the steam workshop, that works too *winkwink*).  But in the meantime, this is Szeth Silverwolf, and my last words to ends this thing off are “"I'm gonna turn ya into colored rain!"

[Complete Review Overhaul] The date is November 27th, 2017, an entire month after the Jungle Inferno Update launched, of which I believed revived TF2 forever. Before my overhaul, I stated I migrated over to OverWatch, and that things changed. Well, things changed again, and I have almost entirely ditched OverWatch. I have NO idea why I left TF2 like I did, in such an unforgiving and doubtful manner. Here's why I think TF2 is indeed Timeless.
[Jungle Inferno] The Jungle Update (Pyro Update) finally released this October, and honestly, it's one of the most positive updates and one of the most largest updates this game has ever had, besides the Uber update or Mannconomy, Pyromania, etc. They fixed Pyro's flame mojo (althought to compensate for this, they added additional damage for holding down m1 on a target, which I dont really care about), as well as adding in 4 new weapons for the Pyro to choose from, along with a META breaking side-grade LunchBox item for Heavy. Casual was Semi-Fixed, and as far as I can tell, ValvE Comp has been untouched since Meet your Match. An entire campaign was released, involving skin rewards, and several new maps to choose from. War Paints were also introduced, which are gun skins, but are appliable to a majority of the weapons in game. War paints can also be unusual, which I still believe can ♥♥♥♥ with the unusual weapons economy, since people can now craft some of the most expensive unusual weapons in the game at their own will, resulting in mass price drops of various items, which I predict that unusual weapons will end up like Earbuds one day, and completely get killed off in terms of price and value(You rarely see anyone with buds these days. Hell, some people I've met still count prices in buds over keys). Weapons like the Bison have been revived, and buffs and nerfs for all around, molding the meta anew as well as balancing the pyro, although I still believe he is still a mindless class that takes no thought whatsoever to be good at. More cosmetics, that as far as I can tell, arent really all that sought after. But overall, Jungle Inferno was a success and revived TF2 for years to come.
[TIMELESS] Yes, I said Timeless. I know what it means, trust me. What makes TF2 Timeless? Not only it's mechanics, but its artstyle, and dedication. Although TF2 failed HARD at marketing itself as a competitive shooter, trust me, it has the potential. The Tutorial sucks, so players adapt and evolve in a way that disregards any recognization of the Tutorial, and in my opinion, shapes more independent thought and gameplay choice. TF2s♥♥♥♥♥♥Tutorial (most of the time) sifts out all the bad players that arent willing to learn, and put dedication into learning this game, and welcomes players who arent afraid to run off the rails and kick♥♥♥♥♥their OWN way. People complain that TF2 needs a system to tell new players if they need power classes or not, but I say left them ♥♥♥♥ing learn on their own. It's a teambased shooter where your choices matter how the game goes, and if they are too dumb to realise the team needs a med without a bright blinking light telling them what to do and how to think, then I dont know what will...There is a reason why players like B4nny exist, and its because he adapted and put dedication into the game. Thousands of hours worth of work that ended up making him one of the most well known players in the entire community, as well as a spot on one of the most advanced teams in the Comp scene, FroyoTech. Im sorry, but the lack of a Tutorial is mainly what battle hardened most of the community. It's that sense of "I'll do it myself" and "♥♥♥♥ it".
The artstyle(well, the old artstyle atleast) is a mix of cartoonish lunacy and muddiness and grime. On one hand, you have bright, colorful, and emotion-filled characters with their own personalities and walks of life and humor, whilst at the same time, they are fighting in dirty, brash, rough, and muted environments, with blood flying everywhere and pure chaos shooting off like guns in the distance. The concept art for TF2 also lead to the idea of a more brash environment, with broken and taped together guns and crude bludgening tools for melees. This is what also makes TF2 unique. It doesnt stick to one artstyle at a time ,and mixes two, if not 3 artstyles, and combines them into one beautifully done masterpiece, that after 10 WHOLE YEARS of existence, has still managed to keep afloat and with a healthy community for an entire DECADE. Very little games ever reach the 10 year mark. This to me is the true sign of timelessness. There are games like OverWatch, which to me, will never reach year 10, simply because it feels like the same. old. shooter. One artstyle, 100% none-stop edgy plotline, and SOMEHOW manages to outdo DooM 2016 at the GOTY award. Although, yes, TF2 is home to edgy players too, but we actually take advantage of that, and turn them into memes and jokes. 10 years and still kicking, baby. Ladies and Gentlemen, welcome to one of the most timeless games in existence: Team Fortress 2!

What can I say about Team Fortress 2 that hasn't been by most fans and gamers?  A few words to describe it is fun, competitive, interactive, exciting, and very co-operative. Let’s start with objective of the game shall we. The entire plot revolves around having two teams (the blue team and red team)fighting it off in different game modes such as arena, capture the flag, control point, king of the hill, payload, man vs machine, and other types. This game even takes the game mode of prop hunt straight out Garry’s Mod (thank you Valve) .To actually get the entire story plot though, they're found in the comic books from the official site. Of course this game has no single player mode, so everything pretty much derives from the online multiplayer.
The gameplay is pretty much a easy to control first person shooter. You have the option to select through 9 different choices of character roaster with expert assassins with their own unique skills. There's the ever so cocky scout, the American patriot who never went to war solider, the mysterious yet psychotic pyro, the drunk Irish demo man, the Russian heavy, the laid back engineer, the brilliant medic, the sharp shooting sniper, and the infamous spy. For a game that doesn't have much story, all these guys have a lot of character and likeness to them. If you haven't seen it, though I guess no one wouldn't, I'd recommend watching the Meet the videos. What I enjoy about the art style is that both the player models and background have that 20th century look to them, it’s just so appealing. Oh, and don’t worry, there a lot of great maps to choose through the game, not including all the other maps from all the other maps made from the steam workshop. That’s another thing to give thanks; the tf2 community are always providing many updates to the game while uploading many new skins, weapons, clothing’s, taunts, and so,so,so many hats to buy from. Just for that, it definitely has a lot of re-playability to get new items to trade with.
Overall I can say that this game is worth everything it gives and possible more. Hell, it’s a free to play game, so there’s no excuse to not have this game in you game list. My only nitpick would be the amount of crates given to you even though you’re not really interested in opening them. Plus, this game came out in Steam in 2007, and now it’s the year 2015, so it definitely has been showing its age. You have the option to sell them, but likelihood of people buying them are pretty slim, unless they’re rare crates. Like I also said, this game depends majorly on online multiplayer, so part of the fun will really depend on the kinds of people you going up against (probably try-hards) Other than that it’s fine. My final verdict for this game is a solid 8.5/10. It has a few problems to it, but nothing really noticeable compared what this this really shines through. You can definitely tell there was a lot hard work the developers and the community put into this game. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who simply enjoys a competitive gunfight, or has a fine addiction to hat collecting. Let’s all expect great things to come later on in the future for the next installment of the team fortress series. Actually, let’s hope there will be an actually story plot for single or co-op campaign. Seriously! All these guys are hilarious, and after watching their recent video “Expiration Date” on YouTube, you know that they could pull something like this off (or possible let people create custom stories on the steam workshop, that works too *winkwink*).  But in the meantime, this is Szeth Silverwolf, and my last words to ends this thing off are “"I'm gonna turn ya into colored rain!"

[Complete Review Overhaul] The date is November 27th, 2017, an entire month after the Jungle Inferno Update launched, of which I believed revived TF2 forever. Before my overhaul, I stated I migrated over to OverWatch, and that things changed. Well, things changed again, and I have almost entirely ditched OverWatch. I have NO idea why I left TF2 like I did, in such an unforgiving and doubtful manner. Here's why I think TF2 is indeed Timeless.
[Jungle Inferno] The Jungle Update (Pyro Update) finally released this October, and honestly, it's one of the most positive updates and one of the most largest updates this game has ever had, besides the Uber update or Mannconomy, Pyromania, etc. They fixed Pyro's flame mojo (althought to compensate for this, they added additional damage for holding down m1 on a target, which I dont really care about), as well as adding in 4 new weapons for the Pyro to choose from, along with a META breaking side-grade LunchBox item for Heavy. Casual was Semi-Fixed, and as far as I can tell, ValvE Comp has been untouched since Meet your Match. An entire campaign was released, involving skin rewards, and several new maps to choose from. War Paints were also introduced, which are gun skins, but are appliable to a majority of the weapons in game. War paints can also be unusual, which I still believe can ♥♥♥♥ with the unusual weapons economy, since people can now craft some of the most expensive unusual weapons in the game at their own will, resulting in mass price drops of various items, which I predict that unusual weapons will end up like Earbuds one day, and completely get killed off in terms of price and value(You rarely see anyone with buds these days. Hell, some people I've met still count prices in buds over keys). Weapons like the Bison have been revived, and buffs and nerfs for all around, molding the meta anew as well as balancing the pyro, although I still believe he is still a mindless class that takes no thought whatsoever to be good at. More cosmetics, that as far as I can tell, arent really all that sought after. But overall, Jungle Inferno was a success and revived TF2 for years to come.
[TIMELESS] Yes, I said Timeless. I know what it means, trust me. What makes TF2 Timeless? Not only it's mechanics, but its artstyle, and dedication. Although TF2 failed HARD at marketing itself as a competitive shooter, trust me, it has the potential. The Tutorial sucks, so players adapt and evolve in a way that disregards any recognization of the Tutorial, and in my opinion, shapes more independent thought and gameplay choice. TF2s♥♥♥♥♥♥Tutorial (most of the time) sifts out all the bad players that arent willing to learn, and put dedication into learning this game, and welcomes players who arent afraid to run off the rails and kick♥♥♥♥♥their OWN way. People complain that TF2 needs a system to tell new players if they need power classes or not, but I say left them ♥♥♥♥ing learn on their own. It's a teambased shooter where your choices matter how the game goes, and if they are too dumb to realise the team needs a med without a bright blinking light telling them what to do and how to think, then I dont know what will...There is a reason why players like B4nny exist, and its because he adapted and put dedication into the game. Thousands of hours worth of work that ended up making him one of the most well known players in the entire community, as well as a spot on one of the most advanced teams in the Comp scene, FroyoTech. Im sorry, but the lack of a Tutorial is mainly what battle hardened most of the community. It's that sense of "I'll do it myself" and "♥♥♥♥ it".
The artstyle(well, the old artstyle atleast) is a mix of cartoonish lunacy and muddiness and grime. On one hand, you have bright, colorful, and emotion-filled characters with their own personalities and walks of life and humor, whilst at the same time, they are fighting in dirty, brash, rough, and muted environments, with blood flying everywhere and pure chaos shooting off like guns in the distance. The concept art for TF2 also lead to the idea of a more brash environment, with broken and taped together guns and crude bludgening tools for melees. This is what also makes TF2 unique. It doesnt stick to one artstyle at a time ,and mixes two, if not 3 artstyles, and combines them into one beautifully done masterpiece, that after 10 WHOLE YEARS of existence, has still managed to keep afloat and with a healthy community for an entire DECADE. Very little games ever reach the 10 year mark. This to me is the true sign of timelessness. There are games like OverWatch, which to me, will never reach year 10, simply because it feels like the same. old. shooter. One artstyle, 100% none-stop edgy plotline, and SOMEHOW manages to outdo DooM 2016 at the GOTY award. Although, yes, TF2 is home to edgy players too, but we actually take advantage of that, and turn them into memes and jokes. 10 years and still kicking, baby. Ladies and Gentlemen, welcome to one of the most timeless games in existence: Team Fortress 2!

TF2 was a good game and it still is, even to this day. Sure you can start complaining about the fact that there hasn't been any major update that brings in new content (That isn't the halloween and christmas updates because those are expected to come every year) for a while and the fact that people stated that Meet Your Match was bad because pubs were ruined overall, but I feel like that TF2 still has a lot of potential, even if it is almost 10 years old.
Valve isn't helping with the situation because the dev team for TF2 is too short for a game like this and we can't just expect the team to put out updates monthly. Would you prefer to get 1 update that added new game content every month and it ends up being extremely broken or get 1 update every once in a while that adds a lot more content than a monthy update and it's a lot more polished?
The truth is, we have to accept that we can't always get what we want and we just have to play with what we have at our disposal. However, people tend to switch to another multiplayer game that's popular like Overwatch because it gets a lot more attention, but you have to consider the fact that the dev team for Overwatch is a lot more larger than TF2 and Overwatch seems to be more popular right now. Sure, I can understand why you would make the switch and I really don't wish to create a flame war about it. We have more than enough people criticizing about Overwatch and I don't wanna be a part of it.
The community servers can keep a player entertained for a long while. We got gamemodes such as randomizer, x10, crits only, zombies, fortwars, minigames, and a lot more that's out there. Maybe you'll enjoy a pony server if that's your thing. Maybe you'll enjoy playing on a minecraft server. I dunno, the choice is completely up to you in picking what you fancy.
Overall, I think TF2 is still enjoyable to play and I hope that this year we can get new amazing content that will keep the players entertained for a good while. Until then, I'll keep enjoying the game that I have been playing for almost 5 years.

I'm VERY skeptical about Team Fortress 2 lately, as to its couple of updates recently. I mean the obvious here, what you'd think if you know a lot about TF2 and stay tuned about it. Yup. F'ing Gun Mettle and Tough Break. Valve ISN'T being original about monetization with it. That's for sure.
The game itself is good, yes. Very addicting, when the thought of obtaining 3 cosmetics for each class comes up, and trying to get what you consider the "best" looking ones. And then painting them. And then there's Stranges, Killstreaks, and so on. That's all rather original and all for me, since it was all before CSGO. And that's fine. BUT.
Adding frigging (emphasize FRIGGING) reskins for Stock weapons, that AREN'T Australiums or Festives, not to mention inspired by a certain other recent Multiplayer game made by Valve, is VERY unoriginal. Not just that either, it just shows how desperate Valve is for cash and whoever they hired for Marketing and such really isn't doing a good job. And before they (Valve, like they're gonna read this)
think I'm full of it, let me introduce a new, much more original idea for reskins of Stock weapons!
Chrome equivalent of Australium in the TF2 universe. This would probably mean buying Tour of Duty tickets, and that's actually MUCH better than something ripped out of another game MADE BY VALVE! Anyway, enough of that...
Yes, the gameplay is solid, even after all the new weapons that made the default weapons be dubbed "Stock". Yes, the game is good for F2Ps, I dunno why people cuss at them...oh right, because most of them wear gibuses and pyrovision goggles and ARE stupid. But if I were to be one, I wouldn't be so much like that, really. Or anyone good at the game.
Anyway, in conclusion, this game is good, but its only flaw is really annoying to the processing parts of my brain, how Gabe Newell could possibly step down TF2 so much as to draw its money the same way from a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT game. I never wanted this. TF2 was and IS so much more fun than Counter Strike (depending on one's mood anyway), and it just...deserved better. Community items are a great idea, it being acknowledged as the world's #1 Hat Simulator is also fantastic, new weapons with brand new models, Australiums...but CSGO-inspired reskins? That's just loow...But yeah, the rest is all good, and if you're reading this, you're most likely new to the game, so if you're interested in playing it, you should totally give it a try.
If you're not new, then...I dunno. It's just gone corrupt to me. Valve should listen to the old-timers and give us something ORIGINAL. Jesus.

This game is fun. Don't get me wrong. But it just.... lacks. When I first started playing it, I was happy. The training was interesting, and the matches were decent. The happy feeling didn't last. With very few gamemodes and not many lobbies that actually worked/had enough players in them for a good game, it started to slide downhill for me. The best thing about this game is the diverse class selection, which is pretty good. With nine different classes to choose from, being split equally into offensive, defensive, and support classes, the game is really fun at first. But then.... you start diverting to three of your favorite classes, then those get boring, and you don't want to use the other classes because you don't like the loadout they come with. On top of that, you can't really get new weapons and equipment unless you pay for it with real money, or 'find' it in game, which is random and unusual.
This game is fun for about five or six hours. After that, it just gets boring.

It's a really fun game and the fact that it is free is also really cool. Almost everything about this game is fantastic. The weapons, the characters and variety that fits almost any playstyle. The weapon drops are enough to keep you playing but not too much to over saturate the weapon market.
