That being said there is one ugly aspect. This game has one of the worst communities I have ever seen. Whether it is some annoying 12 yr old playing it cause his mom's comp can't run anything else, or some 18 yr+ try hard that yells at his team for the smallest mistake, you will find a lot of toxicity (spelling?). It is easy to avoid this community, which is why I still recommend this game, but if bad communities ruin a game for you, you may want to avoid this one (or any free game for that matter).
That being said, there still are people out there that genuinly want to help you learn the game. they exist on youtube and in the guides, so it is very easy to find what you are good at and then just mute people. I know I said if you hate bad communities to avoid this game, but seriously, it is free, so you might as well give it a go.

I don't even know where to start with this. This is only an FPS by definition as it stands out from all the rest.
After thousands of hours of playing this game, I can't praise it enough. The game play is fun, the characters are likeable, most maps are well-designed and enjoyable to play on, the game can be modded serverside (either minor tweaks or major game-changing overhauls) or played vanilla (which is amazing in its own right), and there's many class/weapon combinations to keep things interesting.
The game is entirely free but you may want to buy one item from the store to get premium so you can trade items (which you get randomly anyway), but it's only a dollar or something for the least expensive item. A small matter of convenience and cosmetic, really.
There are only two significant problems: most servers have random critical hits enabled (it's by default) that basically means you're screwed or dead simply because by random chance, you're gonna take 3x damage from a hit; the other major problem is that some weapons are unbalanced or unfun to play against, but it's not a huge problem in this game.
If you got a free night, check the game out. You may just be hooked for a long time. Easily the best game I've ever played and the one I've played most by far. And it's FREE.

It's a really fun game and the fact that it is free is also really cool. Almost everything about this game is fantastic. The weapons, the characters and variety that fits almost any playstyle. The weapon drops are enough to keep you playing but not too much to over saturate the weapon market. It has silly cosmetics and overall is a great game to get into for the casual or more dedicated player.
That being said there is one ugly aspect. This game has one of the worst communities I have ever seen. Whether it is some annoying 12 yr old playing it cause his mom's comp can't run anything else, or some 18 yr+ try hard that yells at his team for the smallest mistake, you will find a lot of toxicity (spelling?). It is easy to avoid this community, which is why I still recommend this game, but if bad communities ruin a game for you, you may want to avoid this one (or any free game for that matter).
That being said, there still are people out there that genuinly want to help you learn the game. they exist on youtube and in the guides, so it is very easy to find what you are good at and then just mute people. I know I said if you hate bad communities to avoid this game, but seriously, it is free, so you might as well give it a go.

I don't even know where to start with this. This is only an FPS by definition as it stands out from all the rest.
After thousands of hours of playing this game, I can't praise it enough. The game play is fun, the characters are likeable, most maps are well-designed and enjoyable to play on, the game can be modded serverside (either minor tweaks or major game-changing overhauls) or played vanilla (which is amazing in its own right), and there's many class/weapon combinations to keep things interesting.
The game is entirely free but you may want to buy one item from the store to get premium so you can trade items (which you get randomly anyway), but it's only a dollar or something for the least expensive item. A small matter of convenience and cosmetic, really.
There are only two significant problems: most servers have random critical hits enabled (it's by default) that basically means you're screwed or dead simply because by random chance, you're gonna take 3x damage from a hit; the other major problem is that some weapons are unbalanced or unfun to play against, but it's not a huge problem in this game.
If you got a free night, check the game out. You may just be hooked for a long time. Easily the best game I've ever played and the one I've played most by far. And it's FREE.

Whether it is some annoying 12 yr old playing it cause his mom's comp can't run anything else, or some 18 yr+ try hard that yells at his team for the smallest mistake, you will find a lot of toxicity (spelling?). It is easy to avoid this community, which is why I still recommend this game, but if bad communities ruin a game for you, you may want to avoid this one (or any free game for that matter).

I know I said if you hate bad communities to avoid this game, but seriously, it is free, so you might as well give it a go.

I don't even know where to start with this. This is only an FPS by definition as it stands out from all the rest.
After thousands of hours of playing this game, I can't praise it enough. The game play is fun, the characters are likeable, most maps are well-designed and enjoyable to play on, the game can be modded serverside (either minor tweaks or major game-changing overhauls) or played vanilla (which is amazing in its own right), and there's many class/weapon combinations to keep things interesting.
The game is entirely free but you may want to buy one item from the store to get premium so you can trade items (which you get randomly anyway), but it's only a dollar or something for the least expensive item. A small matter of convenience and cosmetic, really.
There are only two significant problems: most servers have random critical hits enabled (it's by default) that basically means you're screwed or dead simply because by random chance, you're gonna take 3x damage from a hit; the other major problem is that some weapons are unbalanced or unfun to play against, but it's not a huge problem in this game.
If you got a free night, check the game out. You may just be hooked for a long time. Easily the best game I've ever played and the one I've played most by far. And it's FREE.

Team Fortress 2 is a silly fps, but it is actually good for itself. The silliness makes the game really fun to play, since the characters are pretty charismatic and can be actually funny, making you laugh with their goofy way of acting in the game. It has a good amount of characters and all of them play really well. The game itself also plays well and you probably will have a lot of fun with it.
It does have some problems though, especially for new players. It can be pretty hard for new players to get into the game, since it already has a very established base of players that can utterly destroy you ingame. If you're a new player and is trying to get into the game, try looking for different servers that accept more the new players, and, also, play with Pyro, Demo or Medic, they are probably the ones that are easy to get into. The Engineer and the Soldier are the hardest.
Another fact is the weapons. Players who already are a part of the game usually have better weapons for each character, making them really deadlier than normal and can kill you easier. It can be anoying. But, remember, the more you play the more into the game you can get, improving your skills with it and getting some of these weapons.
These problems are specially harder for new players, but I assure you that, if you try and play it more, you will have some fun. The game can be frustrating, but it is, specially, about the fun, and not the skills, since, this one, you'll get if you try hard and play it a lot. Try it, it is worth it.

Team Fortress 2 is a silly fps, but it is actually good for itself. The silliness makes the game really fun to play, since the characters are pretty charismatic and can be actually funny, making you laugh with their goofy way of acting in the game. It has a good amount of characters and all of them play really well. The game itself also plays well and you probably will have a lot of fun with it.
It does have some problems though, especially for new players. It can be pretty hard for new players to get into the game, since it already has a very established base of players that can utterly destroy you ingame. If you're a new player and is trying to get into the game, try looking for different servers that accept more the new players, and, also, play with Pyro, Demo or Medic, they are probably the ones that are easy to get into. The Engineer and the Soldier are the hardest.
Another fact is the weapons. Players who already are a part of the game usually have better weapons for each character, making them really deadlier than normal and can kill you easier. It can be anoying. But, remember, the more you play the more into the game you can get, improving your skills with it and getting some of these weapons.
These problems are specially harder for new players, but I assure you that, if you try and play it more, you will have some fun. The game can be frustrating, but it is, specially, about the fun, and not the skills, since, this one, you'll get if you try hard and play it a lot. Try it, it is worth it.

If anyone gets hungry while playing Team Fortress 2, here is the recipe to make suger cookies:
Ingredients
3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon baking powder
16 tablespoons (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
1 cup sugar
1/4 teaspoon salt
2 large eggs, lightly beaten
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
Icing, additional granulated or decorating sugar and candies, optional
Preparation
1. Sift flour with baking powder. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer on medium-high speed, beat butter, sugar and salt until light, about 3 minutes. Beat in eggs and vanilla. Reduce mixer speed to low; beat in flour mixture just until combined, scraping down sides of bowl as needed.
2. Turn dough out onto a floured work surface; cut in half. Pat each half into a 1-inch-thick disk. (Alternatively, form disks into 2 or 3 11/2- to 2-inch-thick logs.) Wrap in plastic; chill for 1 hour or up to 2 days.
3. Place racks in upper and lower thirds of oven and preheat to 375°F. Line 2 large baking sheets with parchment. Roll out 1 disk on a lightly floured surface to 1/4-inch thickness. Use cookie cutters to form desired shapes. (If you've formed logs, cut into 1/4-inch-thick slices.)
4. Using a small metal spatula, carefully transfer cookies to lined baking sheets, spacing about 2 inches apart. Sprinkle tops with sugar, if desired. Chill for 10 minutes. Bake until lightly browned around edges and firm in center, 12 to 15 minutes, rotating sheets halfway through. Let cookies cool on sheets on wire racks for 5 minutes, then transfer cookies to wire cooling racks to cool completely.
5. Repeat with remaining dough, rerolling scraps to use up as much as possible. Decorate cooled cookies with icing, decorating sugar and candies, if desired.
Pistachio-Cranberry Cookies: Pulse 1/2 cup unsalted pistachios and 1 cup dried cranberries with 1 Tbsp. of the flour in a food processor to finely chop. Add to dough with rest of flour. Prepare cookies as recipe directs.
Peppermint Cookies: Substitute 1 1/2 tsp. mint extract for vanilla. Grind 20 small peppermint candies in a food processor (you should have about 1/2 cup). Add to dough with flour mixture. Prepare cookies as recipe directs, omitting optional sugar topping. Cool completely. Dip each cookie halfway into 8 oz. melted dark chocolate. Sprinkle with additional crushed mints, if desired. Chill until chocolate has hardened. Bring cookies to room temperature before serving.

If anyone gets hungry while playing Team Fortress 2, here is the recipe to make suger cookies:
Ingredients
3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon baking powder
16 tablespoons (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
1 cup sugar
1/4 teaspoon salt
2 large eggs, lightly beaten
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
Icing, additional granulated or decorating sugar and candies, optional
Preparation
1. Sift flour with baking powder. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer on medium-high speed, beat butter, sugar and salt until light, about 3 minutes. Beat in eggs and vanilla. Reduce mixer speed to low; beat in flour mixture just until combined, scraping down sides of bowl as needed.
2. Turn dough out onto a floured work surface; cut in half. Pat each half into a 1-inch-thick disk. (Alternatively, form disks into 2 or 3 11/2- to 2-inch-thick logs.) Wrap in plastic; chill for 1 hour or up to 2 days.
3. Place racks in upper and lower thirds of oven and preheat to 375°F. Line 2 large baking sheets with parchment. Roll out 1 disk on a lightly floured surface to 1/4-inch thickness. Use cookie cutters to form desired shapes. (If you've formed logs, cut into 1/4-inch-thick slices.)
4. Using a small metal spatula, carefully transfer cookies to lined baking sheets, spacing about 2 inches apart. Sprinkle tops with sugar, if desired. Chill for 10 minutes. Bake until lightly browned around edges and firm in center, 12 to 15 minutes, rotating sheets halfway through. Let cookies cool on sheets on wire racks for 5 minutes, then transfer cookies to wire cooling racks to cool completely.
5. Repeat with remaining dough, rerolling scraps to use up as much as possible. Decorate cooled cookies with icing, decorating sugar and candies, if desired.
Pistachio-Cranberry Cookies: Pulse 1/2 cup unsalted pistachios and 1 cup dried cranberries with 1 Tbsp. of the flour in a food processor to finely chop. Add to dough with rest of flour. Prepare cookies as recipe directs.
Peppermint Cookies: Substitute 1 1/2 tsp. mint extract for vanilla. Grind 20 small peppermint candies in a food processor (you should have about 1/2 cup). Add to dough with flour mixture. Prepare cookies as recipe directs, omitting optional sugar topping. Cool completely. Dip each cookie halfway into 8 oz. melted dark chocolate. Sprinkle with additional crushed mints, if desired. Chill until chocolate has hardened. Bring cookies to room temperature before serving.

I have around 1500 hours, but I am a decent trader and have come pretty far into trading. What I mainly want to review is the stuff I know about: Competitive and Trading. Perhaps the most well-known aspects of the game, yet the most fluctuated (in terms of rating or liking).
Trading- unless you are extremely experienced- revolves around two things: Luck, and Patience. Although you do need some other skills (Price checking, negotiation etc.), you hardly ever get good deals unless you are trading with some 10 year-old whose mother spent well-earned money on a virtual  game. Sometimes I do get good deals (good in TF2 trading terms means profit) on some decently experienced players, but it is rare.( For Me!)
From the TF2 servers I've played on competitive can be good, bad, or of course just normal. Why? Let me try as hard as I can to explain the madness than ensues in playing this game.
Another Source engine shooter boggles us by the fact that it's not a Call of Duty or Battelfield Rip-off, but it sells.
Now, dont get confused by the free price tag, if anything this game makes as much as other games, but in the way CS:GO does. If you're not familar with the system. You get the game, then there's a few ways they take your money. While some may portray it as such, it's not your normal F2P bull**** where they MAKE you buy their items. Instead the microtransactions in the game are quite small. Not an intergral part of gameplay at all. Let me explain
They use a system called Cases, or Crates, and keys. They also use a system that allow low level items to spawn anyways in the middle of play. Crates can be bought on the steam market for a few cents, or dropped, and keys may be bought in-game to open these. When you open these in TF2 you will get items that have cool abilities, but none really gamebreaking. Because for every up in an item there's usually a down
The game itself does a great take on small assymetric play, if you work together, you usually win together, if you don't work together, you lose alone.
All in all there is only one downside I can find. There is too many friggin haters in the community, and when I say hater I mean the bad kind. The one that acts proffesionnal although they're on the bottom of the team, spamming chat, and just HOPING for someone to do something to stop them. All in all heres the score

Over a year ago, I wrote a silly review about Team Fortress 2, involving the questionable naming of cosmetics. That was when TF2 was, in my eyes, full of top-tier to good-tier content. I had little problems with it, and when I usually did find a problem I would wait for Valve to patch the blunder in the next update. I was naive as all hell. A year ago, if you would've told me that TF2 would become a watered-down version of itself trying to become a major competitive force in the world of online FPS games, I would've looked at you and go "oh you're just joshing me, that's not gonna happen."
It happened.
I recently surpassed 2000 hours of Team Fortress 2. 2000 hours since summer 2014. In those 2000 hours, I've seen a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥ sometimes♥♥♥♥♥♥that I could turn a blind eye to, and complete horse♥♥♥♥♥♥that made me a little more than frustrated. Team Fortress 2, at it's basics, is a very refined game. The gameplay is amazing, the maps are (mostly) beautiful, and it also includes a variety of characters with their own charming -- albeit sadistic -- personalities. I got a Steam account just to play TF2, as I had watched the Meet the Team videos before as well as other gameplay videos. I was, and still am, immersed in this game. To say that I hate this game would be a lie. This is one of my personal fave video games of all time, hands down. However, there are a lot of problems with the game at the time of writing this.
This is old news, no doubt, but the Meet Your Match update sucked. I'm talking about this update seven months after its release because the fallout from its impact still hasn't settled. I can only compare Competitive Matchmaking to a dumpster fire started by a drunken hobo who dropped a lit backalley cigarette onto a second hobo, who was sleeping in the dumpster. Casual play is like Competitive play, except this time the fire was started by four W+M1 Pyros. A lot of things are needing to be fixed, such as parties of hackers queuing up into the same game, uneven matches because BLU has 5 engineers who all build near the spawn while RED is steamrolling them, Competitive matches basically dying because the higher your rank the harder it is to find a game, etc, etc, etc. All of this, and way more, have been mentioned before by many others. Sometimes I think Valve will change their ways, then they do something stupid, then they apologize for their blunder, then mess it up again later on down the line. It's the same process of mess up, 'fess up, then mess up again.
I love this game, I really do, but Valve has made a lot of mistakes. Not just only in the MYM update, either. The last update that I considered good was Love & War, and that came out June 18, 2014. Valve, I appreciate your efforts into modernizing Team Fortress 2, but you need to think about what you're doing before you push stuff onto the players. It's time to stop apologizing and start doing something.
TL;DR: TF2, at its core, is a great game. In recent years, however, the quality of the game has dropped significantly. I recommend it, but only if you're willing to put effort into understanding the mechanics of the game.

Team Fortress 2, The game that all my friends play and have devoted their life, money and time to not the game in particular but the hats. When I first downloaded this game, I saw my friend with a bunch of items, playing like a pro.  I played alongside him, however I would get dominated and get few kills. I spent about 10 hours doing this. Afterwards, I wanted to get more experience and play like a pro, So i played offline practise. I sucked at first but in time, I managed to get the gyst of the game and managed to dominate. After about 30 hours of practising I went back to my friend again, and thinking I would play like a pro. Within the first five minutes I was being dominated by the entire opposing team. This was because I was bad at PC shooters (Excluding offline practise). However I was very good at console shooters. So one day I saw that this game had controller support. I plugged my controller in and tried going through the menus (Which was impossible with the controller). I ended up using my mouse and keyboard getting through the menus but finally, I got onto the game. I moved my right stick and found the sensitivity was extremely high. I turned it down and found out the controller is also rubbish with the game because if you move the sticks a tiny bit the game will think you are moving them as far as they go. In a desperate attempt to match up with my friend I thought that maybe getting better items would help. So I played and played and played. In a normal game practise makes perfect however in this game it does not. I continued to play and got maybe one of the items I got. I was really desperate to be able to play with my friends so I went to a last resort of buying the items I wanted. I went to the store and bought them. Then I wondered why not get one of those 'cool' hats. So I devoted my earnings towards buying my first hat. When I was about to buy it, one of my friends told me you could craft hats and that there was no point in buying them (even though I found out later that they were buying these hats themselves. Unfortunately the way that this game works is that you required 2 weapons to make one scrap metal, You would have to use three scrap metal to make one reclaimed metal, and use three reclaimed metal to make one refined metal. Finally you would have to use three refined metal for one hat. What I didnt realise is that this would give you a random hat, and you would have something like a 99% chance of getting this hat called the ghostly gibbus. On average, you will find about one gun every two hours. That means one scrap metal is the equivelant to four hours of time, one reclaimed metal the equivelant to 12 hours of time and one refined metal the equivelant of 36 hours of time. This would mean to craft a hat you will have to spend about 108 hours of time on the game, and in order to  get something that isnt the Ghostly Gibbus you would have to spend an average of 10,800 hours of time on this game, are you really up for that. As of this reason in order to buy a hat (Other than the Ghostly Gibbus) you would have to spend about £500 on a hat. A hat is just a silly little thing that you put on your in-game character. All my friends who have this game have spent hundreds of pounds of this game, and have wasted so many hours of their precious life. One of them said to me that they feel unable to live if they dont play this game. The other problem I have with this game is the repetativeness. There are eight gamemodes however the same thing happens in every game. One team gains something that the other team has/ also needs to have. The team who gets it wins. Having said so the fact that the game can be unpredictable makes it exciting for my friends
So from reading my review you know that this game is for you if you are willing to devote your life to a screen (including your money and family) and if you are MLG pro. Otherwise, don't get this game. I honestly dont think there is a person on the planet who has spent over 100 hours on this game and has kept it as a free to play. It feels more of a pay to win,

Team Fortress 2 has become one of my favourite games to play on a daily basis. It's fun and with the amount of game modes to play and weapons to get you won't be getting bored anytime soon.
The classes are all evenly balanced, my favourites to play are Sniper and Spy. Each character has their own unique weapons and quotes.
Each class has a weakness to another class i find. Like i find the Snipers weakness is spy, as a spy can get right behind it and backstab, Spy's weakness would be pyro as it can set the pyro on fire, making him visible when he tries to cloak.
The weapons you can get are fun to use, like The Huntsman i think the huntsman is really fun to use because it's really satisfying when you get a good kill with it.
In the game you can also taunt, there are each characters unique taunts, but you can buy taunts for all classes. Also some weapons come with different taunts. There are taunts where other players and interact with it, and taunt kills are really funny when you pull one off.
I honestly dont have anything negative to say other then the servers, i find, are pretty shocking.
I would rate this game a 9.5/10

To tie the Half Windsor Knot, select a necktie of your choice and stand in front of a mirror. Then simply follow the steps below:
1) Start with the wide end ("W") of your necktie on the right, extending about 12 inches below the narrow end ("N") on the left.
2) Then cross the wide end over the narrow end.
3) Bring the wide end around and behind the narrow end.
4) Then bring the wide end up.
5) Pull the wide end through the loop and to the right.
6) Bring the wide end around front, over the narrow end from right to left.
7) Again, bring the wide end up and through the loop.
8) Then, bring the wide end down through the knot in front.
9) And -- using both hands -- tighten the knot carefully and draw it up to the collar.
And there you are! Simply keep working on this necktie knot and be sure to practice a few times until you are really good at it.

Over a year ago, I wrote a silly review about Team Fortress 2, involving the questionable naming of cosmetics. That was when TF2 was, in my eyes, full of top-tier to good-tier content. I had little problems with it, and when I usually did find a problem I would wait for Valve to patch the blunder in the next update. I was naive as all hell. A year ago, if you would've told me that TF2 would become a watered-down version of itself trying to become a major competitive force in the world of online FPS games, I would've looked at you and go "oh you're just joshing me, that's not gonna happen."
It happened.
I recently surpassed 2000 hours of Team Fortress 2. 2000 hours since summer 2014. In those 2000 hours, I've seen a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥ sometimes♥♥♥♥♥♥that I could turn a blind eye to, and complete horse♥♥♥♥♥♥that made me a little more than frustrated. Team Fortress 2, at it's basics, is a very refined game. The gameplay is amazing, the maps are (mostly) beautiful, and it also includes a variety of characters with their own charming -- albeit sadistic -- personalities. I got a Steam account just to play TF2, as I had watched the Meet the Team videos before as well as other gameplay videos. I was, and still am, immersed in this game. To say that I hate this game would be a lie. This is one of my personal fave video games of all time, hands down. However, there are a lot of problems with the game at the time of writing this.
This is old news, no doubt, but the Meet Your Match update sucked. I'm talking about this update seven months after its release because the fallout from its impact still hasn't settled. I can only compare Competitive Matchmaking to a dumpster fire started by a drunken hobo who dropped a lit backalley cigarette onto a second hobo, who was sleeping in the dumpster. Casual play is like Competitive play, except this time the fire was started by four W+M1 Pyros. A lot of things are needing to be fixed, such as parties of hackers queuing up into the same game, uneven matches because BLU has 5 engineers who all build near the spawn while RED is steamrolling them, Competitive matches basically dying because the higher your rank the harder it is to find a game, etc, etc, etc. All of this, and way more, have been mentioned before by many others. Sometimes I think Valve will change their ways, then they do something stupid, then they apologize for their blunder, then mess it up again later on down the line. It's the same process of mess up, 'fess up, then mess up again.
I love this game, I really do, but Valve has made a lot of mistakes. Not just only in the MYM update, either. The last update that I considered good was Love & War, and that came out June 18, 2014. Valve, I appreciate your efforts into modernizing Team Fortress 2, but you need to think about what you're doing before you push stuff onto the players. It's time to stop apologizing and start doing something.
TL;DR: TF2, at its core, is a great game. In recent years, however, the quality of the game has dropped significantly. I recommend it, but only if you're willing to put effort into understanding the mechanics of the game.

We've come a long way, but everything will end eventually, no matter how fun it was.
If you are looking for the game's details, read the positive reviews, I will have a little rant here.
A few years ago I found this game through the famous "meet the series", after I started playing I was instantly hooked by the amazing variety of gameplay, even though I do not play anymore do to the reason I will give below I am still active in the community, some of you might know as Gilgamesh from OpenGriefing.

The game:
With the nine classes and huge amount of weapons that come with it TF2 is a game which you can play for days, even months! Each class has their own individual role which is completely unique to it, you can play in all sort of ways, and there is so much to do it rarely feels repeditive. The community is nice, and although most do not appreciate the sight of a new player, there is still a huge amount of nice people. I my self have taught 4 players on how to play TF2 whom I personally don't even know, and I had great fun in doing so, and there more people out there that do the same.
The game has a series of cosmedic items which add a lot of life and color into it. You can dress the big muscle guy called the heavy with his huge machine gun up with a fairy custom, or you can turn the German doctor called the Medic into a WW2 German infantryman of the battle of Stalingrad, these are two examples of thousands of possibilities.
There are many game modes and dozens of maps for each, which let you play the game for an unbelievable amount of time with out getting bored once. These are just the official maps. There are tens-of-thousands of community maps which also enhance the gaming experience.

The community:
TF2 is a very old game, yet it is one of the most played multiplayer games even today. The community is very committed and it was the community that made the game what it is today. Valve kept the game fresh by releasing updates that always added more content with which you could play with your friends and have loads of fun.

With that being said, here comes the problem:
As I said, TF2 has a very committed and loyal community even though the game is from today's standards as old as the bread crumbs that are left in a toaster that one day have the fortune of being vaporized, leaving the toaster as dust.
Now, valve always showed their appreciation for this through out the year by adding fresh content.
This however, has changed.

Valve, like other companies, has noticed the potential of modern competitive games, one genre of which is MOBAs. It is also very obvious that they have grown old of TF2 and want to work on different things. Their plan to keep the game alive, while slowly leaving it was to let their loyal community take over, which I have to say is quite an honorable thing to do.
However, they have completely failed at it.
The problem is, the community may be able to handle parts of the game, but not the entire game it self. It is impossible do to many factors. By this I mean, the community might be able to add content like hats and taunts to the game, but they can not expand the gaming experience, the expanding the gaming experience is exactly what made TF2 a special game, every year there was always something new to try out and after doing that, the normal game was appealing again, and the loop continued. But instead of fixing the issue, they just want to pull it through till the end, like dragging a bleeding body to the hospital but knowing that it won't make it.

Warning Rant:

Team Fortress 2, The game that all my friends play and have devoted their life, money and time to not the game in particular but the hats. When I first downloaded this game, I saw my friend with a bunch of items, playing like a pro.  I played alongside him, however I would get dominated and get few kills. I spent about 10 hours doing this. Afterwards, I wanted to get more experience and play like a pro, So i played offline practise. I sucked at first but in time, I managed to get the gyst of the game and managed to dominate. After about 30 hours of practising I went back to my friend again, and thinking I would play like a pro. Within the first five minutes I was being dominated by the entire opposing team. This was because I was bad at PC shooters (Excluding offline practise). However I was very good at console shooters. So one day I saw that this game had controller support. I plugged my controller in and tried going through the menus (Which was impossible with the controller). I ended up using my mouse and keyboard getting through the menus but finally, I got onto the game. I moved my right stick and found the sensitivity was extremely high. I turned it down and found out the controller is also rubbish with the game because if you move the sticks a tiny bit the game will think you are moving them as far as they go. In a desperate attempt to match up with my friend I thought that maybe getting better items would help. So I played and played and played. In a normal game practise makes perfect however in this game it does not. I continued to play and got maybe one of the items I got. I was really desperate to be able to play with my friends so I went to a last resort of buying the items I wanted. I went to the store and bought them. Then I wondered why not get one of those 'cool' hats. So I devoted my earnings towards buying my first hat. When I was about to buy it, one of my friends told me you could craft hats and that there was no point in buying them (even though I found out later that they were buying these hats themselves. Unfortunately the way that this game works is that you required 2 weapons to make one scrap metal, You would have to use three scrap metal to make one reclaimed metal, and use three reclaimed metal to make one refined metal. Finally you would have to use three refined metal for one hat. What I didnt realise is that this would give you a random hat, and you would have something like a 99% chance of getting this hat called the ghostly gibbus. On average, you will find about one gun every two hours. That means one scrap metal is the equivelant to four hours of time, one reclaimed metal the equivelant to 12 hours of time and one refined metal the equivelant of 36 hours of time. This would mean to craft a hat you will have to spend about 108 hours of time on the game, and in order to  get something that isnt the Ghostly Gibbus you would have to spend an average of 10,800 hours of time on this game, are you really up for that. As of this reason in order to buy a hat (Other than the Ghostly Gibbus) you would have to spend about £500 on a hat. A hat is just a silly little thing that you put on your in-game character. All my friends who have this game have spent hundreds of pounds of this game, and have wasted so many hours of their precious life. One of them said to me that they feel unable to live if they dont play this game. The other problem I have with this game is the repetativeness. There are eight gamemodes however the same thing happens in every game. One team gains something that the other team has/ also needs to have. The team who gets it wins. Having said so the fact that the game can be unpredictable makes it exciting for my friends
So from reading my review you know that this game is for you if you are willing to devote your life to a screen (including your money and family) and if you are MLG pro. Otherwise, don't get this game. I honestly dont think there is a person on the planet who has spent over 100 hours on this game and has kept it as a free to play. It feels more of a pay to win,

Over a year ago, I wrote a silly review about Team Fortress 2, involving the questionable naming of cosmetics. That was when TF2 was, in my eyes, full of top-tier to good-tier content. I had little problems with it, and when I usually did find a problem I would wait for Valve to patch the blunder in the next update. I was naive as all hell. A year ago, if you would've told me that TF2 would become a watered-down version of itself trying to become a major competitive force in the world of online FPS games, I would've looked at you and go "oh you're just joshing me, that's not gonna happen."
It happened.
I recently surpassed 2000 hours of Team Fortress 2. 2000 hours since summer 2014. In those 2000 hours, I've seen a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥ sometimes♥♥♥♥♥♥that I could turn a blind eye to, and complete horse♥♥♥♥♥♥that made me a little more than frustrated. Team Fortress 2, at it's basics, is a very refined game. The gameplay is amazing, the maps are (mostly) beautiful, and it also includes a variety of characters with their own charming -- albeit sadistic -- personalities. I got a Steam account just to play TF2, as I had watched the Meet the Team videos before as well as other gameplay videos. I was, and still am, immersed in this game. To say that I hate this game would be a lie. This is one of my personal fave video games of all time, hands down. However, there are a lot of problems with the game at the time of writing this.
This is old news, no doubt, but the Meet Your Match update sucked. I'm talking about this update seven months after its release because the fallout from its impact still hasn't settled. I can only compare Competitive Matchmaking to a dumpster fire started by a drunken hobo who dropped a lit backalley cigarette onto a second hobo, who was sleeping in the dumpster. Casual play is like Competitive play, except this time the fire was started by four W+M1 Pyros. A lot of things are needing to be fixed, such as parties of hackers queuing up into the same game, uneven matches because BLU has 5 engineers who all build near the spawn while RED is steamrolling them, Competitive matches basically dying because the higher your rank the harder it is to find a game, etc, etc, etc. All of this, and way more, have been mentioned before by many others. Sometimes I think Valve will change their ways, then they do something stupid, then they apologize for their blunder, then mess it up again later on down the line. It's the same process of mess up, 'fess up, then mess up again.
I love this game, I really do, but Valve has made a lot of mistakes. Not just only in the MYM update, either. The last update that I considered good was Love & War, and that came out June 18, 2014. Valve, I appreciate your efforts into modernizing Team Fortress 2, but you need to think about what you're doing before you push stuff onto the players. It's time to stop apologizing and start doing something.
TL;DR: TF2, at its core, is a great game. In recent years, however, the quality of the game has dropped significantly. I recommend it, but only if you're willing to put effort into understanding the mechanics of the game.

Team Fortress 2, The game that all my friends play and have devoted their life, money and time to not the game in particular but the hats. When I first downloaded this game, I saw my friend with a bunch of items, playing like a pro.  I played alongside him, however I would get dominated and get few kills. I spent about 10 hours doing this. Afterwards, I wanted to get more experience and play like a pro, So i played offline practise. I sucked at first but in time, I managed to get the gyst of the game and managed to dominate. After about 30 hours of practising I went back to my friend again, and thinking I would play like a pro. Within the first five minutes I was being dominated by the entire opposing team. This was because I was bad at PC shooters (Excluding offline practise). However I was very good at console shooters. So one day I saw that this game had controller support. I plugged my controller in and tried going through the menus (Which was impossible with the controller). I ended up using my mouse and keyboard getting through the menus but finally, I got onto the game. I moved my right stick and found the sensitivity was extremely high. I turned it down and found out the controller is also rubbish with the game because if you move the sticks a tiny bit the game will think you are moving them as far as they go. In a desperate attempt to match up with my friend I thought that maybe getting better items would help. So I played and played and played. In a normal game practise makes perfect however in this game it does not. I continued to play and got maybe one of the items I got. I was really desperate to be able to play with my friends so I went to a last resort of buying the items I wanted. I went to the store and bought them. Then I wondered why not get one of those 'cool' hats. So I devoted my earnings towards buying my first hat. When I was about to buy it, one of my friends told me you could craft hats and that there was no point in buying them (even though I found out later that they were buying these hats themselves. Unfortunately the way that this game works is that you required 2 weapons to make one scrap metal, You would have to use three scrap metal to make one reclaimed metal, and use three reclaimed metal to make one refined metal. Finally you would have to use three refined metal for one hat. What I didnt realise is that this would give you a random hat, and you would have something like a 99% chance of getting this hat called the ghostly gibbus. On average, you will find about one gun every two hours. That means one scrap metal is the equivelant to four hours of time, one reclaimed metal the equivelant to 12 hours of time and one refined metal the equivelant of 36 hours of time. This would mean to craft a hat you will have to spend about 108 hours of time on the game, and in order to  get something that isnt the Ghostly Gibbus you would have to spend an average of 10,800 hours of time on this game, are you really up for that. As of this reason in order to buy a hat (Other than the Ghostly Gibbus) you would have to spend about £500 on a hat. A hat is just a silly little thing that you put on your in-game character. All my friends who have this game have spent hundreds of pounds of this game, and have wasted so many hours of their precious life. One of them said to me that they feel unable to live if they dont play this game. The other problem I have with this game is the repetativeness. There are eight gamemodes however the same thing happens in every game. One team gains something that the other team has/ also needs to have. The team who gets it wins. Having said so the fact that the game can be unpredictable makes it exciting for my friends
So from reading my review you know that this game is for you if you are willing to devote your life to a screen (including your money and family) and if you are MLG pro. Otherwise, don't get this game. I honestly dont think there is a person on the planet who has spent over 100 hours on this game and has kept it as a free to play. It feels more of a pay to win,

Team Fortress 2 is one of the games I classify as an "Everybody" game. What I mean by that, is that everybody should be given a chance to play it at least once, whether it be at a friends house, just to try out, or even to play full session.
TF2 is a free for all multiplayer FPS game. It isn't the stereotypical "shoot everything you see" game though. This game has nine playable classes to choose from. Every one of them has a unique aspect to them. I'm not going to spoil them for you, as a better approach, you should watch the "Meet The Classes" videos to get a better description of them.
Every class also has their individual weaknesses. Whether it be the Sniper and the Spy, or if it would be the medic and the soldier. Though the community isn't really based upon the defaulties of the game. They're are purchasable items that everybody and you even, will most likley want at some point. The hats. The coats. The accesories that that one person had that you wanted, but he just killed you and went on his way etc.
Resting my case on the items, they're are many styles of gameplay one can take on, making the game have no really OP(Overpowered) people in it. Team Fortress 2 focuses heavily on skill with the individual classes, and while the classes have they're own assortment of community made weapons to choose from, they're is still always something to over-counter it.
The characters are stupid and funny, each having they're own remarks that make you chuckle and continue playing the game, just to get the full effect of it, whether it be calling the Heavy Fat(out of rage or jokingly) or insulting the engineer for sitting on his♥♥♥♥♥

This review is very lengthy, as I have a lot to say about this game. So sit tight, you are in for a long ride.
Let's get the verdict out of the way before we get to the real talk: Yes, I recommend this game.  I have spent hundreds of hours and thousands of dollars on it. Is it worth playing? Yes. Is it worth investing your time for a deeper experience? Probably not.
I already predict a lot of hate for this review, but I need to get it off my chest and explain the issues I have with this game. Once again those are my own opinions that a lot of people happen to share. It is completely fine if you want to argue against it, I will just ask you to be honest and less defensive because TF2 is in a critical state.
First of all, I'd like to point out that I've spent 1780 hours, which might be low for some, high for others. I started playing in late 2009-early 2010 and in intervals of several months between late 2010 and early 2012. I enjoyed this game a lot since it was a fresh change from the FPS games I used to play back in the days (CoD 2/4 or CS). It was extremely fun, and trust me, I do not regret a single minute I've spent on this game, before early 2014 at least. I'm not really the Shakespeare of game reviews, and English doesn't happen to be my first language, but I'll do my best to explain my points clearly. I'm going to spend some time explaining each major part the games.
I - Competitive:
Why do I want to list this subject first? Simply because this will be a quick talk: Competitive TF2 is basically the best place where you can fully enjoy TF2. The competitive community is mostly made of good and helpful people.
You will play the game the way it should've been played, whether it's a lobby, pug or a UGC match. For my part, I didn't really want to get into UGC because unfortunately I was already getting into CS:GO and couldn't get the time to look for a team but there is no reason you shouldn't.
II - Trading:
We had the good part, now the okayish part. Barely spent anytime there. I never got interested in it mainly because I'm not patient, and I can get the thing I need directly without spending 3 years working for a bigger backpack. Most of TF2 is usually into trading, whether they spend 1 hour a month or 23 hours a day in a trading website/server. The trading community is really mixed. It has good people in it, but it also has scammers and idiots. Yet, this is where I've got to meet a lot of good friends, and where I've been amazed by the ego of some. At the current state of the game, according to many professional traders, unless you have some insane item, you won't make any profit. With all the useless hats added, the supply of cosmetics is insanely high, the demand is scattered and the value the currency holds keeps dropping, dragging everything down with it. In short, trade if you want, but watch out for scammers and sharks and stick with the good people. There aren't many, but they are out there. Trading would've been one of the strengths of TF2 if Valve and the heads of some communities didn't ruin it.
III - Community:
It's really mixed. You can find good people if you go to the right pubs, as well as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who will instantly kick you if you aren't a "friendly heavy" or if you ruin their conga or any kind of circlejerk those guys are into. I wasn't lucky with Valve servers as well. Most of the times I played in those servers I was left with autistic meme spouters, 300 ping brazilians or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who will call you a tryhard if you simply try to play the game as intended. Some people also blame bronies or furries for making it worse. I honestly don't care about both, I had to witness a lot of pubs with regulars I've enjoyed playing with dying, and if there is something to blame it is not one of the game's communities such as the ones cited above, but rather the direction the game is currently taking.
IV - Updates:
The game is making a terrible turn. It went from a game that could've been a success in eSports to a casual cash-grabber made to attract more people into Steam. They keep on adding useless lore-breaking cosmetics aswell as useless weapons that keep on making the game worse. Many want Valve to add more weapons to the game - I don't. You have to understand that the point of unlocks are, or were to be very situational items and could also act as a costly alternative such as the Gunboats. Some weapons now are either completely useless such as the new grenade launcher or the Back Scatter or completely random such as the Base Jumper or the Tide Turner. Many people are complaining about EoTL for being one of the worst updates possible to the game. It was overhyped by you guys because you couldn't understand that this was the way Valve wants the game to be. Don't blame those who made EoTL, the ones to blame are those in charge of TF2. They had then to throw in a broken ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game mode that seemed to be coded within a day, as well as a couple of useless weapons or taunts to calm the community down after the disaster. The sad part is that it worked. Meanwhile, almost everyone is still waiting on that "confirmed" matchmaking system which also got "confirmed" back in 2013. Everyone's hyping it, so please, for the sake of the people who still have faith this game, whoever now's in charge of this game, do NOT ♥♥♥♥ it up.
The game is now 8 years old and still a success for the wrong reasons; but how long is it going to last before more and more people get tired by the way Valve handles the game? Once again, most of these are based on my opinions as well as the opinions of others. I hope this  might be useful for some. I had to write it to unleash the anger I had against the incompetent team supposed to replace the original developers. So go ahead, enjoy the game, play it as its fullest. If you've never played this game you are missing something, so do it now while it lasts. Thank you for your time.

Team Fortress 2 is one of the games I classify as an "Everybody" game. What I mean by that, is that everybody should be given a chance to play it at least once, whether it be at a friends house, just to try out, or even to play full session.
TF2 is a free for all multiplayer FPS game. It isn't the stereotypical "shoot everything you see" game though. This game has nine playable classes to choose from. Every one of them has a unique aspect to them. I'm not going to spoil them for you, as a better approach, you should watch the "Meet The Classes" videos to get a better description of them.
Every class also has their individual weaknesses. Whether it be the Sniper and the Spy, or if it would be the medic and the soldier. I'd give this game ten out of ten as it's a great FPS with a varied style of gameplay. As a scout you run in, do a little damage, run out. As a soldier you have area damage and can rocket jump WARNING: this is dangerous as stronger the rocket, harder it hits on enemys and you. As a pyro you can ambush enemys from behind and around corners and set people on fire at long range with the flare gun. I've been playing this game since i found steam around 2009, maybe even a longer while ago.
Tf2 holds a pretty special place in my heart because of the way it steered me. I didn't get into call of duty games and all of that, and i ended up becoming part of the steam community rather than the much worse playstation or xbox ones. That being said there are so many problems with this game that i suppose even someone with 3001 hours cannot handle. For starters the community took a turn for the ABSOLUTE worst. It's VERY unfriendly to new players as well. Too many times have i come across players who decide to 'pubstomp.' That would be the act of joining a pulic server and dominating. Usually this isn't that bad but everyone is a poor sport. They taunt, they spam the chat, they talk trash, they spew memes at you thinking they're clever. The team for this game is no better. They do nothing but add hats. And while if does take time to add weapons into the game because of testing and balancing, it's not like they weren't assigned to one game? They have almost all day to work on it and instead they spend it looking for new hats to add, so they can get money off the people who buy it. This is only slightly offset by the fact that the makers get a small porion of the money, but of course it's very small (Though it does add up)
Overall I think tf2 is dying mostly because of the community, even though the gameplay is getting boring and repetitive anyways even with valve's trashy attempts at making a new gamemode. (Robot destruction? Really?) It's also pretty much become quite the cash grab, with csgo being a close second, the only difference being that the game itself is KIND OF fun too.
If you're someone looking for a good game to get into this would be it, but it would only be it if you were planning on becoming VERY good at the game and fighting past the atrocious community to find the decent people who play competitively. I use the term decent very loosely.
Bottom line, just try it. If you like it then it's fine. I can say with plenty of experience that i've had a great uh, 2000 hours in this game. the other 1000 weren't fun because of the reasons listed above.
(Also no this isn't a rage review because of EOTL or anything, it's actually sad that i'm used to valve letting us down)

Team Fortress 2. Oh my. Probably one of the best F2P games you can play right now.
If you are new to this game you won't get absolutely stomped since if you go on Valve servers you will be matched with people of your skill level. There may be the odd two or three people that are very experienced with the game and frequents Valve servers, but for the most part everyone is around the starting skill level.
There is so much variety and personality within all the different characters in the game. 9 different characters you can play as. That's a lot. I do recommend this game. I recommend you watch the "Meet the __" videos to get ahold of the classes personality and traits. When I was writing this review I hit the character limit so it looks like I will not be writing a full on essay about TF2's characters.
The game itself is very fun. You can play Control Points, where there are a series of points where you either capture or defend. Or Capture the Flag. The Flag is a briefcase to clarify but those are the same things right? You probably get the whole idea of CTF already so I don't think I should explain. Then there's Payload. Payload and Payload Race are one of the funnest gamemodes for me. You can go on the Blu team to push the cart and explode Red teams base, or you can defend your base from the Blu team. Payload Race however, no one is defending and it is a race to see which base they can blow up first. PLR is a lot of fun since its more of a Team Deathmatch sort of thing. Then there's King of the Hill. Pretty self explanatory. King of the Hill is a game where both teams have to capture a point, and the first to do so and hold the capture point for 3 minutes will win. Because the KoTH maps are relatively small, a lot of spawncamping happens but it's still a very fun gamemode. Maybe you just don't want to VS other people. Maybe you just want to play Mann vs Machine! It's like PvE and you can win prizes if you get a Tour of Duty ticket. It's very self-explanatory, but make sure you listen to the people in this gamemode because a lot of them know what they're doing and if you don't, well it'll be worth listening to them.
If you're bored of the gamemodes there is still a lot of player-made gamemodes. You've might have heard of Death Run or Prop Hunt. Prop Hunt is like Hide and Seek, but you turn into a prop and you have to hide somewhere in an area where it looks normal for that prop to be there. Death Run is where there is a couple people operating a Temple Run-esque arena. You can try to bait the enemy into using their trap but failing to kill you, that way you can pass through without getting killed. Or you can be a blood sacrifice for your team and make them pass through with you out of the equation. Or maybe you just want to be the killer. Carefully time your executions and make sure you won't let anyone through. Have control of the arena. Very fun two gamemodes. There are a lot more but this is just two examples.
Don't want to play the game at all? Feel like doing something else? Well trading might be for you. Trading is all about making profit and climbing up the ranks. A lot of sites are centered around TF2 trading and it's not too late to start trading. Even though at the time I'm writing this (3/4/2015) the prices are pretty inflated, trading is still "alive" and kicking. There are a lot of currencies and promo items that are used in trading, but let's start off with the basic two. "Refined" and "Keys". Think of a Refined Metal as a dime. Think of Keys as three one dollar bills. Refined and keys are the most basic way to trade. Keys can be bought off the Mann. Co store for 2.49 USD. Refined Metal is made with weapons you can randomly find.
Two weapons = 1 scrap, 3 scrap = 1 reclaimed, 3 reclaimed = 1 Refined Metal. Seems pretty easy to think about right? Well if we go into other currencies, it starts to get a bit messy. There's Earbuds, Hats, Max Heads, Bill's Hats, Ebenezers, HOUWARS, Unusuals, etc. Look on backpack(dot)tf to really get into trading though.
All in all a great game, and there's always something to do. Relax and trade, or just get into the game and carry your team.
Thanks for reading this review. I could've made it 5x longer but I hit the character limit so yeah. Play this god damn game.

Team Fortress 2.
It's more than a game to me.
It's like family, as cheesy as that sounds. I have had so many good times and memories, honestly tf2 has done a lot for me, a lot for many people, I would not consider this game anything less than a masterpiece. Though it's original vision might have been lost a few times on the way I feel like TF2 is still an amazing game. I've shared it with loved ones both blood and not. I've made friends who I would consider family though it both online and off. I've stuck with TF2 though thick and thin, both in terms of my life and the game's career.
The only imperfections I can see with the game isn't even it's own doing. It's been constantly abused by Valve. It's unoptimized. Under staffed, Under appriciated. Constantly under attack by hackers. It's player count is under it's all around average.
I know that the few devs working on TF2 now are trying their hardest, some might be doing it half-heartedly... trying their best despite not even caring about the game... Only pushing because they know of the loyal and inspired fans this game holds...
Valve is ruining tf2...
However... If you can look past the faults this game falls into... Though soul crushing update after soul crushing update... hackers in valve servers... disapointment after disapointment.
You might just find the shining perfection that is TF2. You might just find the community filled with welcoming and warm-hearted people, the hilarity the game can provide, the advance tech and amazing mechanics that keep the game fresh and interesting and unique! Why when I was new to the game I had child-like wonder and glee fill my heart as I learned and basically ♥♥♥♥ed around all damn day on this game and when I see new people I get that same feeling that keeps bringing me back to this forgotten game...
As cheesy as this sounds... playing tf2 isn't just playing a game, it can be, but commiting yourself to a game like this is more of a relationship with push and pull. I hope to be playing TF2 till I can tell a computer to a goddamn blender, till I'm rotting in some chair. I want to be able to play TF2 with the same child-like wonder I had since the start. I can only hope Valve gets off their goddamn asses and ♥♥♥♥ing saves this game, a game that is miles ahead of other games much newer and shinier than it. A game that puts fire in my heart and let's it burn, and when the ashes settle and cool it allows other flames to be kindled by those ashes and burn even brighter. I want TF2 to be a fire that surpasses my own, a fire I can bring to my children, and my children's children, and so on. TF2 is a game where a depressed teen, a middle aged locksmite, a doctor, and an 11yr old can let everything behind them burn while they partake in something beautiful, something that could bring the most unlikely of people together to have joy and adventure in a bland and gray world.
God this must be cringy, I might even laugh at myself later for writing this, but deep down it's how I feel. This game has some history, with me and with many others.
So do I recommend this game? Though all the♥♥♥♥♥♥Valve has dragged me and this community though? I goddamn ♥♥♥♥ing do.

Team Fortress 2. Oh my. Probably one of the best F2P games you can play right now.
If you are new to this game you won't get absolutely stomped since if you go on Valve servers you will be matched with people of your skill level. There may be the odd two or three people that are very experienced with the game and frequents Valve servers, but for the most part everyone is around the starting skill level.
There is so much variety and personality within all the different characters in the game. 9 different characters you can play as. That's a lot. I do recommend this game. I recommend you watch the "Meet the __" videos to get ahold of the classes personality and traits. When I was writing this review I hit the character limit so it looks like I will not be writing a full on essay about TF2's characters.
The game itself is very fun. You can play Control Points, where there are a series of points where you either capture or defend. Or Capture the Flag. The Flag is a briefcase to clarify but those are the same things right? You probably get the whole idea of CTF already so I don't think I should explain. Then there's Payload. Payload and Payload Race are one of the funnest gamemodes for me. You can go on the Blu team to push the cart and explode Red teams base, or you can defend your base from the Blu team. Payload Race however, no one is defending and it is a race to see which base they can blow up first. PLR is a lot of fun since its more of a Team Deathmatch sort of thing. Then there's King of the Hill. Pretty self explanatory. King of the Hill is a game where both teams have to capture a point, and the first to do so and hold the capture point for 3 minutes will win. Because the KoTH maps are relatively small, a lot of spawncamping happens but it's still a very fun gamemode. Maybe you just don't want to VS other people. Maybe you just want to play Mann vs Machine! It's like PvE and you can win prizes if you get a Tour of Duty ticket. It's very self-explanatory, but make sure you listen to the people in this gamemode because a lot of them know what they're doing and if you don't, well it'll be worth listening to them.
If you're bored of the gamemodes there is still a lot of player-made gamemodes. You've might have heard of Death Run or Prop Hunt. Prop Hunt is like Hide and Seek, but you turn into a prop and you have to hide somewhere in an area where it looks normal for that prop to be there. Death Run is where there is a couple people operating a Temple Run-esque arena. You can try to bait the enemy into using their trap but failing to kill you, that way you can pass through without getting killed. Or you can be a blood sacrifice for your team and make them pass through with you out of the equation. Or maybe you just want to be the killer. Carefully time your executions and make sure you won't let anyone through. Have control of the arena. Very fun two gamemodes. There are a lot more but this is just two examples.
Don't want to play the game at all? Feel like doing something else? Well trading might be for you. Trading is all about making profit and climbing up the ranks. A lot of sites are centered around TF2 trading and it's not too late to start trading. Even though at the time I'm writing this (3/4/2015) the prices are pretty inflated, trading is still "alive" and kicking. There are a lot of currencies and promo items that are used in trading, but let's start off with the basic two. "Refined" and "Keys". Think of a Refined Metal as a dime. Think of Keys as three one dollar bills. Refined and keys are the most basic way to trade. Keys can be bought off the Mann. Co store for 2.49 USD. Refined Metal is made with weapons you can randomly find.
Two weapons = 1 scrap, 3 scrap = 1 reclaimed, 3 reclaimed = 1 Refined Metal. Seems pretty easy to think about right? Well if we go into other currencies, it starts to get a bit messy. There's Earbuds, Hats, Max Heads, Bill's Hats, Ebenezers, HOUWARS, Unusuals, etc. Look on backpack(dot)tf to really get into trading though.
All in all a great game, and there's always something to do. Relax and trade, or just get into the game and carry your team.
Thanks for reading this review. I could've made it 5x longer but I hit the character limit so yeah. Play this god damn game.

In Team Fortress 2 (TF2) there are 9 distinct classes, each with their own distinct abilities-
Scout-Fast, best for capturing control points
Soldier-Best for destroying sentry's, Despensers and Teleporters, also can rocket jump which involes shooting a rocket at the groun and jumping, causing you to jump higher than normal, coming down with a very high velocity, you can use this to inflict alot of damage on the other team and to stun the other team.
Sniper-Best for Sniping as the name says, the name says it all actually. Sniper is for long range attacking and headshots.
Medic-The name states it all, the medic is a doctorm, who heals ypur team and yourself, also, the medic can use something called Ubercharge, which makes the medic and whoever the medic is healing, invincible.
Engineer-Best for defence of bases and for cornering the opposing team. Can build sentrys, teleporters and healing despensers.
Demoman-Best for destroying things and spamming enemy bases with the grenade launcher. Also good for the Demoknight concept, which involve the Demoman Charging at the enemny and ramming into them, killing them.
Pyro-Best for attack, burns the other team and can leave burns on the target, watch out for anti-pyro servers though!
Heavy-A massive bloke, very wide, best for attack and defence, has the highest life out of all of the 9 Classes and uses a rapid fire minigun machine gun.
Spy-Best for sneaking around and taking out the opposuition silently. Can disguise itself as a member from the opposing team, or can become iunvisible, watch out for pyro's, they can burn you while your invisible and reveal you.

At around 100 or so hours about 9 months ago i gave this game a positive rating. Now that i have nearly 650 hours in this game i'd like to say that, as of late 2016, while the game is still every bit as amazing as when i first got hooked, there have been some radical changes that new players need to realize.
First of all, TF2 is a nine-year old game. However, it is continuously being updated by a team of around 5 people, and this means that updates cannot be fully QA tested before being pushed. Sometimes, the only way for the TF team to identify potential bugs is to have players swarm the forums with complaints after a broken update. They are typically quick to fix these bugs, but the meet Your match update, released july 2016, removed several key features such as map voting and what not in favor of a system that uses matchmaking. They readded map voting JUST A WEEK AGO. So certain features are often slow to be readded/fixed. Not to mention the fact that for 8 out of this game's 9 years of existence, tf2 was an ideal game to play on low end commoner pc's, but the past 2 major updates (Tough Break and Meet your Match) have drastically reduced framerate on low end pc's down to unplayable framerates on regular high settings, and on mid-end pc's the game will probably run at between 35-50 fps during intense sequences of battle. I currently have a Core i3 4170 and an RX 470, a pc that can run games like Watch dogs 2 at ultra settings 40-60 FPS (remember that's a 2016 AAA game), and this 9 year old game BARELY scratches 70 FPS during most intense moments on DEFAULT SETTINGS (not maxed out, but that doesn't make a difference anyway), and some of the more recent maps like Swiftwater run at a near-constant 50 FPS. While I am OK with 50 frames in more recent multiplayer games like Battlefield 1 (of which my machine struggles to maintain a consistent framerate, more like 45 fps for that game), for a game nearing its 10th anniversary this is a very poor way to show how well the game has aged. I hope valve will fix this soon because 80% of the people i know that play this game are relatively poor and have♥♥♥♥♥♥PC's, and their hardware should be more than capable of running a game of this fidelity just fine, not with ♥♥♥♥ing minecraft configs at 20 FPS.
Also, this game's community is a mixed bag. I've met many players through this game that have turned out to be great friends, but i've also met people that are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ This problem was even worse with the meet your match update because a lot of cancer from CS:GO and Overwatch started playing the game more often. If you're a new player, then there WILL be people to help you out, but if people start acting like cancer then don't let them deter you; they don't have any real power or influence in this game's community.
Now, for the gameplay itself.  this game is a mix of wacky fps ♥♥♥♥ery and strategic team-based competition. You can take this game seriously if you want or you can just ♥♥♥♥ around and have a great time. The amount of maps and game-modes shows how much this game has been overhauled and given love over the past 9 years, and while some maps are indeed terrible the vast majority of them are well-crafted and very fun to play. There are many paid for items you can buy that make the game even more insane, and while they do NOT make you better at the game they add some much needed diversity to the regular nine classes and they are ultimately worth buying simply because of the effort put into each cosmetic, each specialized strange killstreak part each skin and each overall gadget you can buy. But of course this is entirely optional, and really it just makes you "cool," but in a good way. Unlike CS:GO, which plays out like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mainstream casino, this game's economy is like an underground stock market where the rules of economics are realistic but unique. I can't really do this justice, but once you've played several hundred hours of this game you'll realize why this game's economy is quite possibly the best part of the entire game, on top of being a superb FPS game.
So do i recommend Team Fortress 2? Absolutely. On top of being my 2nd most played video game of all time (Star Wars Battlefront II has taken the number one spot within the past 10 years of my life, probably 2000 hours collectively on console and non-steam PC), this is one of the greatest FPS games of all time. While it's definitely starting to show its age with the recent updates killing the game's optimization, anyone that doesn't have a♥♥♥♥♥♥computer can enjoy a well crafted multiplayer FPS masterpiece that will keep you fragging, backstabbing, and ubercharging for nearly your entire lifetime.

Team Fortress 2 is the successor of Team Fortress Classic (TF1), a game that not many people play anymore. TF2 is vastly different from TF1 in terms of style & gameplay, but one core concept has been passed on from it's predecessor: the need for teamwork.
This game is not at all serious, and plays much differently than the more serious titles such as Call of Duty, Battlefield, or even Counter Strike. It's illogical, cartoony, and mostly comedic in how it handles itself and the environment. However, the learning curve for this game is slightly steep. If you're coming from a background in hardcore, realistic games as mentioned before...then you might find it uncomfortable. If you're -just- coming into the FPS world...then you might find it really uncomfortable. Then again, it's not too difficult to point and click until someone stops moving. :)
There are nine classes to choose from: Spy, Heavy, Demoman, Engineer, Medic, Scout, Sniper, Soldier, & Pyro. These mercenaries duke it out between each other in the most extreme case of corperate-espionage-hostile-takeover-violence that I've ever seen. Each class is unique, and are used in different situations. Knowing these classes, learning to play them effectively, and knowing what your team needs are all essential to having a good time in TF2. Also, utilizing team work is pretty important. Like: all-important. USE TEAMWORK, DAMN IT! STOP RUNNING INTO THE OTHER TEAM LIKE LEMMINGS! WHHHHHYYYYY!!!
The story has evolved over time. From a vauge concept to a fully realised world; with comics, videos, and even TV shorts planned with Adult Swim (don't know when that's coming out), it's definitely become a culture all it's own.
Blutarch & Redmond Mann, sons of a rich "gravel tycoon" are fighting over their dead father's company. Reliable Excavation & Demolition (RED), and Builders League United (BLU) are their respective company factions; with "Mann Co" is supplying the weapons (and hats)! Your job as dron---I mean...respected and valued employee of either faction is to BEAT THE OTHER TEAM in a wide array of game modes.
Capture the Intel, Attack & Defend, and Control Points are the original modes shipped with the game. However, Valve has expanded TF2's gameplay over the years with Payload, Arena, King of the Hill, Payload Race, and Medieval Mode. There area a few special modes added recently called "Special Delivery" and "Mann vs Machine". These two, along with the "Halloween" game modes, differ greatly from the average TF2 match.
This game is addictively, hilariously, sickeningly fun! Just stay away from the hats, as they're a bit of a gimmick (but admittedly, a fun gimmick).
I've been playing it for...wow...a very long time. I think I can safely say that I recommend this game!

Team Fortress 2 is the successor of Team Fortress Classic (TF1), a game that not many people play anymore. TF2 is vastly different from TF1 in terms of style & gameplay, but one core concept has been passed on from it's predecessor: the need for teamwork.
This game is not at all serious, and plays much differently than the more serious titles such as Call of Duty, Battlefield, or even Counter Strike. It's illogical, cartoony, and mostly comedic in how it handles itself and the environment. However, the learning curve for this game is slightly steep. If you're coming from a background in hardcore, realistic games as mentioned before...then you might find it uncomfortable. If you're -just- coming into the FPS world...then you might find it really uncomfortable. Then again, it's not too difficult to point and click until someone stops moving. :)
There are nine classes to choose from: Spy, Heavy, Demoman, Engineer, Medic, Scout, Sniper, Soldier, & Pyro. These mercenaries duke it out between each other in the most extreme case of corperate-espionage-hostile-takeover-violence that I've ever seen. Each class is unique, and are used in different situations. Knowing these classes, learning to play them effectively, and knowing what your team needs are all essential to having a good time in TF2. Also, utilizing team work is pretty important. Like: all-important. USE TEAMWORK, DAMN IT! STOP RUNNING INTO THE OTHER TEAM LIKE LEMMINGS! WHHHHHYYYYY!!!
The story has evolved over time. From a vauge concept to a fully realised world; with comics, videos, and even TV shorts planned with Adult Swim (don't know when that's coming out), it's definitely become a culture all it's own.
Blutarch & Redmond Mann, sons of a rich "gravel tycoon" are fighting over their dead father's company. Reliable Excavation & Demolition (RED), and Builders League United (BLU) are their respective company factions; with "Mann Co" is supplying the weapons (and hats)! Your job as dron---I mean...respected and valued employee of either faction is to BEAT THE OTHER TEAM in a wide array of game modes.
Capture the Intel, Attack & Defend, and Control Points are the original modes shipped with the game. However, Valve has expanded TF2's gameplay over the years with Payload, Arena, King of the Hill, Payload Race, and Medieval Mode. There area a few special modes added recently called "Special Delivery" and "Mann vs Machine". These two, along with the "Halloween" game modes, differ greatly from the average TF2 match.
This game is addictively, hilariously, sickeningly fun! Just stay away from the hats, as they're a bit of a gimmick (but admittedly, a fun gimmick).
I've been playing it for...wow...a very long time. I think I can safely say that I recommend this game!
