At around 100 or so hours about 9 months ago i gave this game a positive rating. Now that i have nearly 650 hours in this game i'd like to say that, as of late 2016, while the game is still every bit as amazing as when i first got hooked, there have been some radical changes that new players need to realize.
First of all, TF2 is a nine-year old game. However, it is continuously being updated by a team of around 5 people, and this means that updates cannot be fully QA tested before being pushed. Sometimes, the only way for the TF team to identify potential bugs is to have players swarm the forums with complaints after a broken update. They are typically quick to fix these bugs, but the meet Your match update, released july 2016, removed several key features such as map voting and what not in favor of a system that uses matchmaking. They readded map voting JUST A WEEK AGO. So certain features are often slow to be readded/fixed. Not to mention the fact that for 8 out of this game's 9 years of existence, tf2 was an ideal game to play on low end commoner pc's, but the past 2 major updates (Tough Break and Meet your Match) have drastically reduced framerate on low end pc's down to unplayable framerates on regular high settings, and on mid-end pc's the game will probably run at between 35-50 fps during intense sequences of battle. I currently have a Core i3 4170 and an RX 470, a pc that can run games like Watch dogs 2 at ultra settings 40-60 FPS (remember that's a 2016 AAA game), and this 9 year old game BARELY scratches 70 FPS during most intense moments on DEFAULT SETTINGS (not maxed out, but that doesn't make a difference anyway), and some of the more recent maps like Swiftwater run at a near-constant 50 FPS. While I am OK with 50 frames in more recent multiplayer games like Battlefield 1 (of which my machine struggles to maintain a consistent framerate, more like 45 fps for that game), for a game nearing its 10th anniversary this is a very poor way to show how well the game has aged. I hope valve will fix this soon because 80% of the people i know that play this game are relatively poor and have♥♥♥♥♥♥PC's, and their hardware should be more than capable of running a game of this fidelity just fine, not with ♥♥♥♥ing minecraft configs at 20 FPS.
Also, this game's community is a mixed bag. I've met many players through this game that have turned out to be great friends, but i've also met people that are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ This problem was even worse with the meet your match update because a lot of cancer from CS:GO and Overwatch started playing the game more often. If you're a new player, then there WILL be people to help you out, but if people start acting like cancer then don't let them deter you; they don't have any real power or influence in this game's community.
Now, for the gameplay itself.  this game is a mix of wacky fps ♥♥♥♥ery and strategic team-based competition. You can take this game seriously if you want or you can just ♥♥♥♥ around and have a great time. The amount of maps and game-modes shows how much this game has been overhauled and given love over the past 9 years, and while some maps are indeed terrible the vast majority of them are well-crafted and very fun to play. There are many paid for items you can buy that make the game even more insane, and while they do NOT make you better at the game they add some much needed diversity to the regular nine classes and they are ultimately worth buying simply because of the effort put into each cosmetic, each specialized strange killstreak part each skin and each overall gadget you can buy. But of course this is entirely optional, and really it just makes you "cool," but in a good way. Unlike CS:GO, which plays out like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mainstream casino, this game's economy is like an underground stock market where the rules of economics are realistic but unique. I can't really do this justice, but once you've played several hundred hours of this game you'll realize why this game's economy is quite possibly the best part of the entire game, on top of being a superb FPS game.
So do i recommend Team Fortress 2? Absolutely. On top of being my 2nd most played video game of all time (Star Wars Battlefront II has taken the number one spot within the past 10 years of my life, probably 2000 hours collectively on console and non-steam PC), this is one of the greatest FPS games of all time. While it's definitely starting to show its age with the recent updates killing the game's optimization, anyone that doesn't have a♥♥♥♥♥♥computer can enjoy a well crafted multiplayer FPS masterpiece that will keep you fragging, backstabbing, and ubercharging for nearly your entire lifetime.

This game, oh this game, it never fails to amaze me. No matter how much I play, I'm always learning new strategies. TF2 brings something that the gaming community was not very familiar with, class based gaming. All nine classes are extremely diverse from the sneaky Spy that will keep you watching over shoulder at night to the Scout, who will always be up in your face.
I'm gonna rate everything on a scale of one to ten, with ten being the best
-Art: 9/10 It has very cartoony yet somewhat realistic art for the charcters and the in-game scenery.
-Availability:11/10 It's FREE TO PLAY, and no, it is not Pay 2 Win either, this game is a legitiment free game, yeah, you don't really find those these days...
-Music and sounds: 8/10 It has great sounds but sometimes the dialogue will cut off other sounds in game. (For more enjoyment, play with earbuds or headphones)
-Class diversity: 9/10 The classes are EXTREMELY diverse, for example, the Sniper and Scout are polar opposites, one uses range to gain an advantage, the other will run up to you and blast you into next year.
-Weapons: 7/10 This can be a very contreversial topic, as some weapons are broken and overpowered, like the phlogistinator, which I like as a weapon, but it's just too broken that you can litteraly decimate an entire enemy team, no skill required. This game is great!
Team Fortress 2 is a first person shooter co-operation game. You are put on either the BLU or the RED team, then you have to beat the other team in a variety of game modes, like capture the briefcase, or take over a control point. You can play as 9 unique and stereotypical characters, they are all funny, but each character has their own pros and cons, so choose your class wisely.
The first class is Scout, a fast running kid with attitude and swag. He sure is good at taking over control points 2 times faster than any other class.
Second class is Soldier, a stereotypical American soldier, who is always angry and is willing to put his life on the line. His weapon is a rocket launcher which is epic.
Third class is Pyro, a hard-to-understand flamethrower-thrower who sees everything as a friendly kid paradise in his eyes, what he doesn't know is what he is actually doing!
Onto the defensive class, Demoman, a Scottish drunk who can kill people with his broken bottle, pretty funny to watch him drink from it and burp xD
The fifth class is Heavy, a fat Russian who is never afraid to use his minigun. I think he's in love with it...
The sixth class is Engineer, a western cowboy who is pretty much a nerd. He can help his team by building sentries and re-supply stations.
The supportive classes are...
Medic, a crazy German doctor who can heal his team mates with his medi-gun. It would be awesome if that actually existed.
Next is Sniper, a joyful Australian sniper. He is so good with his sniper, that when aiming, he never, ever moves a bit. He urinates in jars and throws them at his enemy, yuck!
Last class which I personally like is Spy. A French moody spy whose fiancée is Scout's mother. lol
anyway he can disguise as an enemy and get past enemies, and when the time strikes, STABS THEM TO DEATH!!! Gentlemen?
The classes are great! Now onto gameplay.
Most of the time, the BLU team plays offensively whereas the RED team plays defensively, and sometimes both of them play equally. Or you can play another co-op mode, as the RED team defends against bots, who try to bomb your base, it's so fun! But it's very difficult, so use teamwork.
Team Fortress 2 has a lot of weapons, and customization items for your characters, some items are only wearable on certain characters, and some are compatible with all. There is a Mann Co store where you can buy pretty much anything you want in the game using real life money. Or instead, you can craft your own items! There are sets for each class, which consists of putting on items that are linked with each other. If you complete a set and wear them, you'll will get a boost for your character, the boost depends on the set.
Each class can use different kinds of weapons, you don't need to keep using your stock weapons, but each weapons has their own pros and cons. For example, if Heavy has a new minigun that's more powerful than Sasha, then the new minigun would have lower firing rate, this balances the weapon and makes it fair for everyone in the game.
You can use Steam's workshop and create your own Team Fortress 2 items and weapons! You can create your own hat, outfit, or even make your own weapon! You can make money out of this, you know?

Team Fortress 2 is a first person shooter co-operation game. You are put on either the BLU or the RED team, then you have to beat the other team in a variety of game modes, like capture the briefcase, or take over a control point. You can play as 9 unique and stereotypical characters, they are all funny, but each character has their own pros and cons, so choose your class wisely.
The first class is Scout, a fast running kid with attitude and swag. He sure is good at taking over control points 2 times faster than any other class.
Second class is Soldier, a stereotypical American soldier, who is always angry and is willing to put his life on the line. His weapon is a rocket launcher which is epic.
Third class is Pyro, a hard-to-understand flamethrower-thrower who sees everything as a friendly kid paradise in his eyes, what he doesn't know is what he is actually doing!
Onto the defensive class, Demoman, a Scottish drunk who can kill people with his broken bottle, pretty funny to watch him drink from it and burp xD
The fifth class is Heavy, a fat Russian who is never afraid to use his minigun. I think he's in love with it...
The sixth class is Engineer, a western cowboy who is pretty much a nerd. He can help his team by building sentries and re-supply stations.
The supportive classes are...
Medic, a crazy German doctor who can heal his team mates with his medi-gun. It would be awesome if that actually existed.
Next is Sniper, a joyful Australian sniper. He is so good with his sniper, that when aiming, he never, ever moves a bit. He urinates in jars and throws them at his enemy, yuck!
Last class which I personally like is Spy. A French moody spy whose fiancée is Scout's mother. lol
anyway he can disguise as an enemy and get past enemies, and when the time strikes, STABS THEM TO DEATH!!! Gentlemen?
The classes are great! Now onto gameplay.
Most of the time, the BLU team plays offensively whereas the RED team plays defensively, and sometimes both of them play equally. Or you can play another co-op mode, as the RED team defends against bots, who try to bomb your base, it's so fun! But it's very difficult, so use teamwork.
Team Fortress 2 has a lot of weapons, and customization items for your characters, some items are only wearable on certain characters, and some are compatible with all. There is a Mann Co store where you can buy pretty much anything you want in the game using real life money. Or instead, you can craft your own items! There are sets for each class, which consists of putting on items that are linked with each other. If you complete a set and wear them, you'll will get a boost for your character, the boost depends on the set.
Each class can use different kinds of weapons, you don't need to keep using your stock weapons, but each weapons has their own pros and cons. For example, if Heavy has a new minigun that's more powerful than Sasha, then the new minigun would have lower firing rate, this balances the weapon and makes it fair for everyone in the game.
You can use Steam's workshop and create your own Team Fortress 2 items and weapons! You can create your own hat, outfit, or even make your own weapon! You can make money out of this, you know?

Ok. I dont know where to start. Let me start with cosmetics first. Cosmetics are virtual clothing you can equip to the apparel of your character, and I see them everywhere. Different types of cosmetics are unusuals and stranges, and they are very rare, and are for the very skilled and experienced players. I have a strange cosmetic for my Spy. Its not that good though. Its only up to 'the 'Glamorous' rating. Speaking of stranges and unusuals, you can also equip it on weapons, too. Weapons are not realistic in this game, but it's how we all like them. A good example of a good weapon might be the minigun that Heavy has. My friend Brynley loves Heavy. He uses it almost everytime we play a match together. We often play on Orange X 7, which is a community map. My OTHER friend, Patrick, loves Orange X 7. Community maps are custom maps ingame users can create and customize for others to play. I don't like community matches myself. What I do like are the actual ingame maps created by the developers at Valve, such as Dustbowl, Turbine, Hightower and more. I actually don't remember the other maps, but every single one of them is awesome. Different gamemodes can be catergorised into these maps. These are the gamemodes:
In Capture the Flag, teams must retrieve a briefcase from the enemy base and return it to their own base, while defending their own briefcase. When a player drops the briefcase, the team has one minute to retrieve it before it returns to the home base.
In Special Delivery, a variant of Capture the Flag, teams fight over a single suitcase in an attempt to deliver to their targets.
In Control Point, teams must capture control points by standing on the point for a short amount of time. In some maps, teams can only capture points adjacent to points they already control. In others, RED team already controls all the control points and must defend them from BLU; captured points cannot be reclaimed by RED.
In Territorial Control, a more complex version of Control Point, each map is divided into closed sections, held between teams. Each round has one team attempting to seize control of the opposing team's capture point for that section. Once a team holds all but the enemy's home base point, they attempt to capture the enemy base point while the enemy defends.
King of the Hill features a single control point in the center of the map, with teams attempting to gain control over it. The control point is locked for a set amount of time after the round start. Once the point is unlocked, either team can capture it. Capturing the control point starts the team's clock counting down. The clock that is currently counting down will only stop if the other team captures the point, the clock reaches 0:00, or another map-specific event occurs such as a Halloween boss spawning during the Halloween event. Teams win the round when their clock reaches 0:00 with the control point currently under their control. If the other team is capturing the point, the round will not end until the point's capture progress resets to 0, and the clock will continue to count down until it is actually captured.
In Payload, the BLU team must escort a cart carrying a bomb along a railroad through a series of checkpoints defended by the RED team. The cart moves only when BLU players are nearby. The cart begins moving backwards to the last checkpoint if RED team's players are able to defend it long enough.
In Payload Race, each team has a cart and a railroad, and must deliver their cart to their checkpoint first.
Arena is a team deathmatch in a small map with a single checkpoint. Players do not respawn; teams win by capturing the control point or eliminating the other team.
Mann vs Machine is a six player cooperative mode where the mercenaries defend a structure against increasingly difficult waves of robots. Players have the ability to buy upgrades and improvements between rounds using in-game money earned during previous waves. A "Mann Up" version is available by purchasing tickets with real money to participate in larger events on official servers with the opportunity to win unique cosmetic items after successfully completing a Tour of Duty.
Mannpower is a modified version of Capture the Flag in which teams must capture the enemy's briefcase of intelligence a set number of times while preventing the enemy from doing the same. The game mode is characterized by its usage of grappling hooks and twelve unique power-ups.
Player Destruction is a game mode made official by the community-made Invasion Update that focuses on teams collecting items (bottles of beer) by killing enemy players, and then entering a specific area (jumping into a UFO tractor beam) in order to add them to their team's score.
PASS Time is a game mode inspired by rugby, developed by Valve, Bad Robot Interactive, and Escalation Studios. A single ball can be picked up by a player, and while they hold this, they cannot use any weapons but gain health regeneration, higher defense, faster movement speed, and the ability to see all players on the level. Players can pass the ball to other players or throw it aside to return to their normal patterns of attack, and will automatically drop the ball if killed. The ball can also be stolen if an opposing player intercepts a pass, or hits the carrier with their melee weapon. The goal is to get the ball through the opponent's goal more often than the opponents. The beta for this mode was added in July 2016.
Halloween Mode is a game type up for selection, only accessible days before and sometimes after Halloween. The first Halloween event, or Scream Fortress event started in the year 2009, in the Haunted Hallowe'en Special, part of the October 29, 2009 patch. Scream Fortress features a collection of slightly altered maps, such as Mann Manor, Sinshine, and Brimstone. There have been 14 Halloween maps released to the public so far. Each Scream Fortress event is brought by an update, some of which adding more features to the event and some only enabling the choice of a Halloween server with no changes. Only in Halloween mode can there be a boss fight against AI. Some bosses include Merasmus, The Headless Horseless Horsemann, and Monoculus. Not all maps have boss fights, however, with some only being altered. One of which is Helltower, where instead of Payload carts, there are the two dead Mann brothers. The goal is to push the opposite team's brother into hell, and if neither side does so in a certain amount of time, all the players are sent to hell and must reach the end in order to be able to collect a new item. This is also achievable on a victory of one team.
A training mode exists to help new players get used to the game, using wooden target dummies for practice and to introduce them to concepts of the multiplayer modes, though likely through an oversight is limited to four out of the nine classes. Game modes allowing respawn all have a delay of a few seconds before a player may respawn again, with the respawn system waves' time being relative to the team's role (for example, the defenders have their respawn waves spaced far apart, while the attackers have a shorter delay between each wave). Since 2009, there is also typically a Halloween-themed variation on one or more of the above modes during the weeks around the holiday, with maps or modes updated to include themed decorations and often a more difficult challenge to the players. For example, for Halloween 2012, this included an extremely difficult Mann vs. Machine round involving destroying more than 800 enemy forces. Due to popular demand of the Halloween events, Valve added Full Moon, the ability to play these events on the few days around the full moon throughout the year, and later Eternaween, the ability for players to vote to play the themed-events for a two-hour block at any other time.
With that all being said, this game actually deserves a 10/10 from me.

-TEAM FORTRESS 2 COMPETITIVE BETA REVIEW-
[Whilst I highly recommend the game the game for casual fun, competitive tells a different story]
__________________________________________
A while ago, a complete stranger gifted me a pass to the TF2 Competitive Beta. I was excited. I had seen a lot of players with these passes in-game and, being a former CS:Go player, was interested in seeing how it fared against Valve's other famous competitive game.
The short answer? Not well.
The problem is, Valve has distributed a lot of passes to players that don't actually play the game mode. There are over 2000 empty game servers every time I have attempted to play, and many of these have high pings etc. because of the scarcity of players meaning I have to play with people located quite far from the server itself.
There are normally around 60-70 people playing on a good day, and it's 6v6, so you need to wait for 12 people to all connect, during which people get frustrated and leave, and the match gets cancelled because somebody abandoned.
Abandoning is another issue. The wait times are so long that sometimes my game will freeze and then, when I restart the game, I have been given a match ban because the game froze. that's not MY fault, it's Valve's, but they feel the need to ban for 8 hours anyway. Valve seem to think there's a way around this. if you have a match ban, you will only be connected to a game with other players who have match bans -- but there are so few people playing at any given time that this completely defeats the purpose.
Unlike CS:GO, TF2 starts you all at the same rank, rather than playing unranked matches and then being assigned an appopriate rank, you start at rock bottom - 'Fresh Meat'. Given that no F2P players are able to get a pass, the majority of my opponents have been exceptionally good. I mena, like, SERIOUSLY, good. One of them was even using hacks, showing that despite Valve's♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥crackdown, cheaters still exist out there.
Basically, I highly recommend TF2 for its casual features, but if you've come to play Competitive, wait about 6 months for the player base to grow, or just swap over to Overwatch if you can't be f*cked to put up with Valve's servers.

After playing Team Fortress 2 for the past year and a half, I can say without a doubt that this is one of the best FPS games I have ever played. The fact that it takes genuine teamwork to complete an objective, and not just everyone doing their own thing, was awesome to me. In most FPS games, game modes are more based on a team's overall kill count, instead of a team's ability to cooperate and succeed. Team Fortress 2, on the other hand (as stated in the title), is a completely team-based objective game. If you want to succeed, you must work with your fellow team mates, and strategically decide who should be what class. Which brings me to my next point: balance. The game, unlike many other FPS games I have played, is very well balanced. Because each class has its own distinct strengths and weaknesses. In many other FPS games, each player can be whatever they want, and still have a chance at winning. But in Team Fortress 2, the game depends on class balance in the teams. A team cannot succeed with only Engineers, or only Soldiers, Heavies, etc. A team always needs a balanced number of each class on it. And sometimes, one needs to sacrifice the class they would rather play, and be the class that the team needs most at the current point in time. This is a WONDERFUL Free to Play game, which brings me to my final point: money. Obviously, Team Fortress 2 is Free to Play, which was the main reason I got it to begin with. But the biggest complaint that I have heard in the past about a lot of Free to Play FPS games, is that even though they are Free to Play, they are mostly Pay to Win. But with Team Fortress 2, that is not the case. Every player in the game has the ability to find any weapon in the game with random drops. The only thing paying for something does for you is it gives a premium membership, at which point you gain the ability to trade with other players within the Team Fortress 2 Universe. Your biggest issue with being a Free to Play, though, is other people. People who have been playing for a long time, and especially those who bought the game before it was free, will look down upon you for being what they call an F2P (standing for Free2Play). My advice to you is: don't let anyone put you down in this game. You have as much of a right to play it as they do. They simply feel that since they have been playing longer, that they have more "authority" over you. This is not true, you control you. So you just get out there and do the best you can at what you're doing. You may not be good at first, but you'll get there. You'll find you strengths and weaknesses, and then you will improve your skills over time. Everyone starts out bad. Even the veteran Team Fortress 2 players. So, overall, I would most certainly give Team Fortress 2 5 stars for gameplay, class balance, and giving everyone (F2P or not) a fair chance in the game.
Thank you for reading, and have fun.

Ok. I dont know where to start. Let me start with cosmetics first. Cosmetics are virtual clothing you can equip to the apparel of your character, and I see them everywhere. Different types of cosmetics are unusuals and stranges, and they are very rare, and are for the very skilled and experienced players. I have a strange cosmetic for my Spy. Its not that good though. Its only up to 'the 'Glamorous' rating. Speaking of stranges and unusuals, you can also equip it on weapons, too. Weapons are not realistic in this game, but it's how we all like them. A good example of a good weapon might be the minigun that Heavy has. My friend Brynley loves Heavy. He uses it almost everytime we play a match together. We often play on Orange X 7, which is a community map. My OTHER friend, Patrick, loves Orange X 7. Community maps are custom maps ingame users can create and customize for others to play. I don't like community matches myself. What I do like are the actual ingame maps created by the developers at Valve, such as Dustbowl, Turbine, Hightower and more. I actually don't remember the other maps, but every single one of them is awesome. Different gamemodes can be catergorised into these maps. These are the gamemodes:
In Capture the Flag, teams must retrieve a briefcase from the enemy base and return it to their own base, while defending their own briefcase. When a player drops the briefcase, the team has one minute to retrieve it before it returns to the home base.
In Special Delivery, a variant of Capture the Flag, teams fight over a single suitcase in an attempt to deliver to their targets.
In Control Point, teams must capture control points by standing on the point for a short amount of time. In some maps, teams can only capture points adjacent to points they already control. In others, RED team already controls all the control points and must defend them from BLU; captured points cannot be reclaimed by RED.
In Territorial Control, a more complex version of Control Point, each map is divided into closed sections, held between teams. Each round has one team attempting to seize control of the opposing team's capture point for that section. Once a team holds all but the enemy's home base point, they attempt to capture the enemy base point while the enemy defends.
King of the Hill features a single control point in the center of the map, with teams attempting to gain control over it. The control point is locked for a set amount of time after the round start. Once the point is unlocked, either team can capture it. Capturing the control point starts the team's clock counting down. The clock that is currently counting down will only stop if the other team captures the point, the clock reaches 0:00, or another map-specific event occurs such as a Halloween boss spawning during the Halloween event. Teams win the round when their clock reaches 0:00 with the control point currently under their control. If the other team is capturing the point, the round will not end until the point's capture progress resets to 0, and the clock will continue to count down until it is actually captured.
In Payload, the BLU team must escort a cart carrying a bomb along a railroad through a series of checkpoints defended by the RED team. The cart moves only when BLU players are nearby. The cart begins moving backwards to the last checkpoint if RED team's players are able to defend it long enough.
In Payload Race, each team has a cart and a railroad, and must deliver their cart to their checkpoint first.
Arena is a team deathmatch in a small map with a single checkpoint. Players do not respawn; teams win by capturing the control point or eliminating the other team.
Mann vs Machine is a six player cooperative mode where the mercenaries defend a structure against increasingly difficult waves of robots. Players have the ability to buy upgrades and improvements between rounds using in-game money earned during previous waves. A "Mann Up" version is available by purchasing tickets with real money to participate in larger events on official servers with the opportunity to win unique cosmetic items after successfully completing a Tour of Duty.
Mannpower is a modified version of Capture the Flag in which teams must capture the enemy's briefcase of intelligence a set number of times while preventing the enemy from doing the same. The game mode is characterized by its usage of grappling hooks and twelve unique power-ups.
Player Destruction is a game mode made official by the community-made Invasion Update that focuses on teams collecting items (bottles of beer) by killing enemy players, and then entering a specific area (jumping into a UFO tractor beam) in order to add them to their team's score.
PASS Time is a game mode inspired by rugby, developed by Valve, Bad Robot Interactive, and Escalation Studios. A single ball can be picked up by a player, and while they hold this, they cannot use any weapons but gain health regeneration, higher defense, faster movement speed, and the ability to see all players on the level. Players can pass the ball to other players or throw it aside to return to their normal patterns of attack, and will automatically drop the ball if killed. The ball can also be stolen if an opposing player intercepts a pass, or hits the carrier with their melee weapon. The goal is to get the ball through the opponent's goal more often than the opponents. The beta for this mode was added in July 2016.
Halloween Mode is a game type up for selection, only accessible days before and sometimes after Halloween. The first Halloween event, or Scream Fortress event started in the year 2009, in the Haunted Hallowe'en Special, part of the October 29, 2009 patch. Scream Fortress features a collection of slightly altered maps, such as Mann Manor, Sinshine, and Brimstone. There have been 14 Halloween maps released to the public so far. Each Scream Fortress event is brought by an update, some of which adding more features to the event and some only enabling the choice of a Halloween server with no changes. Only in Halloween mode can there be a boss fight against AI. Some bosses include Merasmus, The Headless Horseless Horsemann, and Monoculus. Not all maps have boss fights, however, with some only being altered. One of which is Helltower, where instead of Payload carts, there are the two dead Mann brothers. The goal is to push the opposite team's brother into hell, and if neither side does so in a certain amount of time, all the players are sent to hell and must reach the end in order to be able to collect a new item. This is also achievable on a victory of one team.
A training mode exists to help new players get used to the game, using wooden target dummies for practice and to introduce them to concepts of the multiplayer modes, though likely through an oversight is limited to four out of the nine classes. Game modes allowing respawn all have a delay of a few seconds before a player may respawn again, with the respawn system waves' time being relative to the team's role (for example, the defenders have their respawn waves spaced far apart, while the attackers have a shorter delay between each wave). Since 2009, there is also typically a Halloween-themed variation on one or more of the above modes during the weeks around the holiday, with maps or modes updated to include themed decorations and often a more difficult challenge to the players. For example, for Halloween 2012, this included an extremely difficult Mann vs. Machine round involving destroying more than 800 enemy forces. Due to popular demand of the Halloween events, Valve added Full Moon, the ability to play these events on the few days around the full moon throughout the year, and later Eternaween, the ability for players to vote to play the themed-events for a two-hour block at any other time.
With that all being said, this game actually deserves a 10/10 from me.

The game is starting to become more of a social experience, what with the conga lines and friendly players on opposing teams. My only concern, however, is that Team Fortress 2 may be rather intimidating to the newer players, maybe a bit overwhelming. With all of these new cosmetics, a vast arsenal of weapons, and the ability to turn any bloody battlefield into a parade has changed the face of shooters. I'm afraid that newer players may start playing and will be immediately turned off by either the vast personalities and items, or just the overall sillyness. Regardless, TF2 remains a great game over 7 years after its initial launch. Props to you, Valve!

After playing Team Fortress 2 for the past year and a half, I can say without a doubt that this is one of the best FPS games I have ever played. The fact that it takes genuine teamwork to complete an objective, and not just everyone doing their own thing, was awesome to me. In most FPS games, game modes are more based on a team's overall kill count, instead of a team's ability to cooperate and succeed. Team Fortress 2, on the other hand (as stated in the title), is a completely team-based objective game. If you want to succeed, you must work with your fellow team mates, and strategically decide who should be what class. Which brings me to my next point: balance. The game, unlike many other FPS games I have played, is very well balanced. Because each class has its own distinct strengths and weaknesses. In many other FPS games, each player can be whatever they want, and still have a chance at winning. But in Team Fortress 2, the game depends on class balance in the teams. A team cannot succeed with only Engineers, or only Soldiers, Heavies, etc. A team always needs a balanced number of each class on it. And sometimes, one needs to sacrifice the class they would rather play, and be the class that the team needs most at the current point in time. This is a WONDERFUL Free to Play game, which brings me to my final point: money. Obviously, Team Fortress 2 is Free to Play, which was the main reason I got it to begin with. But the biggest complaint that I have heard in the past about a lot of Free to Play FPS games, is that even though they are Free to Play, they are mostly Pay to Win. But with Team Fortress 2, that is not the case. Every player in the game has the ability to find any weapon in the game with random drops. The only thing paying for something does for you is it gives a premium membership, at which point you gain the ability to trade with other players within the Team Fortress 2 Universe. Your biggest issue with being a Free to Play, though, is other people. People who have been playing for a long time, and especially those who bought the game before it was free, will look down upon you for being what they call an F2P (standing for Free2Play). My advice to you is: don't let anyone put you down in this game. You have as much of a right to play it as they do. They simply feel that since they have been playing longer, that they have more "authority" over you. This is not true, you control you. So you just get out there and do the best you can at what you're doing. You may not be good at first, but you'll get there. You'll find you strengths and weaknesses, and then you will improve your skills over time. Everyone starts out bad. Even the veteran Team Fortress 2 players. So, overall, I would most certainly give Team Fortress 2 5 stars for gameplay, class balance, and giving everyone (F2P or not) a fair chance in the game.
Thank you for reading, and have fun.

It's a shame because only yesterday I was happy playing what was the only shooter I know which doesn't take itself seriously, provides a fun atmosphere for all participants and allows enough freedom for you to find or create a game which is enjoyable to you.

I mean yes, I know the point of every game is to win but it's the playing that counts, the fun little things that you do in matches is what made TF2 special, but it seems that's far removed, and it's a shame as I feel Valve is more interested in pushing this to be "Just like every other game out there" than it is in keeping the game with its unique features which set it aside from everyone else.
Goodbye TF2, you have served me well.

This game is very fun but just OK.
Gameplay is taken up by 9 classes- Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Sniper, Medic and Spy. Like L4D, they have unique personalities, which is cool. You play as the RED or BLU teams, looking the same with palette changes. Kill the other team is the objective, with different modes such as CTF or Payload, where you push a cart to the end of a track. It kinda gets boring after a while.
The graphics are excellent, as are the physics. They went for something different as an art style- a cartoony style set in the late '60s-early '70s. The physics are ragdoll physics, which can create some funny results tagging along with the killcam. This game uses the great Source engine for physics.
The score in this game is good, but not great. There are a couple good songs sprinkled here and there, some are good, some suck. The effects are good too, but vocal effects get annoying after around 15 minutes of playing a match, having a person asking for a Sentry or Dispenser every 2 seconds.
Maps are OK in terms of navigation, some are easy to move around in, some are hard.
PROS:
+Graphics are great, along with Sources physics and rendering
+Some maps easy to navigate
+Good community
+Couple of good songs
+Variety in game modes
+Stuff people make may or may not make it into the game
+Lots of mods and maps
+Not COD
CONS:
-Gameplay gets boring after 1-2 hours
-Too many people taunt instead of reaching for objective
-Vocal effects get annoying
-DLC prices are RIDICULOUS, charging upwards of almost $50 for a hat that doesn't affect the game
-Weapons stats are nerfed and some become OP
-Trades are stupid, asking 1 scrap for a rare item as an example
-Too many and too hard achievements, asking too much out of you
OVERALL: 8/10 Recommended, but I would download it just to put it in your library and to say you own TF2. I wouldn't waste too much money on DLC.

Okay, this game is, or at least used to be a lot of fun for me. On to the review.
Graphics- 9/10
The visuals of the game are very lovely and even workshop items look very good. This is the kind of game that isn't too straining on the eyes, unless of course you're like me and first played it on an oolder computer with an older graphics card and wound having all the enviornments look like a blinding mess of colors due to missing textures but that can be resolved.
Control- 9.5/10
The controls are very responsive and aren't difficult to learn if you've played other Valve games on a computer. I don't have much to say about them other than the fact that there's not run button. You can't run in this game unless you're Scout who runs in general being the fastest character in the game, the others can't run, in my eyes they appear to be jogging, but that's not a tragedy. It's fun to go about the game without much of a problem, and there's no problems with the controls here.
Story- 4/10
Now the reason this rating is low is due to the fact that there's no real story other than the Meet The *insert character name here* videos on youtube, but honestly I could dig for a long while and probably find no real story to the game at all, or why these two teams became enemies, or hell I still don't understand why both teams characters are the same as one another. Plus with the lack of an actual Single Player Mode/Campaign there's nothing I can really say to boost a rating for this part.
Gameplay- 4.9/10 (Unfortunately...and this rating was planned to be higher originally)
There's a reason for a low rating here too, and it's not even Valve's fault why I have it like this. It's the community's...What once was a game filled with mostly normal gamers ranging from new to active and fair gameplay that tied in greatly with anything from Steam Workshop for the game, just...got completely ♥♥♥♥ed up one day all of a sudden. Now for the most part you can't go onto one game without some little kid that shouldn't even be playing an FPS even as silly as this one, some "MLG" junky, or just some immature player that completely ruins the expierence for gamers like me who prefer to PLAY a game for fun, not turn into something that not only I, but many others have complained about for a long time, ESPECIALLY when this "MLG" storm hit the COD series, completely ruining it for me. I'm not saying it's annoying the first time you hear it (because it's easy to laugh it off for a little while), but it is after you hear the words "GET NO-SCOPED!" or *insert sound of a bunch of people flipping their♥♥♥♥♥♥over a no-scope or whatever* or even having to see the 1,000 "get rekt" enter into a lobby chat. It's getting annoying and in my opinion, MLG shouldn't be consider a major league, there's no reason for it, and now that it's hit TF2 my outlook on the game will never be as positive as it used to be.
Overall Rating: Approximately 7/10
Final Verdict: Recommended, but may not completely satify.
This game when I first played it was such a fun experience that I was happy to be able to share with many that have the game, but unfortunately now that's changed and I can never look at Team Fotress 2 the same way. A couple have my friends have quit TF2, and I know why now. Now I'll make this clear: I don't HATE the game, I'm just very disappointed with a good amount of it's built up community being composed more and more of immaturity then of what gaming is about and what it used to be. If I go back to this game again, it'll probably only because I'm playing it with one or two other friends. Other than that, my disappointment has made me isolate this game a lot, and it's a real shame that things wound up this way. If you don't want to follow my word on it, then you don't have to, but if you do, it's only a fair warning, not a banner saying "AVOID THIS GAME", because I'd never go as far as to say in an honest review that a game isn't worth playing unless it's really so bad to the point it's unplayable. With that, I bid everyone farewell, I've done my part here.

Now for the most part you can't go onto one game without some little kid that shouldn't even be playing an FPS even as silly as this one, some "MLG" junky, or just some immature player that completely ruins the expierence for gamers like me who prefer to PLAY a game for fun, not turn into something that not only I, but many others have complained about for a long time, ESPECIALLY when this "MLG" storm hit the COD series, completely ruining it for me. I'm not saying it's annoying the first time you hear it (because it's easy to laugh it off for a little while), but it is after you hear the words "GET NO-SCOPED!" or *insert sound of a bunch of people flipping their♥♥♥♥♥♥over a no-scope or whatever* or even having to see the 1,000 "get rekt" enter into a lobby chat. It's getting annoying and in my opinion, MLG shouldn't be consider a major league, there's no reason for it, and now that it's hit TF2 my outlook on the game will never be as positive as it used to be.
Overall Rating: Approximately 7/10
Final Verdict: Recommended, but may not completely satify.
This game when I first played it was such a fun experience that I was happy to be able to share with many that have the game, but unfortunately now that's changed and I can never look at Team Fotress 2 the same way. A couple have my friends have quit TF2, and I know why now. Now I'll make this clear: I don't HATE the game, I'm just very disappointed with a good amount of it's built up community being composed more and more of immaturity then of what gaming is about and what it used to be. If I go back to this game again, it'll probably only because I'm playing it with one or two other friends. Other than that, my disappointment has made me isolate this game a lot, and it's a real shame that things wound up this way. If you don't want to follow my word on it, then you don't have to, but if you do, it's only a fair warning, not a banner saying "AVOID THIS GAME", because I'd never go as far as to say in an honest review that a game isn't worth playing unless it's really so bad to the point it's unplayable. With that, I bid everyone farewell, I've done my part here.

Team Fortress 2. I cannot even start to describe how great it is. It was so great in my opinion that I was playing it every free second I got. Team Fortress 2 is a FPS (First-Person Shooter for those of you who don't know) with 9 different classes you can use to kill either RED (Reliable Excavation and Demolition) or BLU (Builders League United). The game premise is complete your objective before your enemy does. There are a lot of wacky weapons in this game such as the Cow Mangler 2000 or the Bison 4000. This game will have you screaming at the people who kill you and taunt you afterwards, and heaving a sigh of relief after making it through the enemy defense. The games classes are: the Scout, Soldier, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy, each with their own abilities. For example, the Spy can turn invisible for a short amount of time, and the Scout, who is the fastest, is best for both attack and defense. In fact, why are you still reading this? Go. Download it. Have a crapload of fun.

Overall, TF2 is fun and I would greatly recommend it.

As for myself, I hopped into this game only 1.5 year ago and I'm still enjoying it, so let me just give a few tips if you want to pick it up for the first time:

Team Fortress 2 is very different from other shooter games in three regards:
1: it has a sort of cartoony look which actually compliments the game as it's not so real, but just real enough to make it look superb.
2: the weapons in this game are vastly different in style whereas in most of these games, everyone has SMGs. In TF2 the weapons are everything from rocket launchers, to flame throwers, to mini guns. It makes this game very fun to play.
3: This game is totally free to play. In most other games of this style, you have to plunk down twenty bucks or so, this game you can start for free, gather different weapons, and expand your armory for tons of playing modes.
And TF2 is equipped with many different playing modes, offline practice, trading, and more updates, that the game is still refreshingly new, eight years later.

My logged hours may not reflect it but I've been with this game for what seems like the dawn of time. I paid for my copy back in.... 2009 I think... after playing it countless times at the local gaming cafe. It's a great and "simple" FPS with a pretty decent community. I mean every community has ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s but for the most part, it's been amazing! I'm a pretty vanilla player. I don't craft. I don't care about hats. I don't care if I have a weapon that's something other than "normal". But if you're into that, it's crazy how extensive that side of things is. I just like to get lost for hours on some random map, depending on my mood, and go at it. Always Team Red suckas!
It's easy to pick up and go but it's complicated enough that even after all these years of playing, I discover some new tactic or achievement I can get or do a thing I didn't know I could do. For the most part, everything is pretty balanced and each class really does hold his own as well as aide in combat. You can either be a badass and go off on your own or work with your team to use each other to achieve victory. That is something I really appreciate.
Also, let's just talk about maps/game modes for a sec. The traditional are just as great as what the community makes. I think it's cool that you can have your own server and build your own map. I know I have enjoyed several rounds of Dodgeball, Prop Hunt, and whatever that Slenderman, Weeping Angel, other horror people game mode things are. Also, if you haven't, there's a Mario Kart server that is just super silly and chill. I recommend checking that one out in particular.
The only thing I absolutely hate is the ridiculous and/or random trading requests in the middle of battle which I suppose is more about the players than the game. I really just wanna play and not worry about 2954 pings from "HerpaDerp1234" distracting me from taking down the other team. Can you wait til set-up or PM me so we can trade after the match or when we are done playing if you are THAT desperate for whatever I have? Come on man...
All in all,  it's a great time killer. It has a great amount of variety depending on how you like to play and it's super fun. I reccomend this to everyone no matter the type of video game you like playing.

As for myself, I hopped into this game only 1.5 year ago and I'm still enjoying it, so let me just give a few tips if you want to pick it up for the first time:

2. Start getting your bearings with one of the following classes: Medic (highly recommended), Heavy, or Soldier. These classes are the most straightforward in terms of getting used of gameplay and game mechanics. Later on you can try Pyro, Demoman and Engineer, and finally Sniper and Spy.

I still recommend it, BUT, this is not a game that you can just hop into and do well from the beginning, there are lots of things you must know, a lot of do's and don't's, and with this game being almost 8 years old and some players having almost 8 years of experience, there is a HUGE skill gap that cannot be ignored, especially on the official servers. As for myself, I hopped into this game only 1.5 year ago and I'm still enjoying it, so let me just give a few tips if you want to pick it up for the first time:
1. Do some practice in off-line mode before taking on the online experience. Bots don't steamroll and grief as much as the pubstompers on Valve servers, so you can explore the game a bit without getting absolutely stomped every game you play.
2. Start getting your bearings with one of the following classes: Medic (highly recommended), Heavy, or Soldier. These classes are the most straightforward in terms of getting used of gameplay and game mechanics. Later on you can try Pyro, Demoman and Engineer, and finally Sniper and Spy.

100+ hours is nothing to scoff at, really, compared to the other players here.
I started playing TF2 when it first went F2P, then bought a couple of inventory expansions a while later.
Back then the game was still pretty nice, albeit it being F2P, an influx of newbies (yes, me included). I continued playing on and off for about a year or so, till I just stopped. No idea why I did, but I just did.
At least till MvM came out. I went in, tried queuing for a game and played a few games. Then I just stopped.
So fast forward to last week, I got back into the game due to boredom.
Sure, there were new weapons, new hats, all that jazz.
But the community wasn't the same any more.
I'm a player from Singapore, hence, I used to frequent the
and Starhub E-Club servers back in 2011 and 2012. Those were gone, mainly from DDoS attacks and the community in general (from what I could gather online). And now it's just (mostly) Dustbowl, 2Fort, Orange and PLR Upward 24/7 servers around.
Starhub servers were probably the best servers to play in, since there was actually map rotation, rather than just a fixed map 24/7 over and over again.
Needless to say, it got bland pretty damn fast.
At this point, I really wish I could recommend TF2, but with the way things are (I'm not sure about the other side of the world - Western countries lol) I don't think I can. It's still fun, though. But for me it doesn't feel like I'm returning to the same TF2 as it was before. It just feels wrong.

This a very entertaining game that allows you to battle with friends, or just anyone, by choosing one of nine classes that each has their own pros and cons. You will either be on team blue or team red. Obviously, the teams are against eachother and you want to battle the opposing colour. There are a variety of game modes to choose from where you must beat the other team. You can trade items, and there is even a whole currency for this game that is used in trading, or when identifying the price of your specified item.
Overall I think this game is great. I highly recommend it for people who love action filled games, and who love to learn new skills. I recommend helping your team out if you would like to win, and don't leave them behind. Team Fortress 2 is a great game, but is better accomplished as a team rather than a singular person.
If you've never tried the game, I recommend you give it a shot, it's loaded with entertainment, and you might just like it.

I don't have many things to say about the game that haven't been said already, and quite frankly, I don't feel like repeating others. Anyways, let's start with an initial presentation of the GAMEPLAY:
Team Fortress 2 is a first-person shooter developed by Valve that uses team-based cooperation heavily in its gameplay, providing 9 different classes that all play a distinct role. The Scout is a lightweight class that is used for flanking and, as such, is most beneficial to be directed through secondary paths, such as to surprise the enemy. The Soldier is an "average" class that doesn't have many downsides. The versatility it provides makes it a "swiss maggot knife". The Pyro is usually devised as a harrassing class, dealing damage with afterburn to weaken the enemies. There's a character limit to the review, so I'll speed it up. The Demoman uses traps to prevent the enemy team from advancing. The Heavy is  a sort of "walking sentry" that acts as a wall between the enemy and the objective, being able to deal tremendous amounts of damage. Well,♥♥♥♥♥♥ I ran out of space, so I leave you all with a warm hug and a friendly goodbye. 10/10 nice game

To put it bluntly, I really enjoy Team Fortress 2. I am adicted to it. To be honest to anyone whos thinking of gettting it (Baring in mind its free :P) I'd say go for it. One, its super fun and original in the way it presents its wepons and Playable Characters. Also Once you start playing, you wont be able to stop! Trust me, I've tried to play another game. Then just 10 minutes later I get bored and Team Fortess is the only game that apeals to me at the momment. Plus all of it's video's to help make the game more popular than it already is really bring the TF2 experience to life. To be fair, its different in that concept. Most RPG or shooter MMO's dont care to much about giving us a full briefing of the characters were playing, so its kind of a mystrey we have to figure out ourselves. If only other games gave a whole life to each playable character they introduce to us. Or atleast tell us a little bit about themselves, like how they got that scar (the snipers story) or how the medic uber charges people (The medic's story) It really is'nt one of those "Typical" games you only play once or twice and it has no replay value. Valve have done a splended job here. I rate it 9/10. I now think im in the mood for some Team Fortress 2 now. Huh, funny that eh?

is a "Free to Play", Multiplayer, First Person Shooter (FPS), and a Hat (Cosmetic) Simulator.
A very fun game. Especially, very addictive and good for relaxation, but it depends how good you are at the game or on your picked class.
There're about 9 classes in the
: [Offensive Classes:] Scout, Soldier, Pyro, [Defensive Classes:] Demoman, Heavy (Weapons Guy), Engineer, [Support Classes:] Medic, Sniper and Spy.
Each class has it's own strength and weakness. For example, Spy has a low health, but he can kill can instantly by backstabbing you.
TF2 has 2 teams: BLU and RED. They hate each other, and they attack each other. Nothing interesting.
Maps can be different (pretty obvious). But unfortunately, maps can affect the gameplay, because like I said before, each class has it's own weakness. For example, Sniper can kill you pretty easily in a very wide map, and you can get annoyed.

You don't need them to play a game. Players usually care so much about cosmetics, because they want to look good and feel good, while they play a game. Most of them, spend about $500 on the game, only because of the hats. Players also care about the "qualities" of the items. Some qualities can be very expensive, so I don't suggest to spend money on crap. However, hats are not the only ones. Players also waste money on weapons, due different qualities or reskins.
There are 2 different kinds of TF2 updates: Official Updates and Community Created Updates (they're official, too).
Well, it's pretty simple:
- Are created by the main creator/company called VALVe. In their updates, you can find new gamemodes, new weapons (which are usually made in the summer or in the winter), new maps, bug fixes and especially there is a 90% chance that VALVe is going to add new hats, made by the community from the Steam's workshop.
- VALVe usually cares what community makes, but they don't allow community mess with the balance of the game, meaning VALVe doesn't allow us to create new weapons, which can have different stats, and especially add new maps. (However, VALVe added community maps only in the beginning, when TF2 was still new and fresh. But now everything is different, because in nowadays TF2 became as a very popular game.)
So like I said before, VALVe actually cares what community creates. So VALVe likes to add new hats and new weapons (just models) created by some talented people from the community. But majority of the community hates to see, that every new update has a new hat. And to be honest: It's normal.
If you didn't know, there was a big over hyped update called "End of the Line", and it was actually the most useless update in the TF2. It had tons of cosmetics, a new taunt, a new weapon, which is a actually a reskin with no stats.
Before an update arrived, the community really hoped to see a map called "Snowplow" with the new gamemode, but when the update arrived, the map was canceled by VALVe. VALVe said, that the map
. Later, that sentence became as a
, because other maps made by VALVe are more confusing, than a "Snowplow".

However, in VALVe servers you may find a voting system, which allows any player to vote something. Here is a list current voting types:
So imagine again those 2 teams again: Imagine, that you joined the BLU team, and you see that the teams are not balanced at all, and whenever you come out of your base - you always die. So you decide to vote to "Scramble Teams".
The voting will fail, because your enemies are having fun AND because your teammates (noobs) doesn't know how to vote at all, or just completely ignores the voting.

Each player becomes a unique part of the glorious pandemonium of Team Fortress 2. All players have their style, their preferences, their good classes and their weaknesses, their habits and oddities. Each player has a weapon he treasures, a cloak he adores, and an opponent he fears.
To a first-time player, the battlefield seems an undistinguishable mess of rockets and bullets. An experienced player takes seconds to indentify key players, weak points, safe spots, important targets, and imminent threats.
Not every game manages to do this. Few games rise above fun to become a layered treasure trove of ridicule and tactic. But Valve, an unbelievable eight years ago, managed to make the most intimate, most adreninaline-fueled game of chess you will ever encounter.
Recommending this game is, of course, futile. Thousands have done so before me. I merely want to proclaim my hope that thousands will have the chance to do so in the future.

In TF2, the classes actually have variety, and actually appeal to different types of people. Also, they have their own personalities, which is always cool.
The drop system in the game is just perfect. Valve has mastered how to make successful free 2 play games. You can pay for weapons and (probably the most bought thing on this game) hats. But the random drops are sufficient enough that once you play for a while you will get good  weapons. And even the default weapons are still really good.
Overall this game is just one of the best Shooters out there. There is not one shooter that is on the market today, whether that be something like Battlefield or CoD or something like Planet Side 2, that feels like you're having more fun than TF2.

After playing Team Fortress 2 for a substancial amount of time, I think I can honestly say that is one of the most fun, addicting, and overall well-though-out multiplayer experiences I have ever been a part of. I mean I've played BIG franchises like Call of Duty: Black Ops and Battlefield 3, and sure they were fun for a while, but this game is relentless. Every time, there's always something new to experience, some other new thing to try out, keeping gameplay fresh.
The basics start with the classes. This is a class-based game, and goodness it knows it. None of the nine classes are even remotely alike, but all are incredibly important to victory in any of the gamemodes offered - payload, control points, and king of the hill just to name a few. The reason being is that they are all balanced meticulouslyso that nothing is overpowered or underpowered: either its strength also being its weakness or its reliance on teammates for survival or being a jack of all trades. And it's this mentality, for instance as there are also many others, that provides diversity in the game and keeps you on your toes.
This game is also very colourful, despite the gore and rolling heads. Each class is also a character, not simply a faceless soldier in the battlefield, and you grow to love them. I recommend searching the "Meet the Team" videos online, also made by Valve, so that you can see just how hillarious they can be. As for art style, although you may be taken aback or, perhaps, even repulsed by it at first - Don't worry. The cartoon-ish way they decided to represent the universe seems a bit strange, but you get used to it or, if you're like me and you enjoyed watching cartoons as a kid, you will com to adore it.
There's also a sort of "economy" in the game. I know, it seems odd, but it's real. It's a bit complicated, and out of the scope of this review, so I simply recommend looking around. All you need to know from here is that players trade for various in-game cosmetics and reskins made over TF2's 7 YEAR LIFETIME, and have a good time while doing so. Yes, this is a completely player-instituted and maintained economy which actually has been going on for years now. It shows how dedicated this community is to this one game, and how much time many people have put into it, and that is incredible.
So to wrap it all up, tl:dr or whatever, Team Fortress 2 is a remarkable game. It has lived strong for many many years, and I hope that doesn't change, as to lose an incredible multiplayer experience such as this would be a sad shame.

After playing Team Fortress 2 for a substancial amount of time, I think I can honestly say that is one of the most fun, addicting, and overall well-though-out multiplayer experiences I have ever been a part of. I mean I've played BIG franchises like Call of Duty: Black Ops and Battlefield 3, and sure they were fun for a while, but this game is relentless. Every time, there's always something new to experience, some other new thing to try out, keeping gameplay fresh.
The basics start with the classes. This is a class-based game, and goodness it knows it. None of the nine classes are even remotely alike, but all are incredibly important to victory in any of the gamemodes offered - payload, control points, and king of the hill just to name a few. The reason being is that they are all balanced meticulouslyso that nothing is overpowered or underpowered: either its strength also being its weakness or its reliance on teammates for survival or being a jack of all trades. And it's this mentality, for instance as there are also many others, that provides diversity in the game and keeps you on your toes.
This game is also very colourful, despite the gore and rolling heads. Each class is also a character, not simply a faceless soldier in the battlefield, and you grow to love them. I recommend searching the "Meet the Team" videos online, also made by Valve, so that you can see just how hillarious they can be. As for art style, although you may be taken aback or, perhaps, even repulsed by it at first - Don't worry. The cartoon-ish way they decided to represent the universe seems a bit strange, but you get used to it or, if you're like me and you enjoyed watching cartoons as a kid, you will com to adore it.
There's also a sort of "economy" in the game. I know, it seems odd, but it's real. It's a bit complicated, and out of the scope of this review, so I simply recommend looking around. All you need to know from here is that players trade for various in-game cosmetics and reskins made over TF2's 7 YEAR LIFETIME, and have a good time while doing so. Yes, this is a completely player-instituted and maintained economy which actually has been going on for years now. It shows how dedicated this community is to this one game, and how much time many people have put into it, and that is incredible.
So to wrap it all up, tl:dr or whatever, Team Fortress 2 is a remarkable game. It has lived strong for many many years, and I hope that doesn't change, as to lose an incredible multiplayer experience such as this would be a sad shame.

Ah, Team Fortress 2. This game is a first-person shooter done RIGHT. It doesn't need yearly releases like CoD to be /amazing/. So, let's start, WHY is it amazing?
First things first, it's because it's free. 100% free. That means anybody on Steam can pick up this game ANYTIME. But oh-oooh, being free is merely what catches your attention.
TF2 consists of a war between RED and BLU, battling it out in whatever gamemode your playing; whether it being capturing control points or grabbing the opposite team's intel. THIS GAME IS ADDICTIVE. As you play, play, and play you get more and more bloodthirsty as you go continue and holy crap is killing people in this game both hilarious AND satisfying.
Oh, characters, you say? The characters consist of nine playable different mercenaries with three different categories; Offensive, Defensive and Supportive. Each and every class has their ups and downs. For example, the Scout is great for dodging bullets as well as escaping and grabbing intel, but has poor health and is easy to take down. Meanwhile, the Heavy is a powerhouse with his giant health, being able to take down enemies in mere seconds when locked on, but in turn is incredibly slow and thus makes him more vulnerable to the Sniper's headshots or the Spy's backstabs. But there's more. These characters aren't just bland with the personality of cardboard. No. These characters are hilarious on their own, each with different personalities ranging from the Soldier's loud-mouthed insults towards all countries other than America to the drunken Scottish mumbles of the Demoman. Aside from these nine classes, you'll be introduced to NPCs such as your administrator Helen or the CEO of Mann Co., Saxton Hale.
The gamemodes are amazing. Like I said previously, Control Points involve a team seeking out the control points scattered across the map as they try to claim them as theirs while the opposite team has to stop them while King of the Hill is similar in the aspect of capturing control points, only this time both teams are trying to capture one giant control point in the middle of the map. Capture the Flag is about entering the enemy's base and capturing their intel, before quickly bringing it back to your own. Payload involves a team pushing a cart across the map attempting to deliver it to the enemy's base to blow it up while the enemy tries to stop you. And then there's Mann vs. Machine, which involves you and five other people teaming up to destroy AN ARMY OF ♥♥♥♥ING ROBOTS.
One of the best features is the Workshop, which allows users to create and submit creations of their own which may be incorporated in the game, whether it be full-on weapons or cosmetics to make your character look swaggy.
Overall, this game is definitely worth the zero dollars it steals from you. It is a fun game, free of charge, with great replayability, enjoyable gamemodes, a diversity of classes, and brilliant cosmetics to wear, I'm actually going to give Team Fortress 2 a 10/10.

Even without buying every hat in the store, this game can be great. Random drops help avoid paying players having too big of an advantage over free players, the game has a good pace, and the replayability is nigh-endless.
The classes are fun to toy with; if someone finds a certain class unwieldy or undesirable for their play style, they have 8 more to choose from; Fast-pace gamers can try the scout, Stealth/strategy-gamers can play the spy, Berserkers can use the heavy, etc.
The game modes are wonderful, and just as diverse as the characters themselves; payload maps, control points, capture-the-flag, even medieval swordfights.
The game's light humor is also worth a mention; things such as chunking jars of urine at people, being totally fooled by a dude in a cardboard mask, spycrabbing, all par for the course.
Though I can see how it can eventually get a bit repetitive, the game is a large amount of fun nonetheless, and maybe even because of its repetitive nature. There's just something almost hypnotising about the endless race to the finish, everyone always huddled around a tiny spot (be it a bomb rolling slowly down the tracks or a king-of-the-hill circle), the constant unrelenting bulletstorm, slapping people around with a fish, the fun goes on for hours.
It's alright.

Ahh, good old TF2. Before i found this game, i was mostly a console gamer, only going on my pc to play games like Terraria and Minecraft but this game opened a whole new genre of games that i never really knew was there. It combines the action and tense feel of Call of Duty, while at the same time captures the humour of a game like portal and through every hard time in my life, this game was always there to cheer me up with the wonderful and co-operative community never failing to make me smile. Servers dedicated to trading and some are just chat room esque servers that you can join and loose hours on.
One thing I hate with a passion about TF2, is that valve barely add any weapons anymore because they make way more money selling virtual hats that appear in new crates that you have to pay so much money for. If you looked on the workshop right now you would probably see up to 5 weapons that are top rated on the workshop and I know Valve have to check if the weapon is O.P or not and think of names, but come on valve. In the past 5 updates they have added 14 new weapons which may seem like alot, but if you factor in the frequency of these updates (22/12/14 for Smissmas 2014, and 20/12/13 for Smissmas 2013 -only 3 updates in between these in 2014-) and also the fact that 6 are only reskins, it equals 8. 8 new weapons in a whole year (not including festive reskins) and how many hats were added? Oh yeah, 178.
Now for the game mechanics. There are nine classes you can choose from. The scout, the soldier, the pyro, the demoman, the heavy, the engineer, the medic, the sniper and the spy. The scout is a fast moving class that runs faster than any of the other classes and captures points/pushes payloads at twice the speed of any other class but has low health. He has a scattergun, a pistol and a bat for his regular loadout but can change his secondary weapon to a can of pop, and can also change his melee (bat) to a fish. The soldier has a rocket launcher, a shotgun and a shovel to start with and can take out big groups of enemies with the explosion from his rocket launcher. There is also a cool mechanic for the soldier where you can aim you rocket launcher at your feet and fly up into the air! There is also a whole loadout dedicated to this technique. He is also slower than most other classes. The pyro has a flamethrower, shotgun and axe when he starts and can also push people away with his/her 'airblast' from his/hers flamethrower. The demoman shoots pill looking explosives and has a grenade launcher, sticky bomb launcher and a bottle for his melee. Similar to the soldier he has a lot of different tactics associated with him and can use a shield to travel faster than the scout for a second and slice the enemies with his sword/bottle. He can also be jolted into the air by his sticky grenades. The heavy has a minigun, shotgun and fists when he starts but can change his shotgun into a sandwich and his fists into bear claws or brass knuckles. This class moves incredibly slow but with the help of some items (Gloves of running urgently) can move faster (the speed of a pyro) when equipped. The engineer can create sentry guns which automatically scan for enemies and shoot at them without the need for you to be around but it can run out of ammo or lose health so you have to use your wrench. This depletes your amount of scrap metal which you get from ammo boxes, weapons on the ground and other broken sentry guns. He can also build teleporters for fast travel and dispensers to give you health and scrap metal. The medic has a medigun which fires a beam that heals anyone you click on and you can fill up an 'ubercharge' meter which, when full, grants you and the person you are healing, immunity for a short period of time. The sniper has a sniper and finally, the spy has a knife, a revolver and a cigarette holder which is secretly a disguise kit. The disguise kit allows you to look like a class on the enemy team and use your knife to backstab any enemies which is an instakill unless they are ubercharged or are a sniper and have a razorback.
Mann VS Machine is a gamemode added back in 2012 where you and a group of 5 other people attempt to stop robot versions of your classes from taking a bomb to the hatch in the back of the map you are playing. You can buy upgrades to increase your chance of surviving the waves so it is basically like a 3D tower defense with different classes and weapons. Even though the gamemode can become repetitive after a while, it is always good to come back to after a while.
Even though the game has just become a ploy for money by Valve, it is still extremely fun and i would recommend it to anyone who would like to ruin their social life by playing this game too much.

Woah woah whoa! I should explain myself before I get pelted with rancid sandviches. Tf2 is not a bad game, however, it IS a game that I can't enjoy for the life of me. I've never liked the FPS genre and this is a fresh entry to this over saturated and bland genre. That said, I still hate it.
Let's start off with some pros
-Graphics still hold up
-F2P
-ERMAHGERD MvM IZ AMAZE-BALLZ
-So many items!!!
-Unique and diverse gameplay
-TRADING=BLISS
-Ungodly amount of items
-addictive af
-Has its own economy.....WHAAAA??!!
Yes, it is enjoyable sometimes. Everyone already knows this so what's the point in this review?
Nah, that's it, I'm out, wrap it up!
*Door closes*
*Door opens*
Ok now let's do this! Why do I have problems with this game?
First off, the community. Most people in TF2 rival that of LoL and CS:GO. That said not all are bad, but the majority are rude, F2P shaming, weapon shaming, trolling, harassing, hacking, or scamming people. I am not a F2P. I actually used to have an unusual with pro ks but I sold those to buy much better games.
The weapons are NOT balanced. The gunslinger, any engie primary, the bfb, the phlog, the wrangler, the powerjack, THE ********* AIRBLAST, anything that manipulates motion, all one-hit kills, the black box, the spies revolver, ECT. are all annoying and OP. Does that mean I don'y use some of them? No. But it does mean I don't feel justified when get a kill or get killed with one. You may just say "git gud skrub" or "U just mad cuz bad" and I don't mean to brag but I beat Expert MvM and I top-score a majority of the time. I also used to be Comp(which is better) but I got sick of that. Yes you could argue that there is a counter for everything but most of the time you won't have that counter in that life and you might not even have the counter. THAT MAKES IT Pay2Win!!!!
On the other hand, there are a fair bit of TERRIBLE weapons, but I won't name them. CRITS ARE NOT I repeat ARE NOT balanced! I can be 1v1 with a scout of equal health and same weapons and I'll know I have the edge in skill, but he gets a lucky crit and I lose.
There is so much waiting in the game Some classes are boring to play anyway. With a game that gets so much praise for being so action-packed I was surprised how boring it was.
I could talk about every class and their flaws but I'd rather not waste your time any further.
So, is TF2 bad? NO. I actually enjoy it but it isn't as great as so many people say. It's like a mobile game. You don't play it and leave a masterpiece like Half-Life 2 or Portal dormant because it's a better game. You play it because it's addictive with enough fun and content to wash the hours away until you realized you have to go to work instead of progressing your world-wide conquest in the newest open-world game. Did I enjoy the TF2 session? Marginally, yes, but not as much as I would so many other games.
Also, THE HITBOXES??!!!?!?! WHAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA???!!!

This game is one that I find my coming back to and for a good reason. Though it can seem simple, the way Team Fortress 2 is set up means you can play so many different ways with the nine classes that is is hard to get board of it.
