Ahh, good old TF2. Before i found this game, i was mostly a console gamer, only going on my pc to play games like Terraria and Minecraft but this game opened a whole new genre of games that i never really knew was there. It combines the action and tense feel of Call of Duty, while at the same time captures the humour of a game like portal and through every hard time in my life, this game was always there to cheer me up with the wonderful and co-operative community never failing to make me smile. Servers dedicated to trading and some are just chat room esque servers that you can join and loose hours on.
One thing I hate with a passion about TF2, is that valve barely add any weapons anymore because they make way more money selling virtual hats that appear in new crates that you have to pay so much money for. If you looked on the workshop right now you would probably see up to 5 weapons that are top rated on the workshop and I know Valve have to check if the weapon is O.P or not and think of names, but come on valve. In the past 5 updates they have added 14 new weapons which may seem like alot, but if you factor in the frequency of these updates (22/12/14 for Smissmas 2014, and 20/12/13 for Smissmas 2013 -only 3 updates in between these in 2014-) and also the fact that 6 are only reskins, it equals 8. 8 new weapons in a whole year (not including festive reskins) and how many hats were added? Oh yeah, 178.
Now for the game mechanics. There are nine classes you can choose from. The scout, the soldier, the pyro, the demoman, the heavy, the engineer, the medic, the sniper and the spy. The scout is a fast moving class that runs faster than any of the other classes and captures points/pushes payloads at twice the speed of any other class but has low health. He has a scattergun, a pistol and a bat for his regular loadout but can change his secondary weapon to a can of pop, and can also change his melee (bat) to a fish. The soldier has a rocket launcher, a shotgun and a shovel to start with and can take out big groups of enemies with the explosion from his rocket launcher. There is also a cool mechanic for the soldier where you can aim you rocket launcher at your feet and fly up into the air! There is also a whole loadout dedicated to this technique. He is also slower than most other classes. The pyro has a flamethrower, shotgun and axe when he starts and can also push people away with his/her 'airblast' from his/hers flamethrower. The demoman shoots pill looking explosives and has a grenade launcher, sticky bomb launcher and a bottle for his melee. Similar to the soldier he has a lot of different tactics associated with him and can use a shield to travel faster than the scout for a second and slice the enemies with his sword/bottle. He can also be jolted into the air by his sticky grenades. The heavy has a minigun, shotgun and fists when he starts but can change his shotgun into a sandwich and his fists into bear claws or brass knuckles. This class moves incredibly slow but with the help of some items (Gloves of running urgently) can move faster (the speed of a pyro) when equipped. The engineer can create sentry guns which automatically scan for enemies and shoot at them without the need for you to be around but it can run out of ammo or lose health so you have to use your wrench. This depletes your amount of scrap metal which you get from ammo boxes, weapons on the ground and other broken sentry guns. He can also build teleporters for fast travel and dispensers to give you health and scrap metal. The medic has a medigun which fires a beam that heals anyone you click on and you can fill up an 'ubercharge' meter which, when full, grants you and the person you are healing, immunity for a short period of time. The sniper has a sniper and finally, the spy has a knife, a revolver and a cigarette holder which is secretly a disguise kit. The disguise kit allows you to look like a class on the enemy team and use your knife to backstab any enemies which is an instakill unless they are ubercharged or are a sniper and have a razorback.
Mann VS Machine is a gamemode added back in 2012 where you and a group of 5 other people attempt to stop robot versions of your classes from taking a bomb to the hatch in the back of the map you are playing. You can buy upgrades to increase your chance of surviving the waves so it is basically like a 3D tower defense with different classes and weapons. Even though the gamemode can become repetitive after a while, it is always good to come back to after a while.
Even though the game has just become a ploy for money by Valve, it is still extremely fun and i would recommend it to anyone who would like to ruin their social life by playing this game too much.

Flee. Do not download this well-balanced, constantly-updated shooter. Return to where you came.
Hours will go by in a blink of an eye. The game is constantly dropping new weapons for you to toy with, forging a play-style that's all your own, whether it is the infamous Phlog Pyro, the combat Engineer, or the Demoknight. Each new weapon has its advantages and disadvantages, so choose your weapons wisely.
The achievement system will drain your soul from you. You will spend hours attempting to grind up some achievements for the additional weapons it gives you. Some achievements are specificly made to reward longer playtimes (such as obtaining a total of one MILLION healing points as a medic) and cater to those who like a bit of gratification for their hard efforts.
The TF2 community is varied and incredibly complicated. Many servers have made modified the game's mechanics for a more interesting experience - a x10 server will show you the overpowered potential your weapons can become; a Randomizer server will force you to adjust your playstyle based on whichever weapons have been given to you, ranging in usefulness or absurdity.
Customization will drag you deep within the confines of the trading community. The occasional hat drop will encourage you to customize your character to forge your own identity. TF2's economic system is based around metal, keys, and earbuds - containing the qualities of good currency. On trade servers you will see dedicated individuals, peddling their wares in an attempt to make a profit. The coveted Unusual hats, or limited-availability items (Big Kill, Max's Head, ect.)
The game's visual design is bright and colorful, and the various classes each have their own individual personalities, expressed in their Meet the Team videos and their in-game quotes. Each class offers a unique play-style, with different statistics and special abilites to ensure that it can be difficult at times to find yourself bored.
The game looks generally great, even on the lowest graphical setting. It's aged well and has been polished to near-perfection. Most computers should have little to no difficulty running it.

TF2, lol! A fun and addicting game, to be sure. Ok, so TF2 has been out for quite a while. But whereas other games die off or become cult favorites, this game perseveres and endures the test of time; not just because it is a fun game, but because of the unique weapons and other items that you can either buy off the in game Steam store, or craft yourself with components you break down from items you come across. And unlike most other games out there, where you have to spend money to actually get better stuff to be able to compete with others, the better stuff in this game comes with drawbacks to balance things out, so as to prevent people who don't spend money to play, leave because they can't really compete with the people who do have said uber powerful stuff.  More often than not (there are a few exceptions), the default weapons and items are better than having their upgraded counterparts. Where Steam really makes their money is on accessories (glasses, clothing, etc). I can tell you that there are some accessories I'd love to have, but as they are only cosmetic and have no benefit other than looking good in game, it's really not worth to me, to spend your hard earned money purchasing these items. If I'm going to spend my money on in game items, it has to benefit the way i play the game, and not just for the classes i play to really look good and show off.
All that having been said, there is however a downside to this game, as there are a LOT, and i really mean a LOT of immature kids that play this game. To give you a good example, I was in a group of people in the Man vs. Machines (MvM) game mode, and this kid (who sounded like he's no older than 7 or 8) came on voice chat and would not shut up even after being asked very politely to do so. It took having to call a vote to kick him to resolve the situation; which is when the match went by much more smoothly, and more efficiently after that. So be prepared, if getting this game, as you will come across more than your fair share of people that make you wanna shake your head, sigh, and be like "ugh!".
Is this game worth getting? Yes, it sure is. It's free, is a fun distraction from the everyday hassles of life, and has little graphics requirements to where pretty much anybody can play it without having to purchase a new graphics card (or computer for that matter).

Like in Team Fortress Classic Team Fortress 2 has nine character classes: Spy, Pyro, Soldier, Heavy, Medic, Sniper, Demoman, Scout and Engineer. Each class' abilities on the battlefield have been streamlined, which, along with the graphics, is what makes Team Fortress 2 so much more accessible than TFC. No longer do you have Engineers running around with railguns and EMP grenades. Medics can't "infect" the other team, Spies don't have tranquilizer darts, and none of the classes have hand grenades.
In TF2, each class has roughly three main ways of attacking - a primary weapon (the Heavy's minigun, Pyro's flamethrower, Engineer's sentry gun, etc.) and secondary (various classes have shotguns, others pistols, while the Demoman has a highly effective mine thrower) and melee weapons (the Scout's bat, the Medic's bonesaw, and so on). Though classes now possess fewer means of attacking, the resulting gameplay feels much more focused. Each class has a very clearly defined role and the means to ensure they perform successfully. The only limiting factor is, of course, how effectively your team meshes together.

After about a year of playing I could you that this a very good Free to play game, there is so much chaos and fun happening on the screen that I got sucked into it the second my friend showed it to me, the classes each have a different and funny personality and the map designs are done pretty smoovely  and are very understandable enough to get by.
the gameplay is fast, action packed and generally fun. (Although each class plays differently so you'll ether find your own way to play each class yourself or find a youtube tutorial online, Personally if your a new player it'd suggest soldier as a class since his gameplay is basically the easist to learn how to play as.)
The tutorial mode is decent enough that you'll find out the basics, but that's really about it, so you will have to play a few practice rounds to figure each class out.
But of course for everything, there are problems, but I only ran into about 3 of them.
1.Updates: If you are a person who loves updates for Guns,Maps,Gamemodes,etc.... your not gonna run into it here, because there is has been no major updates for a while...(Unless you want BONUS DUCKS.)
2.Matchmaking: I found that the matchmaking in Team Fortress 2 is not terrible, but its not the best ether, there are no servers for new players so you'll find yourself confused on what to do or where to go.
The Mann vs Machine Gamemode is a little better but if you decide to pay for a mannup ticket, beware, there are people that WILL boot you just beacuse you haven't done any tours of duty.
3.Community. The Team Fortress 2 community is very nice one.... I just haven't meet them yet, you'll find that alot of people don't use the chat system at all, if they are using it, they are ether:
3.1: Spamming music or a really annoying sound
3.2: spamming really rude comments with their own key binding
3.3:that some people will spam key bindings so you won't know if a Spy is actually behind you or if they are telling you to move your gear up to the front lines if you're an Engineer.
3.4 Or are just being plain up Dbags to you and your team.
(But don't worry, there some really nice people that call out spys behind you, tell you to go when their uber is ready, and generally after a game people will say "GG" (Which basically means "Good Game")
3.5: And the last thing, the trading requests.... for me where so ANNOYING that once I saw one in a game, I just turned the chat off all together.
So to sum it up into a sentence, Team fortress 2 is a great party game to just get a few friends on Steam and have just have a generally good time, but the the bad things i mentioned could get under your skin so be careful, even though youtubers like Star_ and Jerma985 make it look fun, it's a totally different story once you, yourself start playing it, but hey, that's just my opinion.

At the time of writing this, I have about 450 hours in the game. It's a very strategic game, and each weapon has its use for the current situation.
Team fortress 2 is a really interesting experience. There is a competitive atmosphere, so if you want to join competitively (and make money if you are good) then there's that. But it's not all competition, there are tons of other things to do in the meantime.
TF2 is amazing because of the lovely modding community and what it brings to the table. There are hundreds of weapons, each of them performing an action relative to the current situation. With 9 classes that are each very balanced and very powerful if used correctly, the game never gets stale. Mix that in with the frequent updates, hundreds of mods, about 20 default game modes, lots of modded gamemodes, on any one of thousands of an ever expanding selection of maps, and you have so much variety.
I never liked cs:go so maybe i'm bias, but I can't help but feel that TF2 requires more skill to be proplerly good at, and it's more rewarding too. CS:GO might be more competitive because of the one-life system and limited set of weapons, but TF2 has a lot of content that takes more time and effort to master. Aside from that, i simply think it's much more fun because I take risks and die, without fear of sitting out the rest of the round.

At the time of writing this, I have about 450 hours in the game. It's a very strategic game, and each weapon has its use for the current situation.
Team fortress 2 is a really interesting experience. There is a competitive atmosphere, so if you want to join competitively (and make money if you are good) then there's that. But it's not all competition, there are tons of other things to do in the meantime.
TF2 is amazing because of the lovely modding community and what it brings to the table. There are hundreds of weapons, each of them performing an action relative to the current situation. With 9 classes that are each very balanced and very powerful if used correctly, the game never gets stale. Mix that in with the frequent updates, hundreds of mods, about 20 default game modes, lots of modded gamemodes, on any one of thousands of an ever expanding selection of maps, and you have so much variety.
I never liked cs:go so maybe i'm bias, but I can't help but feel that TF2 requires more skill to be proplerly good at, and it's more rewarding too. CS:GO might be more competitive because of the one-life system and limited set of weapons, but TF2 has a lot of content that takes more time and effort to master. Aside from that, i simply think it's much more fun because I take risks and die, without fear of sitting out the rest of the round.

If you dont want your soul anymore, just sell it to this game. Honestly, it really needs it, considering how many people have been quitting the game, because of the recent lack of effort Valve has been putting into it.
Though, that does not mean it's a bad game! Far from it, actually! In fact, most of the negative reviews are from people who even state that they love the game, just not the state that it's in right now... and the people with 0-5 hours who just complain that they can barely run the game because of their crappy computer. If Valve stopped focusing on Dota and VR for one second, they could probably make a really good update that could change TF2 for the best! Even with all of the lazy and horrific updates recently, such as Meet Your Match, it still comes out to be one of my favorite and most played games of all time, and for a good reason!
The action-packed gameplay and massive amount of variety this game has only scratches the surface of it all! It has an amazing and active community, that can actually come up with better ideas than Valve themselves, an astonishing amount of customizable options, a huge assortment of maps, not including the community-made ones, and even crazy strategies and tricks, that don't simply require pressing e or shift, such as trimping, rocket jumping, and trickstabbing! Ever wanted to be a fat Russian man cosplaying as Street Fighter's M. Bison while wielding a frying pan as a weapon? You can! Ever wanted to get drunk with aliens? You can! Ever wanted to chase people around as the Incredible Hulk? That's not in the main game, but that's what mods, like Freak Fortress are for!
TF2 is almost 10 years old now, and is still staying strong with over 40 million downloads, and new players each day. I've played this game for around 4 years now and it still hasn't grown on me! As new fps competitors join the video game industry, I, and many other die-hard fans will still consider TF2 to be the best of the best.
EDIT: Jungle Inferno was AMAZING, and yet another reason to get this game. TF2'S BACK, BABY (though, we still need competitive and matchmaking improvements...)

This game may be a bit old, but still has its charm. The cartoony style of this shooter and also the hats-system (developed by the Greece Minister of Finance) makes it unique. You can obtain the most ridiculous items (even a sandwich) while being in game, and the fun thing about it is that you can also pick up different primary weapons which have different (sometimes useful) effects. Furthermore the classes (from heavy to scout) are well balanced, I don’t have the feeling that one class outstands the other one in this game. However some classes might fare better on specific maps (for example, sniper on orange). The voices and videos of the characters are really funny and well ilustrated. My personal favourite class is the engineer, since I come from a rural area and also enjoy beer and play the guitar. The downside about this game is the Mann vs Machine game mode. It is quite fun to play, but to pay €0, 83 for every game just seems like playing blackjack in the casino. You don’t enjoy the game and the rewards you get are not worth the money you spent on completing the tour (although I was lucky and found an Australium sniper rifle on my 2nd tour on the two cities map). In my opinion they should make this game mode more affordable. Since this will increase the player amount on MvM servers and hopefully reduce the long loading times. Now only pro’s pay for this game mode and when you want to try this game mode as a newbie you will get burned down by all your teammates since you didn’t buy the right upgrades or equip the right weapons. You can’t blame these pro players (as they pay good money for this game mode) as for the MvM newbies (since they want to try out something new). I personally don’t like games which are built upon economic models, but bravo to Valve for setting up this brilliant trade system (from an economic perspective, off course). However this MvM mode is only a part of the game and as mentioned before the rest of this game is quite brilliant, so therefore I give it an 8 out of 10.

TF2 is a great little game that is a comic update of the classic Team Fortress (often called TFC). It is one of the better multiplayer games out there because it doesn't take itself too seriously and it has many different modes of play ranging from capture the flag to capture the point to pushing a payload to name a few. The maps are many and varied and often based on the best of TFC maps. The classes all have the ability to acquire by trade, random find, and purchase a variety of awesome weapons and tools that really expand the experience of players.
The game has some minor issues. The players are mostly cool people who don't cheat but you still get the occasional jerk and just plain offensive person who enjoys being racist or worse. Some classes are very frustrating to deal with when too many players use them at once, such as spies and demomen.
The biggest issue is that the connections can be quite unstable for the game. Nearly everyone will encounter systemic lag from time to time and it can be very frustrating to be playing with a 70 ping, suddenly have it soar to 250 and then even hit as much as 1000ms. You can have the best internet possible and the game will still lag like this from time to time. That said, it is remarkably playable even with high lag. I have still managed to kill many players with pings much lower than mine due to the game's mechanics.
Enjoy this game! It is worth it!

A breathe of fresh air on a rainy afternoon.  It's like running through the dessert, then tripping and falling only to land in the body of water called TF2.  A game that defies the need for perfect graphics and visuals to be "good."  It is almost as if God himself (should he exist) reached down and coded with his 7 hands this amazing game.  I find myself being able to play multiple (3) matches before getting bored.  Its like I just can't get enough.  You remember that day when you were less than a year old? Yeah that day.  Smiles all the time and little puffs of cheddar goodness.  That is life now. Replace those gerber cheddar puffs with Cheeto cheese puffs and you're the same kid all over again. Interacting with your cartoon entertainment on a saturday morning, shooting a holes in the face like the kid you are.  Lets face it, America's youth is troubled.  All kids want to shoot people in the face.  Can you blame them? Look at the world we live in.  I tell you what we need. A revolution of baby shooters practicing on TF2 to take back America.  Restore it to the constitutional ways of Abraham Lincoln (before he slayed vampires).  Bring back the values of our founding fathers.  Or Germany's founding fathers would be fine too. That kill all the Jews thing.  I love my mod on Left For Dead 2 where all the Zombies are Jews and the survivors are Nazis.  Thats some real life shiz right there. Have you ever had chocolate cake you didn't like? EXACTLY! So play this game.

TF2 is a great little game that is a comic update of the classic Team Fortress (often called TFC). It is one of the better multiplayer games out there because it doesn't take itself too seriously and it has many different modes of play ranging from capture the flag to capture the point to pushing a payload to name a few. The maps are many and varied and often based on the best of TFC maps. The classes all have the ability to acquire by trade, random find, and purchase a variety of awesome weapons and tools that really expand the experience of players.
The game has some minor issues. The players are mostly cool people who don't cheat but you still get the occasional jerk and just plain offensive person who enjoys being racist or worse. Some classes are very frustrating to deal with when too many players use them at once, such as spies and demomen.
The biggest issue is that the connections can be quite unstable for the game. Nearly everyone will encounter systemic lag from time to time and it can be very frustrating to be playing with a 70 ping, suddenly have it soar to 250 and then even hit as much as 1000ms. You can have the best internet possible and the game will still lag like this from time to time. That said, it is remarkably playable even with high lag. I have still managed to kill many players with pings much lower than mine due to the game's mechanics.
Enjoy this game! It is worth it!

Team fortress 2 has typically 12 people put on either team, both blue and red team.
Either team has the same options, the only difference being either one is defending and the other attacks (this principle does not apply to KOTH).
Each encounter is nothing like the last as the game is multiplayer only, the reason this occurs is due to the available selection of weapons, all of which vairy in their use and applicability. For example the ''Jarate'' for the sniper class replaces your SMG, removing a close quarters combat option, whilst the ''Jarate'' gives the sniper an opportunity to help with the team damage and get into the freigh, throwing his 'Jarate' on enemy players marks them for death, meaning they take more damage from yourself and allies.
The only gripe I have this game is that my friends don't play, after playing the newly released Overwatch I have come to respect the annoyences found within TF2 (Team Fortress 2 for short) such as an enemy Pyro walking toward you, continuously firing away with his flamethrower, burning you into smitherines. The reason I have come to this conclusion is due to some aggrovating enemy abilities but I digress.
Cosmetics, Collectables - there all here, with many items to collect spanning in rarity and quality you will foreseably never finish your collection but thus the ignorance goes, I vouch for this dilema.
The game also gets pretty regular updates in my opinion, and you will recieve the contents of such game regardless of weither or not you have purchased a premium account.
As you can tell by my hours I have played this game a considerable amount, heck since I was 12 and I'm turning 17 in a few months. If that doesn't awake your interest then nothing will.
Sidenote: Playing this game with friends is hands down the best multiplayer F2P (Free to play) game experience out there, and if there is better, I haven't heard of it.
In short TF2 is an extremely thrilling, inspiring and joyous multiplayer game with many new things to experience and items/cosmetics to collect.

A masterpiece by Valve. Best free to play game on Steam. You don't need the best of the best gaming pc to play TF2. TF2 combines a fast-paced experience of smooth FPS gameplay, memorable characters, an evergrowing community, and and new store items, cosmedics and weapons consistantly being added on to the game. Graphics are not the powerhouse in TF2, but that is ok, since Valve purposefully does so for that good old cartoony look, and so that anyone could play it without spending so much money on their computer. But what makes this game truly special is definetly its character classes. No other FPS game will ever be able to recreate classics such as Scout, Spy, Heavy or Demoman, etc. Unique modes where one team pushes the kart while the other team tries to neutralize, to classic FPS modes such as capture the flag are also included. However, it can be quite a challenge for early/new players. Be prepared to die ALOT, since your skills in other FPS games such as COD, Halo, or Killzone won't carry over. But Valve sure does a good job in keeping the gameplay fresh with the Steam workshop capability, where you can vote on which items from the workshop you would like to see next in the game!
Pros: Fast paced gameplay, memorable characters, unique game modes, TF2 store
Cons: Challenging for beginner players

But what makes this game truly special is definetly its character classes. No other FPS game will ever be able to recreate classics such as Scout, Spy, Heavy or Demoman, etc. Unique modes where one team pushes the kart while the other team tries to neutralize, to classic FPS modes such as capture the flag are also included. However, it can be quite a challenge for early/new players. Be prepared to die ALOT, since your skills in other FPS games such as COD, Halo, or Killzone won't carry over. But Valve sure does a good job in keeping the gameplay fresh with the Steam workshop capability, where you can vote on which items from the workshop you would like to see next in the game!
Pros: Fast paced gameplay, memorable characters, unique game modes, TF2 store
Cons: Challenging for beginner players

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play, though lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes to choose from: the Scout, the Soldier, the Pyro, the Demoman, the Heavy, the Engineer, the Medic, the Sniper and the Spy. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow each to fill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or better skill levels.
There are two official modes of play: player versus player, also known as Multiplayer, and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objectives for both teams to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co. Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play. I have been playing since 2013 and I still return to the game on a regular basis.

This game is the official logo of steam.
No matter where you go, you will always find something TF2 related on steam.
This game is fun in every aspect. From the hilarious classes to the amazingly stupid GMod videos, and dramatic and awe-inspiring SFM movies.
This F2P game has by far sucked more time out of anyones life than any other game on Steam of the same type.
I'll start with the classes. Each of the 9 classes has a specific personality that define who they are, where they came from, and how they are. You have the scout, The beat-em-up boston boy, The Soldier, The Crazed stereotypical american, The heavy, The obese, hilarious fool, and i can keep on going and going.
Gameplay wise, if you want a fun competitive game to play this is definitely the game for you. You have 9 stock playstyles that you can play to get the most  basic gameplay. Then we get these things called drops, which you can acquire weapons from. If you change out the loadouts, which you can, you can make your playstyle more complex and comfortable to your needs, to give you a challenge or to give you a challenge and help your skill.
Then we get the economy. I swear this game teaches you economics by itself. The games economy runs off of metal, hats, cosmetics, and large arrays of items. If you dont become a Premium you sadly wont enjoy the full experience, but i highly suggest you do. I mean its only .99 cents to become a Premium anyway. Anyways, the economy runs nicely, and after a while, trading, scrapbanking, raffling etc, will be your life in this game aside from gameplay.
I could keep on going about the game but i'd be here for hours, so heres my TL;DR.
TL;DR.
This game is amazing in every aspect, from gameplay to videos. The economy is amazing, the weapons, classes, and overall everything is amazing. While there are exploits in the game, it is still easily one of, if not, the most popular game on the steam store that is free. I highly suggest you get the game, it IS free, and start playing. Trust me, you dont wanna miss out on this game!

KILL ME WITH SUPERIOR FIREPOWER. That's all I can say. I get slap-happy and stoopid with adrenaline playing this fragfest of a killing game. I am giddy among the rain of giblets. You'll be fragging jokers all day! You'll forget food. You'll forget showers. You'll forget to use the toilet. You will become a single-focus zombie mad murdering death machine, and you'll like it. Rrrraaaawwwwrrrr!!!!1!
Then, when it's all over, you will appreciate wee little kittens and otters and whatnot, docile as a flower.
Until next time.

Ive played this game for quite some time and had much fun in this game, it is quite original and a unique gem in the line of video games out there. For instance, I was walking around in Dustbowl and encountered an enemy pyro. Then astonishingly, he croutched down, pulled out an axe, and called me a "spy" in friendliness. I did the same except with a shovel. Being a new Tf2 player and never seeing this behavior before, I scrounged the voice command list for "spy". Upon completing my feat of seeking the correct word, we walked toward eachother slowly, legs crouched, and stared at eachother, spamming "spy". We did this for a few moments until one of my team mates (soldier) came waddling himself down towards me and the pyro. He stared at us both in confusion, the little ghost dangling off his gibus in the fresh dusty air, and shot a rocket at the pyro, sending his body flying many yards away. Upon seeing my first Tf2 ragdoll, I burst into tears crying with laughter as the pyro's body fell through the air and made the "squish" splat noise. Such a sight is unheard of in any other game and is quite common in this game. I am not a Tf2 fanboy, as I have grown up playing games like the Halo series my whole life since before I was 5, and playing CoD for a few years. I can easily say Halo is a very fun game, but that is another story. You will never find another experience like the ones you find in Tf2 nearly all the time every day, there is much laughter to have and enjoy in this game. 10/10 Is gud stuff. -Heavy

TF2 is a free to play game that doesn't give a premium members an advantage in gameplay. The stock weapons that are available to all players from the beginning of the game have no downsides or special stats and are techinally the best. free to play players can still get weapon drops but at a slower rate than the premium members. Premium members can get cosmetics from random drops, trade with other premium players, and unlock weapons at a faster rate than free to play players. You can become a premium member by making a purchase from the mann co store with items under 1 dollar. (any purchase makes you premium). TF2 is an enjoyable multiplayer FPS game for premium members and free members alike. With funny characters, addictive gameplay and the free updates that add new content to the game, this is a game that everyone on steam should at least try.

TF2. This is nearly the ultimate Free-To-Play game on Steam. Second only to Dota 2 in the number of users playing daily.
Why is it so popular? Let's take a look, shall we?
First off, the obvious: It's free. 100% free. This means its accessible to everyone on Steam. This is just the icing on the cake though. What really shines about TF2 is the game itself.
Team Fortress 2 usually consists of two teams (Red and Blue) going head to head against each other. Sometimes fulfilling certain objectives or just downright killing each other. There are many, many maps and modes, such as Payload, Capture Points, and Mann VS Machine. But the general idea no matter the map or mode is to KILL EVERYTHING THAT MOVES! And my god, is it fun to do so. The game has 9 playable mercenaries, each actually being a certain "class". Each class is divided into 3 different roles: Offense, Defense, and Support. Let's go over each role and class.
Offensive roles specialize in dealing damage to the opposing team. These are your main attack force. Scouts are the speedy hit and run class, with the ability to double or even triple jump depending on equipped items. Soldiers pack a bit more firepower with their rocket launchers, which gives them not only power, but mobility due to the ability known as "rocket jumping". The Pyro is great at setting the opposition on fire, as well as extinguishing burning teammates using an airblast.
Defensive roles serve to inhibit enemy access and to hold enemies back from vital points on the map. Overall, the defensive group has the most firepower of all the groups. Demomen can safeguard areas with stickybombs that they can detonate when enemies come by. Heavies are great for mowing down incoming troops and pushing back forces. Heavies can also keep enemies in an area while whittling their health for teammates to finish off. Engineers can build Sentry Guns for effective area defense, as well as build Teleporters and Dispensers for logistical support of the team.
Support classes cannot hold the fight on their own, but their specialized abilities can tip the balance in their team's favor. They offer the offensive and defensive classes an extra edge in battle and can help turn the tide of the game. Whether crippling the enemy advance from behind or keeping teammates healed, the support classes are always handy to have around. Medics are the team healers, capable of providing numerous buffs depending on their equipments. Spies are great for sneak attacks or eiliminating key threats. Snipers excel at long range, also eliminating key threats, as well as extinguishing burning teammates with jarate and providing a damage boost to teammates.
Next, let's look at the presentation.
TF2 has a very unqiue art style. It's somewhat cartoonish, but very appealing. It's simple, and un-complex. But it doesn't need to be complex. It's simplicity is it's strength. Everything is detailed enough to where you can easily tell whats going on, what a specific model or item is, and they all stand out. The soundtrack is also very appealing and catchy, especially the main theme. I personally have it as a ringtone/alarm tone on my smartphone! :)
One of the best aspects of TF2 is the Steam Workshop. Users can submit designs for items and weapons, and possibly have them added to the game! A very lucrative sub-market has also emerged from this game in the form of the Crate Keys. That's a whole different ballgame in and of itself, so we won't get into it here.
During normal gameplay on most servers, you can obtain random items, weapons, and sometimes crates, and taunts....through the item drops system. You can only receive so many drops per week, and you will get them randomly as you play. You can use these items and weapons to customise your mercenary's loadout, or you can use them to craft other items, hats, and weapons. You can take multiples of items and craft them into Scrap, then Reclaimed Metal, then Refined Metal. You can then use these metals to craft specific class weapons/items, among other things. The crafting system is simple yet robust, with lots of possiblities. Some of it is very luck based. You can take some very common items and end up crafting a super rare hat or gun worth a lot of moolah on the Steam Market!
All-in-all, Team Fortress 2 is just a very fun game. Endless entertainment awaits when you start up this game, especially if you play with friends on your favorite server. Probably the best free-to-play game on Steam.

Premium members can get cosmetics from random drops, trade with other premium players, and unlock weapons at a faster rate than free to play players. You can become a premium member by making a purchase from the mann co store with items under 1 dollar. (any purchase makes you premium). TF2 is an enjoyable multiplayer FPS game for premium members and free members alike. With funny characters, addictive gameplay and the free updates that add new content to the game, this is a game that everyone on steam should at least try.

NOTE: This review is not for casuals and/or people with lot of money, if you consiter yourself one or both, you will like this game.
Ahh Valve, what a wonderful company. An amazing spree of some of the greatest games out there on PC. With great series like Left 4 Dead, Half-Life, and Counter-Strike, it's hard to imagine them make a bad game. TF2 is a game Valve would love to wipe under the carpet, unless it was making them tons of money!
Seeing the previous Team Fortress' gameplay and screenshots the graphics in TF2 have somehow downgraded. I'm not a big graphics guy, but it seems strange to somehow get worse over time. I like to enjoy the games I play, and let's just say this game has become free to play for a reason.
TF2 is not competitive, I'd be lying if I told you it was. If you want to get any fun out of this game, take nothing seriously. This game
recognised by MLG, to put that in perspective, most if not all Call of Duty games are recognised. Like a majority of the Call of Duty games the online community is filled with hackers, about 1 in 15 people, to top that off there is also no reporting feature. unlike Call of Duty games there is no offline or singleplayer to escape the hackers. (Unless you count bots) Unlike almost every other halfway decent game no amount of practice in this will make you better at this game, thanks to the "random" system the in-game combat has.
New players will be astonished as their first few drops fall, items that is, not blood. It can be easy to think that different  weapons will make you better, and they will to an extent. Some players may try to convince you stock weapons are the best, almost all of which are not using stock weapons while telling you this. Not the case, better weapons require you invest time or, better for Valve, money.
They say money makes the world go around, and TF2 is no exception. Love that feeling you get from getting that "random" critical hit? You can smack the enemies away with your cash. This also works well with normal hits as the random number generator will tend to hit the higher numbers along with the game's profits.
Most game types are repetitive and involve some sort of objective of which the most powerful class, the Sentry, can be used to blow everyone away. For a game known for it's balanced gameplay there are a lot of things and classes that feel either useless or inferior.
Really there is very little fun to be had playing this game, which is why I give this game a solid no. Those that are giving this review a thumbs down at the moment are without a doubt hurt by the truth this review has given to potential new players of the game they spent thousands on to get a leg up in. Thanks for reading, and click that thumb up!
P.S. Despite all this, this game is still better than Overwatch.

This game is strange. It's many things; pretty, funny, stupid, intense, skilled, unbalanced, but mainly strange. Instead of following others or setting the bar for class based shooters, TF2 creates it's own bar  and shatters the expectations of what shooters can be. On a base level the game is clever: 9 classes going through various gamemodes that can actively counter eachother. Then on the basis 9 classes each class get MANY various weapons that can change their play styles completely, Like a class that's normally defensive can now go and dominate the front line. Beyond that each class has their own personality as oppose to various other shooters where you are just a plain soldier. This game also doesn't like to take it's self seriously with the various taunts and humor. It also has hats...What other shooter can let you do that? So now I can go around and mow down waves of enemies dressed as a ballerina. This game is great. definitely my favorite FPS.

I'm going to write a review about this game, because of how great it is.
First off, this game is like a sense of fresh air out of the window, a FPS in which allows you to customize your character, with items that you can find. and also, can we talk about how great the Maps, Classes, Weapons, and Items in the game and how detailed they are.
Second, the game has tons of great Classes
We have the Scout - A fast running class with a Scattergun, Pistol, and a Bat, he has the ability to kill a person from a close of distance with a Scattergun, if it runs out, switch to the pistol, and shoot until they have low health, then get the bat, and BONK! Them.
We have the Soldier - A USA Class, in which has a Rocket Launcher, A Shotgun, and a Shovel. Its a Great class, but its slow. their are many ways to boost him, with items. He's a great class for people who like to blow things up.
We have the Pyro - A dangerous human (If you can call him that) that has a Flame Thrower, a Shotgun, and a Axe. He is at Normal speed, and is very dangerous with the Flare Gun and the Sharpened Volcano Fragment. more things make him OP such as the Backburner which crits if the player is hit in the back. It always crits if that happens.
Next we have the Demoman - He has a crazy drinking problem, and he uses a Grenade Launcher, a Sticky Bomb Launcher, and a Bottle. He's a class in which is used for skill, and not just for attacking with, usually people use him with the Charge N Targe which makes it to where you can charge up and Speed very fast to others to get crits. Its a great class, and i would recommend only for Skilled players.
Next up, The Heavy - The big guns of the classes, he carries a Minigun, a Shotgun, and his own Fists. A Class that tries to protect the team from damaging points, like Soldiers, or Scouts, he usually is the best of the class, and eats a Sandvich LIKE A BOSS to gain health back. (The Sandvich is a item which you can get from a Achievement in which you have to get 10 Heavy Achievements.)
Next "Everyones Favorite" The Engineer - That lazy Scumbag of the team, He puts up sentries, and uses his Shotgun, Wrench, Pistol, and most importantly, The Construction PDA! everything used is required to be the best ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of the team, Sentries are built to the lvl 3 stage. and he can also build, teleporters, and Dispensers.
We have the Medic - the player in which heals the team from damage. He uses the Syringe Gun, The  Medi Gun, and the Bone Saw, to be a good medic, the medic isnt really a attack class, but i find it funny for people to use it as one.
Then we have the Sniper - That guy who pisses into a jar to throw it at enemies for crits, but seriously, Jarate is♥♥♥♥♥♥ in. a. jar! the Sniper is a class used for getting headshots, and getting kills from a far distance, he uses the Sniper Rifle, the smg, and the Kukri, and is the best class for some starters.
And last, we have the Spy - The one that sleeps with Scouts mother, Possibly. but the Spy is a person who likes to disquise as others to backstab them to death, he uses the Butterfly Knife, The Revolver, the Invis Watch, and ofcourse, The Sapper, and a disquise kit, he smokes, and can go invisable and disquise, what more do you want.

Welcome to Hat Fortress 2.9.
After 69 years in the making, hopefully it was worth the weight.

The Team Fortress Series pioneered the genre that we now know as the "Hero-Shooter", a class based game that revolves around cooperating using the different classes to attack/defend an objective. Need to Defend a point? Call your local engineer and hell set you up a nice sentry turret that will mow down anyone who gets in it's way. Of course such a devastating force has to have some sort of counter-play, and here comes your Spies to sap'em or your medics to God-Mode so you can get past it. This game has this type of flow that there is a always a class that is good to counter another one.
Valve always used to be pioneers, creating great games like Half-Life, Portal etc., but then they realised "Steam makes us a lot of money, so why should we care about making games anymore?".  So they simply started shuttting down one of their moneymakers and the updates started going down hill. Several major updates in a year started becoming stories of when Valve cared about this game. Now we are lucky just to get 1 in a year, but even then they just come out buggy, broken and so forth, they gives us things nobody asked for, instead of listening to their community.
Just to be clear i do realise of the minimal numbers of developers that the game has, and that is one more problem i have with Valve, their working structure. You see in Valve, employees are free to work on whatever they like, whenever they like. So naturally since Vive is the big thing one the block, everyone wants to be part of the next big thing! Leaving all their products behind, just to be outclassed by others in the market. As of recent, more and more "Hero-Shooters" started appearing, starting to outclass Team Fortress simply due to the worker numbers that they have. I know that people hate the "TF2 VS. OW" argument, but comparing both games in terms on content, Overwatch is completely destroying TF2. Why? Blizzard has over 100 people working on their game. Meanwhile Valve has only 10-13 people working.
Recently Valve announced their next game in 6 years, Artifact. Now this seems like a good thing right? Until you realise that is a Hearthstone esque-game, based on Dota 2. Now i don't have any problems against These types of games, only due to the fact that they are heavily based in RNG and just serve to grab some money, in Hearthstones case, it cashed in on World Of Warcraft, and now Artifact is cashing in on Dota 2. What does this have to do with tf2? Well, instead of caring about this game, Valve decides to make a cashgrab, but i hope with the backslash that people are giving them, i hope they open their eyes.
About the game itself, your biggest challenge is to just start playing. The tutorial is horrible, the default settings are horrible, and supposed "Matchmaking" that is supposed to pair you with "People of similar skill" is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, You can be rank 1 and get people from ranks 60-150. Valve does a horrible job at showing new players the more complex mechanics of the varying classes, such as rocket-jumping, sticky jumping, leaving them to get obliterated by vets with 2000 hours on this game. Unless you are ready to die a ridiculous amount of times or just surrender to the cancer-inducing idle servers, your gonna have a bad time. However! There is always a chance for you to get that perfect game, that game where the matchmaker actually works and gives you a balanced game, where teams fight tooth and claw for the objective, and that, that is one of most fun experiences you will ever have, the feeling of accomplishment when you finally get pass that nasty sentry nest, the feeling when you capture the objective 4 minutes into overtime, that feeling is amazing.
I don't reccomend this game, simply because of Valve. If they don't care about their game, why should I?

TF2. This is nearly the ultimate Free-To-Play game on Steam. Second only to Dota 2 in the number of users playing daily.
Why is it so popular? Let's take a look, shall we?
First off, the obvious: It's free. 100% free. This means its accessible to everyone on Steam. This is just the icing on the cake though. What really shines about TF2 is the game itself.
Team Fortress 2 usually consists of two teams (Red and Blue) going head to head against each other. Sometimes fulfilling certain objectives or just downright killing each other. There are many, many maps and modes, such as Payload, Capture Points, and Mann VS Machine. But the general idea no matter the map or mode is to KILL EVERYTHING THAT MOVES! And my god, is it fun to do so. The game has 9 playable mercenaries, each actually being a certain "class". Each class is divided into 3 different roles: Offense, Defense, and Support. Let's go over each role and class.
Offensive roles specialize in dealing damage to the opposing team. These are your main attack force. Scouts are the speedy hit and run class, with the ability to double or even triple jump depending on equipped items. Soldiers pack a bit more firepower with their rocket launchers, which gives them not only power, but mobility due to the ability known as "rocket jumping". The Pyro is great at setting the opposition on fire, as well as extinguishing burning teammates using an airblast.
Defensive roles serve to inhibit enemy access and to hold enemies back from vital points on the map. Overall, the defensive group has the most firepower of all the groups. Demomen can safeguard areas with stickybombs that they can detonate when enemies come by. Heavies are great for mowing down incoming troops and pushing back forces. Heavies can also keep enemies in an area while whittling their health for teammates to finish off. Engineers can build Sentry Guns for effective area defense, as well as build Teleporters and Dispensers for logistical support of the team.
Support classes cannot hold the fight on their own, but their specialized abilities can tip the balance in their team's favor. They offer the offensive and defensive classes an extra edge in battle and can help turn the tide of the game. Whether crippling the enemy advance from behind or keeping teammates healed, the support classes are always handy to have around. Medics are the team healers, capable of providing numerous buffs depending on their equipments. Spies are great for sneak attacks or eiliminating key threats. Snipers excel at long range, also eliminating key threats, as well as extinguishing burning teammates with jarate and providing a damage boost to teammates.
Next, let's look at the presentation.
TF2 has a very unqiue art style. It's somewhat cartoonish, but very appealing. It's simple, and un-complex. But it doesn't need to be complex. It's simplicity is it's strength. Everything is detailed enough to where you can easily tell whats going on, what a specific model or item is, and they all stand out. The soundtrack is also very appealing and catchy, especially the main theme. I personally have it as a ringtone/alarm tone on my smartphone! :)
One of the best aspects of TF2 is the Steam Workshop. Users can submit designs for items and weapons, and possibly have them added to the game! A very lucrative sub-market has also emerged from this game in the form of the Crate Keys. That's a whole different ballgame in and of itself, so we won't get into it here.
During normal gameplay on most servers, you can obtain random items, weapons, and sometimes crates, and taunts....through the item drops system. You can only receive so many drops per week, and you will get them randomly as you play. You can use these items and weapons to customise your mercenary's loadout, or you can use them to craft other items, hats, and weapons. You can take multiples of items and craft them into Scrap, then Reclaimed Metal, then Refined Metal. You can then use these metals to craft specific class weapons/items, among other things. The crafting system is simple yet robust, with lots of possiblities. Some of it is very luck based. You can take some very common items and end up crafting a super rare hat or gun worth a lot of moolah on the Steam Market!
All-in-all, Team Fortress 2 is just a very fun game. Endless entertainment awaits when you start up this game, especially if you play with friends on your favorite server. Probably the best free-to-play game on Steam.

This game is great, to put it simply. It has 9 well balanced and unique classes and many different weapons. Each weapon has both and upside and a downside so that no weapon is really overpowered, and weapons can do as little as give a bit of bonus damage for slower speed or completely change a class's play style. For example, I'll talk about the Demoman. The Demoman is a defensive class, having a grenade launcher that contains bouncing explosive projectiles and a stickybomb launcher which can be used to place remotely detonating bombs. The Demoman also has a bottle as a melee weapon. If the player wants, he or she can replace the stickybomb launcher with a shield. Shields give the Demoman the charge ability, which launches him in the direction he is facing. Shields give passive defenses, allowing the Demoman to survive longer. This completely changes the Demoman's play style, from a strategic defensive class to an offensive 'in your face' class.
After playing this game for a while, you will notice many people talk about overpowered classes and weapons, however that is not true. A class many people complain about is the Pyro. Its flamethrower can be constantly burning by holding M1, and people think of this as a class using no skill. However, any Pyro that doesn't instantly die is completely the opposite. The Pyro has an airblast ability allowing it to reflect projectiles. This makes the Pyro great against Demomen, since they can blow away sticky traps. The nature of the Pyro's flamethrower combined with afterburn damage also makes them great against Scouts, who are the fastest, have the lowest health, and are most effective at close range. But, because the Pyro is weak at medium and long range, most other classes can pick it off from afar. To counter this, Pyros have to be smart and take alternate routes and ambush. A weapon is made especially for this, called the Backburner. It does more damage from behind, at the cost of less airblasts. Another flamethrower for the Pyro, called the Degreaser, does less damage from pure fire, and relies on quick combos with weapons with its increased weapon switch speed.
One thing that makes this different from most FPS games is the Spy. The Spy does not rely on pure combat, more stealth and deception. The Spy can disguise as enemy players, turn completely invisible, and disable enemy sentry guns built by enemy engineers. The Spy can also instantly kill someone with his knife if he attacks from behind. A Spy makes gamemodes like Attack/Defense possible, stopping the enemy team from all becoming engineers and easily winning with many sentries. Every class has counters like this, some obvious and some more clever, and each person's unique set of weapons with their unique strategy make every game different.

The Team Fortress Series pioneered the genre that we now know as the "Hero-Shooter", a class based game that revolves around cooperating using the different classes to attack/defend an objective. Need to Defend a point? Call your local engineer and hell set you up a nice sentry turret that will mow down anyone who gets in it's way. Of course such a devastating force has to have some sort of counter-play, and here comes your Spies to sap'em or your medics to God-Mode so you can get past it. This game has this type of flow that there is a always a class that is good to counter another one.
Valve always used to be pioneers, creating great games like Half-Life, Portal etc., but then they realised "Steam makes us a lot of money, so why should we care about making games anymore?".  So they simply started shuttting down one of their moneymakers and the updates started going down hill. Several major updates in a year started becoming stories of when Valve cared about this game. Now we are lucky just to get 1 in a year, but even then they just come out buggy, broken and so forth, they gives us things nobody asked for, instead of listening to their community.
Just to be clear i do realise of the minimal numbers of developers that the game has, and that is one more problem i have with Valve, their working structure. You see in Valve, employees are free to work on whatever they like, whenever they like. So naturally since Vive is the big thing one the block, everyone wants to be part of the next big thing! Leaving all their products behind, just to be outclassed by others in the market. As of recent, more and more "Hero-Shooters" started appearing, starting to outclass Team Fortress simply due to the worker numbers that they have. I know that people hate the "TF2 VS. OW" argument, but comparing both games in terms on content, Overwatch is completely destroying TF2. Why? Blizzard has over 100 people working on their game. Meanwhile Valve has only 10-13 people working.
Recently Valve announced their next game in 6 years, Artifact. Now this seems like a good thing right? Until you realise that is a Hearthstone esque-game, based on Dota 2. Now i don't have any problems against These types of games, only due to the fact that they are heavily based in RNG and just serve to grab some money, in Hearthstones case, it cashed in on World Of Warcraft, and now Artifact is cashing in on Dota 2. What does this have to do with tf2? Well, instead of caring about this game, Valve decides to make a cashgrab, but i hope with the backslash that people are giving them, i hope they open their eyes.
About the game itself, your biggest challenge is to just start playing. The tutorial is horrible, the default settings are horrible, and supposed "Matchmaking" that is supposed to pair you with "People of similar skill" is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, You can be rank 1 and get people from ranks 60-150. Valve does a horrible job at showing new players the more complex mechanics of the varying classes, such as rocket-jumping, sticky jumping, leaving them to get obliterated by vets with 2000 hours on this game. Unless you are ready to die a ridiculous amount of times or just surrender to the cancer-inducing idle servers, your gonna have a bad time. However! There is always a chance for you to get that perfect game, that game where the matchmaker actually works and gives you a balanced game, where teams fight tooth and claw for the objective, and that, that is one of most fun experiences you will ever have, the feeling of accomplishment when you finally get pass that nasty sentry nest, the feeling when you capture the objective 4 minutes into overtime, that feeling is amazing.
I don't reccomend this game, simply because of Valve. If they don't care about their game, why should I?

This game is great, to put it simply. It has 9 well balanced and unique classes and many different weapons. Each weapon has both and upside and a downside so that no weapon is really overpowered, and weapons can do as little as give a bit of bonus damage for slower speed or completely change a class's play style. For example, I'll talk about the Demoman. The Demoman is a defensive class, having a grenade launcher that contains bouncing explosive projectiles and a stickybomb launcher which can be used to place remotely detonating bombs. The Demoman also has a bottle as a melee weapon. If the player wants, he or she can replace the stickybomb launcher with a shield. Shields give the Demoman the charge ability, which launches him in the direction he is facing. Shields give passive defenses, allowing the Demoman to survive longer. This completely changes the Demoman's play style, from a strategic defensive class to an offensive 'in your face' class.
After playing this game for a while, you will notice many people talk about overpowered classes and weapons, however that is not true. A class many people complain about is the Pyro. Its flamethrower can be constantly burning by holding M1, and people think of this as a class using no skill. However, any Pyro that doesn't instantly die is completely the opposite. The Pyro has an airblast ability allowing it to reflect projectiles. This makes the Pyro great against Demomen, since they can blow away sticky traps. The nature of the Pyro's flamethrower combined with afterburn damage also makes them great against Scouts, who are the fastest, have the lowest health, and are most effective at close range. But, because the Pyro is weak at medium and long range, most other classes can pick it off from afar. To counter this, Pyros have to be smart and take alternate routes and ambush. A weapon is made especially for this, called the Backburner. It does more damage from behind, at the cost of less airblasts. Another flamethrower for the Pyro, called the Degreaser, does less damage from pure fire, and relies on quick combos with weapons with its increased weapon switch speed.
One thing that makes this different from most FPS games is the Spy. The Spy does not rely on pure combat, more stealth and deception. The Spy can disguise as enemy players, turn completely invisible, and disable enemy sentry guns built by enemy engineers. The Spy can also instantly kill someone with his knife if he attacks from behind. A Spy makes gamemodes like Attack/Defense possible, stopping the enemy team from all becoming engineers and easily winning with many sentries. Every class has counters like this, some obvious and some more clever, and each person's unique set of weapons with their unique strategy make every game different.

This... this is the pinnacle of PC Gaming, and the most refined, polished, and smoothed out gameplay it features is not found anywhere else.
Oh... and its free.
Team Fortress 2 offers a massive plethora of gameplay options, unique styles, and 9 fine tuned and diverse classes, that each present their own thing on the battlefield. Each of the classes are truly completley different, and have lots of thoght and time put into them by Valve in order to be their own thing on the team based battlefield.
No longer do you have to play a faceless mute soldier that might as well be a clone, and be a class that might as well not even be its own thing. Team Fortress 2's classes all have unique and belivable personalities and backstory that goes far past what most would think goes into a Multiplayer only FPS game.
The map design of the game is also truly spectacular, with many different maps set in the 1968, that all have great layout, which suits the needs of all the classes, and provides the players with many  different strategies with which to play on said map. Maps also have extremley high fidelity and some of them look truly spectacular, with it being hardly noticible that the game is 8 years old.
The TF2 Community is great, with friendly players and a lust for trading. There is also lots of people playing the game, hardly any server you will find empty, and you can be sure to be able to get deals on any item you are buying or selling.
Now... here is the problem...
To be able to truly enjoy TF2 one needs a premium membership, which is achieved by buying anything from the Mann Co. store, and this membership lasts forever. Without said membership, players cannot trade, get certain weapons, and will be generally abused by other members of the community.
That is literally the only problem with TF2.
End of story get it now.

These hours are legit, I played this game a lot in the past to avoid some tragic stuff in real life. I was young and didn't really have my gaming consoles anymore because of my brothers and I had a really bad pc, which i still own. TF2 was one of the games i could play pretty well on this pc but with horrid graphics, but it was one of the more fun games I installed. I met some real cool and nice people on this game as well as people who i plan to keep by my side. The community back then was more humble compared to nowadays. You have competitive gamers who spam their bind keys with unfunny/gross jokes and very obnoxious people who are either yelling at you or telling you to do specific things to win the game. When really, it doesn't even matter if you win or lose. However, you also have those people who are really awesome and you may meet some nice friends along the way! Although you never know what kinda person you're going to meet on this game. In my honest opinion, if you want to have a game to just waste time on (and money) or just mess around with people you know (which is what I do now), this is perfect. Esspecially the mann vs. machine co-op. I mainly play that now. Although to me, the game lost its touch, update wise, and I moved onto other games.
I believe it's worth a shot to try it out but other than that, I'd keep it as a casual game. I don't think the competitive scene is worth getting into anymore because it's being flooded by crude people. Atleast from my experiance after over about 4+ years of playing it just got worse and worse. You will eventually be tied into drama even if you try to avoid it. You'll be more stressed than actually having fun, I'll tell you that!
Although in all seriousness, this game is losing its touch and probably isn't worth making it your main game MAINLY because the updates they've been releasing are becoming very dull and not as great as they used to be. BUT, it's a great game to just play to pass the time and have fun! All you'll really notice nowdays is...people really love to trade more than actually play. Living off as a free to play would be very tough and you'd need to be patient with items you would want, unless you got that MONEY! Hope this helps.

No matter what FPS game you play, you can thank Team Fortress for making it possible. The original Team Fortress was a free mod for Quake 1 that came out in 1996, and it forever changed FPS games. TF was the first game that really focused on class based team play. So many games follow that model now. Team Fortress 2 is not quite the same game as its 1996 incarnation. The game no longer has grenades, it has a slower pace, and at a competitive level, it actually requires teamwork to win. Team Fortress 2 has been out for over 3 years now and it is only growing in popularity. The competitive community is getting bigger, and it shows no signs of slowing down. If you are looking for a fun FPS with lasting appeal, Team Fortress 2 is for you.

I like this game. Honestly, for all my complaints about it, I really and truly love this game. But, it's a sinking ship. Now, don't get me wrong, there's a lot good with it. Tons of ways to play, loads of weapons, hundreds of maps, and it's easy enough to learn. On the other hand though, it has it's fair share of issues.
The community is pretty much the number 1 problem. Ever since Valve made it F2P, hordes of idiots no longer hindered by the issue of paying for it joined the bandwagon, meaning that even people who shouldn't be able to contribute to the experience now can. Through this, any potential good people see the way that the masses play, and adopt the 'strategies' {W+M1ing, 'nade spamming, healing only heavies, etc.} for their own, leading to an endless spiral of stupidity. In terms of balancing, almost every single time SPUF throws a temper tantrum over something being 'op' {OMG vlve git rd of sandman!}, Valve caves in and nerfs the offending material, so expect to have to relearn to use your favorite weapons every other month or so. As a final aside, apart from a few servers here and there, rest assured that almost every server you visit will be a mish mash of people who should still be training on bot servers {and should probably never leave them}, people who are leagues better than you and only there to grind stranges and spam memey nonsense, traders who are only there to idle/spam trade requests,  and the occasional troll. Very rarely will you find a server where everyone is polite, actively playing, and more or less on your skill level. The same issues also plauge co-op mode, even more so than pvp. You'd expect to see the usual pub filth in Boot Camp {and you do}, but not in Tour of Duty mode, which is pay to play. You'll sadly still see the normal assortment of trade spammers, caber demoknights, gunslinger engis, people that call for kicks over any and everything, and really just a general lack of common sense. And as of the newest update, in both versus and co-op, if you're repeatedly placed on garbage teams, you either have to suck it up and stay, or recieve a temporary matchmaking ban.
After the community, I'd say Valve themselves are the next biggest problem. Everytime you turn around, there's a new hat, a new misc item, a new kit to make your weapon fire glowy pumpkins and set your head on fire after a few kills, and so on and so forth. New weapons though, which one would think would be the core of an online fps, are rarely released, with multi-year periods between weapon packs. There are loads of weapon reskins though, including slightly differently colored ones, scratched up ones, ones with blinky christmas lights, the insanely rare golden ones, and that stupid frying pan that goes for over $4k {in a f2p game, no less}. Although to be fair, weapon stats are changed so much that we technically get new weapons every now and then. This game has gone from "Capture the point and kill all enemies in your way" to "holy wow guise stout shako 3 ref trade me up!". It's no longer an fps, it's a dress up game with murder as an optional sidequest. Valve sadly seems to longer care about making the game fun as much as they do fattening their wallets. One need look no further than the Halloween events of the last 3 years, where the new gameplay elements more or less amounted to "pick up this item and mindlessly spam instant death beams" and dozens {yes, dozens} of misc items being released, the majority of which can't even been worn once the event ends or outside of a full moon.
Valve remains either unable or unwilling to compete with Blizzard {their main competition after Overwatch was released} in any meaningful way, and seem perfectly content to just let their game lose more and more players. Truly, the golden age of this game is over, with any competent players bound to permanently rage-quit sooner or later, and head for new shores.

Team Fortress 2 is an exceptional game in which players must rely on teamwork, tactical skill, dexterity, and a small amount of luck in order to kill off mercenaries on an opposing team, and work their way to their goal together. No one class in this shooter can do everything, which means that players need to rely on each other to get the job done, and bring home the gold for their team. Each class is well-balanced, with a variety of fun weapons to play with, that can synergize with each other in interesting ways.  Every game mode is fun, and there are several maps for each different objective type, meaning if you grow bored of one, you can easily find something else to do within the game. In addition to everything else, the game is dripping with theme. As one of 9 mercenaries, you fight for either Reliable Excavation and Demolition, or Builder's League United, and do your best to thwart the other team, forwarding your employers' goals of world domination, in a setting that wouldn't be out of place in a sixties spy thriller. The setting doesn't take itself at all seriously, though, and the characters, weapons, and even maps are extremely silly. This game is well-balanced, pretty, entertaining, and just a blast to play.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Second, there's Soldier, who is the son of Sweet Tooth and Jack the Ripper's great great great great granddaughter, so he's crazy too. However, as opposed to killing nice ladies who never did anything wrong, he kills with his freinds and is a sterotypical patriot. Oh, and he has a RPG.
Third, there's Pyro, the only woman in the game(I think) and daughter of the Empty Child, who wears a gas mask and fire retardant suit. Armed with a Flamethrower, she can burn down people. Plus, she worships Vulcan, God of Fire.
Fourth, there's Demoman, who wears a eyepatch, as his other eye can grant wishes, and can use explosives to both blow people skyward, often in many pieces, take out any buildings and give people seizures. Eh, not much else to say about him other than he's a achoholic.
Fifth, there's Heavy, a twelve foot tall, machine gun toting being. He is bald, and people call him fat. But in truth, it's not fat. Just muscle. He has a IQ of 45 and has difficulty saying certain words. He can also eat a sandwich to somehow heal himself.
Sixth, there's Engineer. He graduated at the finest school of engineering, and if he gets in his freind's house, he will build a Sentry to shoot burglars, a Dispensor to heal others, a Teleporter to-you guessed it-teleport and a anti-brony system to keep those damn bronies out.
Seventh, there's Medic, a either elderly or not elderly ex-Nazi physician who follows people around and heals them with a gun that fires healing beams. He also regenerates health and can make people invulnerable. No-one knows how. The real question: Does anyone CARE how?
Eighth, there's Sniper, a Jedi Knight who can wind up things in other rooms and throw bottles of urine at people. As the name says, he's a Sniper, but I prefer to wander into battle and help my teammates. Oh, and he has a collection of sheilds.
Finally, we have Spy, a Changeling who can insta-pwn people with his Knife and Sapper. He can also disguise as other people, become invisible and even fake his own death. He can also shhot at long range. Plus, he's in a relationship with Scout's Mum.
