Before I say anything, I need to get something off my chest. Out of all video game genre's in the history of history, I tend to ignore first person shooters the most. It's not that the games within this catagory are bad, just kind of bland for the most part. However I barely have any right to critisice this genre, seeing as how I've only played two or three first person shooters, but, even still, I can't really say that this genre is one I hold high oppinions on. It's just that it doesn't have things I can really praise with a straight face. Not trying to offend anyone. For me to actually enjoy a first person shooter: It has to have creativity, class, personality, and uniqueness. So what does Valve go and do? Create the one first person shooter that DOMINATES MY LIFE!
Oh man, where do I even begin? Let me start with the most important detail, the classes. Valve included a total of nine unique members to take controll of, all with thier own seperate personalities to distinct them from one another. Every member of the roster have unique traits that make them so, Lovable. Not only does it truly feel like nine different odballs in a group, but it also supports how the game plays. In most other FPS games you can usually get any job done just fine yourself. Trying to do that here is usually the equivelent of signing your death sentence. If you want even the slightest chance of getting anything done, you'll need to learn how to work alongside your team mates. So hows that for you, it's  fun and encourages team work.
Everything is fine tuned for balance so nothing is overly powerful, so if you end up dying alot it's your own fault. This is a timeless experience that will suck hours from your life away from you. As for me, this game may not be my favorite game of all time but it's easily up there. This is a true gem among shooters, best part is that it's free. Seriously, this game is quite possibly the greatest FPS of all time.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

If you like playing a fps, but in a casual sense, this is the game for you. You can find that Team Fortress 2 (unlike other fps games) has more than just a handful of weapons to use on one person, but an enormous amount of weapons for 9 different and unique characters, with perks and disabilities to each. I find this to be helpful for the casual player as it helps give options for different moods and play styles.
TF2 also includes many different maps with many different objectives, and for most of these, the objective is not to kill people, but to achieve a goal and eliminate people that get in the way. One thing about this is that you have a lot more health compared to other games. This also helps the casual style because you don't have to panic as much about dying before you even react to a situation, and allows you to think more about strategy and less about quick killer instinct.
Finally, TF2 includes hats. This may feel like an arbitrary point, but it is one of the most important pieces in my opinion. In other games, the monotone colors and blank faces make it seem like you're not even interacting with real people. The hats and cosmetics in Team Fortress 2 allow you to personalize your characters, and it can express your personality through the different classes. In that sense, you can tell the differences between one person and the next, and you can truely feel like you are playing a game with others. From a casual standpoint, you can see that laughing at other peoples' choices of clothing and noticing what they look like can put you into a happy setting and a more relaxed and entertained state of mind.
Of course, there are plenty of problems with it, and not all of these qualities work for everyone, but in the end the game is worth keeping with all of it's ups and downs. Because hey, Valve made it.

Take two at a review of this game. I'll make it quick since it's early 2015 now and TF2 has been out for nearly eight years. That said, it's balanced. They keep adding things while still keeping it balanced, with a few notable exceptions. (google Short Circuit, heh) It has lots of game modes, and they keep adding more as well...with Mannpower and its grappling hooks currently in beta. There are tons of communities...many are mature, many are not. There's surely at least one for you and you'll make friends, spend thousands of hours playing. The best part is, it's not an MMO...it's a real competitive and cooperative FPS that you can pick up and put down at any time.
Getting bored of the standard game modes? Try mod servers. Versus Saxton Hale/Freak Fortress 2 are the undisputed kings of the modding scene, but there's Deathrun, Prop Hunt, Dodgeball, FortWars, Jailbreak (not my thing, but meh), Slender, Hidden, TF2 Ware, TF2 karts, and so much more. The TF2 dev team has done plenty to rope people in, but it's the modders that fill in the gaps. With the absurd gameplay variety stemming from nine distinct classes, and a Player vs Player foundation, it's impossible to get bored of this game.
Also, you might see a hat or two. And some ducks eating bread.

I'm torn with this review. It's fun when the classes that you want to play actually WORK. Yes, I'm one of THOSE guys. I understand the point of this game: each class has different strengths and weaknesses, and you need the right balance of them depending upon the other team's mix. But after a while, being a Soldier or Heavy gets BORING. Especially Heavy. And no matter WHAT your class is, you're going to die A LOT. There's always a counter for WHATEVER you're doing, and that sounds good in THEORY, but it just becomes annoying.
The voice acting is fun, and some of the CLASSES are fun, but the game becomes annoying pretty quickly. The relatively few hours that I have in this game have come over the course of SEVERAL YEARS. I play for an hour, then stop for a few months.
The Scout is my main, and that's pretty fun. Soldier always becomes fun immediately after Scout because you do more damange, but you're gonna run out of bullets in your clip, have to reload, and get swamped. Then, it goes to Huntsman Sniper, which is fun when I can hit shots (and♥♥♥♥♥♥off teammates when we INEVITABLY have more snipers than we need), and then, when you're REALLY desperate, play Demoman with no projectile weapons. But, even then, it eventually becomes boring. Especially Pyro. Yeah, you're doing a lot of damage, but are you having any FUN? I do, but only for a VERY short time.
Oh yeah, Engineer is fun when your sentires dominate, but that Spy is inevitably going to ruin your fun. Nothing is more infuriating when you first start playing this game than the Spy. I wouldn't be surprised if most people ragequit when they first started playing this game because of the Spy.
Inevitably, I'll look at how few hours I have in this game compared to, say, CS:GO, and think "Huh. Is it REALLY that bad?" Then I'll play for an hour and say "Oh yeah. NOW I remember why I don't play this game."

Team Fortress 2 is a very fun and addicting game. It's styles are more or less classic and it's so simple to play!

You don't need to have excessive amounts of skill and items to be good, unlike COD.
Most people are really nice to you and might help you with some tips and tricks.
You can make money of the game by selling your items thru the market.
Sometimes people just taunt to have fun instead of killing, which is sometimes fun.
Many fun servers to play on.
Fun gamemodes like VS. Saxton Hale.
You can create items thru the workshop and MAYBE make money of that if it gets accepted in-game.
You can trade with other players.
Cons:
Some innapropriate sprays, like nudity, sexual pictures, My Little Pony porn and other types of porn.
Some cursing and foul language.
There are hackers, but little of them.
Crates from the mann co. store rarely have very valuable items (items like unusual hats).
(The foul language, the innapropriate sprays, things like that are only on non-Valve servers)
Overall this game is amazing awesome and I would recommend getting it anyday!

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play, though lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes to choose from. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow each to fulfill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or better skill levels. The game has an active dev team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content such as weapons or game modes.
At the time of this review, there are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objective or objectives for each team to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play. I have been playing since December 2014 and I still return to the game on a regular basis.

Many firstperson shooters feel the same: you're the only one that matters; any weapon will kill in one to two hits; the game takes itself way to seriously; the main goal is KILL, KILL, KILL. Overall, it seems to me that most FPS genre games are lacking a bit in the diversity department. Team Fortress 2 addresses that by giving you a crazy, colorful, whacked-out, and unpredictable world to screw around in. With nine classes to choose from, each with his own arsenal of specialized (and sometimes hilarious) guns, bombs, and blunt instruments to do battle with, you're presented with countless different play styles. Customizing the mercenaries with nonsensical wardrobe changes is a big part of the game as well; just visualize a giant, brutish man wearing a tutu! Team Fortress 2 also encourages a team dynamic of sorts. While you can go off on your own and sucseed, coordination with other players is vital, as each class has his own way(s) to help out his fellow mercenary. I know, this is quite the exstensive review on a free game, but please heed my word and give this a shot. I'm certain you'll enjoy it!

Team Fortress 2 is the shining star of free-to-play games. Its unbeatable diversity with weapons is amazing, and I’m still impressed how it maintains being balanced with so many crazy weapons and strats, like a gun that lets you do 8 double jumps, and the ability to “rocket jump”. In the same server where a Soldier is getting his 20th kill after an intense firefight, on the other side of the map, a Heavy wearing a santa hat and a large white beard is conga-ing around with his friends. TF2 makes a great free-to-play game because you can’t hop in with 20 bucks and buy the most overpowered weapon.  Every weapon has advantages and downsides, making them situational. You don't have to pay to get weapons, if you are patient enough. Every 48 minutes you play, you are given a free TF2 weapon (with a slim chance of it being a hat.)

It's freakin' TF2. Do I really need to say anything else?
Okay, for realsies, TF2 is by far one of the most thilling, enjoyable, addictive, rewarding and downright fun experiences on ANY system. While this game may not seem so serious on first glance, the core gameplay and mechanics of TF2 are top-notch, the classes and their different weapons are VERY well balanced and the expansive array of different weapons and cosmetics for each class really gives you the creative freedom of making your class and playstyle truly unique.
The classes on general are all well implemented into the game and all have their own unique playstyles, attributes, weapons and other. This means that there's bound to be a class that suits practically everybody's different styles of play and each class as a whole seems very well adapted to their uses for the team (e.g Medic used to heal/protect/assist team members while they do their jobs, Scout used to quickly get to control points and capture much faster.)
The main reason behind why I find this game so fun and addictive is quite simple; Challenges.
The game is CONSTANTLY rewarding you for attempting different game types, mixing up your game style, playing as different classes or something else entirely. This could be something as simple as getting a certain number of kills with a certain class or weapon or as challenging as accomplishing a series of progressively hard goals without dying.
Even if you do eventually grow tired of the standard TF2 gametypes, the "Servers" feature allows you to search for a completely new and different way of playing a gametype or a new gametype entirely, such as Trading Servers, Medieval Mode, Arena Mode or anything else that the community of TF2 can think of.
All in all, Team Fortress 2 has to be not only one of the most fun experiences on Steam, but on ANY console as a whole, thanks to its great core gameplay, rewarding challenges, well balanced classes and weapons and also its awesome and creative community. Even if you do get this game free-to-play, you'll immediately want to upgrade yourself to not only make your classes and weapons truly unique, but also broaden the already-deep amount of content on offer.

Updates give the game a fresh feel to it and keeps players in the game. I also can see why people are moving away from the game and giving it game negative reviews.For instance, if you were a big trader and you don't like where the economy is going, it makes sense that you would want to stop playing. Team Fortress 2 is quite possibly one of the most addictive multiplayer games of all time. And I'm saying this as a guy who started in November 2014 and has had over 300 hours of game experience (which is nothing compared to some people who have well over 10,000 hours). This was the game that got me into online shooters. Some of you have may play Call of Duty.
If you have then read on because this review is for Call of Duty players.
Differences from Call of Duty:
- First of all, the gameplay. Call of Duty has a familiar "run and gun" aspect to the series. Straight up deathmatch. Just run around a corner, shoot a guy, then shoot another guy... NONE OF THIS IS IN TF2. There's a reason it's called Team Fortress 2; first of all, you have a team, and (depending on the gamemode), you must assault or defend territory (Control Points and Payload) or either defend or take certain pieces of Intelligence (Capture the Flag basically, only with a briefcase that has notes flying out of it). You can't be a lone man and carry the team because the other team WILL KILL YOU thanks to the advantages and disadvantages of each class (which I shall explain later). Instead, you need to think of yourself and your teammates. Think tactically. How can you help the team to win?
Should you assault the front lines? Go behind the the enemy and take them out one by one? Or will you defend and reinforce your own territory? How would this option suit your class? The options are limitless, though both risky and rewarding.
Oh, and also, most gamemodes do not allow you to respawn instantly. You have to wait for a while, meaning that dying is often not a good option to the team effort.
-Classes. In this game, you don't just select your weapons and quickscope every enemy that comes into site. Instead, you take advantage of each class's particular weapons, stats and special abilities.
There are nine of them, each with their own gameplay style and personality.
*The Scout - An extremely fast class who can double jump. This allows him to move quickly around the maps of the game and either weaken or take out enemies faster. He wields a scattergun and the ability to aim is especially important here (There is no auto-aim in Team Fortress 2). However, he has low health, meaning he will die easier then other classes (unless you dodge enemies with your speed) and is generally bad at long range combat.
*The Soldier - A class who has low speed but makes up for it because he can fire rockets at his feet to fling him anywhere and everywhere. He has a rocket launcher and is terrifying in close range combat and is a equally so at long range at long range depending on the circumstances. He can cause splash damage and take out enemies in seconds if mastered. However, for his downsides, he is average in all stats, never excelling in anything. Good for beginners.
*The Heavy - A very slow minigun wielder who has massive amounts of health and can kill almost all classes very easily at short range. However, due to his slow speed and large size, everyone often targets the Heavy by exploiting his weaknesses. Heavy may require support from other classes such as Medics in order to keep him alive and fighting. His main role is to defend certain points support heavy advances on enemy positions. The Heavy is a must on populated servers.
*Pyro - A rather quick and offensive class that can cause chaos for the enemy team. Pyro set people on fire and burn them to death. They excell in close range and can spot out Spies by lighting them on fire. Pyro is a fairly balanced class but can be countered by many classes such as Heavies and Scouts.
*Demoman - A versatile class that can fire grenades to protect positions and cause massive damage to the enemy team. A good Demoman is the bane of many peoples existence in the game and can wipe out opponents at all ranges. He is extremley hard to master and not recommended for beginners.
Also, KABOOM! You're dead.
*Engineer - A defensive and support class that can construct Sentries, (to control areas) Dispensers (to heal teammates) and teleporters (to bring his team to the front lines faster). Average at most stats, he can also damage and kill enemies, though not to the effectiveness of other classes. Spies can destroy his buildings.
*Spy - A support class designed for getting behind the enemy lines and backstabbing opponents. They can change the tides of a game by eliminating a dangerous target or destroying buildings by an engineer. Everyone fears them because they can disguise as teammates and promptly betray you moments later with a backstab before disguising again and killing off your team in secret. If you fail as a spy, it can mean instant death due to your low health and damage output.
*Sniper - Not like the ones in Call of Duty. You cannot quickscope with a sniper in this game nor will you do a whole lot other than die by attempting to do so on the front lines. No, instead, you must stick to back lines, stay as support and eliminate key targets with headshots on the battle. Snipers, much like spies, can change the course of a game by eliminating the best players and allowing your team to complete objectives easily.
*Medics - One of the most useful classes in the game. They heal teammates form injuries, keeping them alive and build up an "ubercharge" whilst doing so. Ubercharges have a range of abilities (depending on the weapon) such as Critical Hits and Invincibility. Medics are not made for direct combat and are weaker than most classes, though it is completely possible to play this way using your syringe gun and bonesaw as weapons.
- Maps are a lot larger in Team Fortress 2 due to the amount of players and tactics employed to boost chances of survival. They are very balanced and due to community support, they are usually bug free and far from exploitable.
All in all, it is HUGELY recommended to anyone looking for decent gameplay. And guess what? Its free to play. Download today!

Honestly I don't see the appeal. It's a pretty decent Free To Play shooter with 9 classes. Most of the time it's just shoot in the general direction of bad guys and you're likely to get a few hits if not some kills.
The real draw to this game (apperently) is all the drops which range from weapons to clothing to other nick nacks. But the loot system is bad, I have 3 copies of the same gun, and considering how infrequent drops are, this sucks and doesn't hold the same allure as Diablo's would.
And this leads to the next problem, unless you fork out money, you can't trade with anyone. I have 4 crates in my inventory and I can't do anything with them, can't even give them away for free because I don't want to pay for an item. So when your drop is a crate, have fun shelling out anywhere from 1-2 bucks for a key to open it and get something that you might already have...
But the real question is: Is it fun? Yeah it's kinda fun, in that mindless "shoot randomly and be a general idiot" kinda way. The thought of getting drops is fun but in reality they usually suck unless you pay to get better drops. So I suppose I can recommend this game on the basis that the core game is free, however it does loose it's fun after a few hours...
